brief_summary:
The goal of this clinical trial is to learn if AWARE-a brief, 4-session group program based on motivational interviewing-reduces alcohol and other drug use and sexual risk behavior among young adults experiencing homelessness (ages 18-25). The study will also learn how well AWARE can be delivered in real-world drop-in center settings and what it would take to keep the program running long-term.

The main questions it aims to answer are:

* Does AWARE reduce the frequency, quantity, and consequences of alcohol use more than services as usual?
* Does AWARE reduce sexual risk behavior (condomless sex with primary and casual partners, number of sexual partners, and alcohol or other drug use during sexual activity)?
* How consistently and well can AWARE be delivered at community drop-in centers?

Researchers will compare AWARE to services as usual at three drop-in centers in Los Angeles and Pittsburgh to see if AWARE works to better.

Participants will:

* Attend up to 4 group sessions of AWARE or continue receiving usual services at their drop-in center
* Complete surveys about their alcohol and drug use, sexual behavior, and health at study enrollment, and 3 and 6 month follow-ups.
title: Implementing an Evidence-based Alcohol Use and Sexual Risk Intervention in Young Adult Homeless Service Settings

brief_summary: The purpose of this study is to investigate the safety and feasibility of using distributed intracortical recordings from the language network to decode intended language output in individuals with severe communication impairment due to severe communication impairment resulting from amyotrophic lateral sclerosis (ALS), locked-in syndrome, and brain injury including from stroke.
lead_sponsor: The University of Texas Health Science Center, Houston
primary_outcomes: Safety as assessed by the number and type of adverse events that occur
title: REstoration of Communication and LAnguage With Intracortical Microelectrodes

brief_summary:
This randomized study evaluates EMILY.AI, an investigational (non-CE-marked) smart oxygen valve that automatically adjusts the oxygen flow delivered to a patient, second by second, according to oxygen saturation (SpO2), heart rate and respiratory rate measured by a pulse oximeter.

Adults admitted to the pulmonology ward of Hospital Universitario Fundación Jiménez Díaz (Madrid, Spain) with acute respiratory failure are randomly assigned to receive oxygen titrated automatically by EMILY.AI or oxygen managed as usual by the nursing team, from randomization until hospital discharge. All participants wear the device; in the usual-care group it only records data.

The study compares the time patients stay within their target saturation range, episodes of low and high oxygen, nursing workload, oxygen use, length of stay and patient experience. This substudy is part of clinical investigation FJD-EMILY-23-02, whose other substudies are registered in separate records.
primary_outcomes: Percentage of time with SpO2 within the target range
title: Automated Versus Manual Oxygen Titration With the EMILY.AI Device in Hospitalized Patients With Acute Respiratory Failure

interventions: Recombinant Human Interleukin-2 Fusion Protein with Human Serum Albumin (VDJ010)

brief_summary: The purpose of this protocol is to evaluate the feasibility and acceptability of a preoperative exercise intervention (Prehabilitation) program, along with intraoperative Electroencephalography (EEG) recordings, and pre and post operative cognitive testing in older patients undergoing a major surgery.
primary_outcomes: Evaluate the feasibility of a preoperative home-based exercise intervention program, with intraoperative EEG recording, and pre and post operative cognitive testing, among older patients undergoing major surgery.

Evaluate the acceptability of a preoperative home-based exercise intervention program, with intraoperative EEG recording, and pre and post operative cognitive testing, among older patients undergoing major surgery.
title: Prehab-COG: Does Preoperative Exercise Improve Postoperative Cognitive Outcomes?

brief_summary:
Hip fracture is a common orthopedic emergency in the elderly, and it is associated with significant morbidity and mortality. Surgical reduction and fixation are the definitive treatment in most patients, effective perioperative analgesia that minimizes the need for opioids and related adverse effects (such as delirium) is essential in this patient population.

In this study we are going to compare the effects of ultrasound guided pericapsular nerve group (PENG) block and suprainguinal fascia iliaca compartment block (FICB) on postoperative analgesia and quadriceps strength following total hip arthroplasty.
title: Comparison Between Ultrasound Guided Pericapsular Nerve Block And Suprainguinal Fascia Iliaca Nerve Block in Hip Surgery

brief_summary:
This study will compare two ways of supporting adults with cirrhosis after they leave hospital. Cirrhosis is severe scarring of the liver. Eligible participants will have been hospitalized for liver-related complications and will be ready for discharge. The main question is whether adding an artificial intelligence (AI)-assisted management service to usual care reduces unplanned hospital care caused by worsening liver disease during the next 90 days.

The study plans to enroll 180 adults at three centers. Participants will be assigned by chance, with an equal chance of receiving usual care alone or usual care plus AI-assisted proactive management. Participants receiving the additional service, or their authorized caregivers, will complete a brief daily health report taking about 3-5 minutes and may report symptoms when they occur. The system helps organize reports and identify information requiring attention. Nurses check the information, and physicians make clinical decisions. The system does not independently diagnose illness, prescribe treatment, or change medication.

Both groups will continue their usual medical care and have study follow-up contacts on days 7, 30, 60, and 90. The study will compare unplanned emergency visits, hospital observation, acute same-day treatment, and readmissions related to worsening liver disease. Safety and the burden of using and delivering the service will also be assessed. Participants with urgent symptoms should seek emergency care without waiting for a response from the study platform.
primary_outcomes: Proportion of Participants With a First Liver-Related Unplanned Acute Healthcare Utilization Event Within 90 Days
title: Artificial Intelligence-Assisted Care After Hospital Discharge for People With Decompensated Cirrhosis

brief_summary:
The goal of this study is to investigate whether a dynamic group intervention that combines conversation and creative arts can reduce loneliness and support well-being and quality of life among older adults experiencing subjective or mild cognitive impairment.

The study will also explore how participants connect with one another, express emotions, and develop relationships during the group sessions.

Fifty older adults aged 65 and older, with subjective or mild cognitive impairment, will take part in the study.

Participants will:

Attend 10-group sessions that combine open conversations combined with creative arts, such as art, music, movement, and drama. Group sessions will be video-recorded to help researchers study participants' interactions and processes in the group.

Complete questionnaires about loneliness, well-being, and quality of life at Baseline, Pre, Post the intervention and follow-up.

Answering questions about how they feel before and after selected sessions.

Participate in an interview and share their experiences of participating in the group.

Researchers will also observe group interactions to better understand how relationships and emotional expression develop during the sessions.
primary_outcomes: changes in scores of the Three-Item Loneliness Scale
title: Dynamic Creative Arts Group Intervention to Alleviate Loneliness and Support Well-Being in Older Adults With Cognitive Changes

brief_summary: Assessment of RUCONEST (C1 Esterase Inhibitor \[Recombinant\]) in Alleviating Neurological Symptoms Linked to Infectious Pathogens
title: Exploring the Extended Efficacy and Initial Use of RUCONEST® in Managing Neurological Symptoms Linked to Infectious Pathogens

brief_summary:
The goal of this clinical trial is to learn whether artificial intelligence (AI)-assisted remote symptom monitoring can reduce hospital admissions related to malignant bowel obstruction (MBO) in patients with advanced cancer who have MBO or are at risk of developing MBO.

The main questions it aims to answer are:

* Does AI-assisted remote symptom monitoring reduce the proportion of patients who experience at least one hospital admission due to MBO within 90 days?
* Does AI-assisted remote symptom monitoring improve patient-reported outcomes, quality of life, healthcare resource utilization, and survival outcomes compared with standard care? Researchers will compare AI-assisted remote symptom monitoring plus standard care with standard care alone to determine whether remote monitoring can reduce MBO-related hospital admissions and improve patient outcomes.

Participants will receive study-specific assessments and follow-up for at least 90 days. Participants in the monitoring group will receive regular automated symptom-monitoring calls, and optional stool samples may be collected for microbiome research
title: AI-Assisted Remote Monitoring for Patients With or at Risk of Malignant Bowel Obstruction

brief_summary: This is a single-center, prospective, open-label, 1:1 randomized parallel-controlled investigator-initiated trial. A total of 120 adult patients with abnormal glucose undergoing elective or semi-elective non-emergency general or orthopedic surgery will be enrolled. Subjects are randomized to rtCGM-guided perioperative glycemic management (experimental group) or conventional POCT-only glycemic management (control group, using blinded rtCGM sensor for post-hoc data collection). The primary endpoint is hierarchical composite of postoperative length-of-stay and CGM Time-In-Range analyzed by win-ratio. Secondary objectives include glycemic metrics, rtCGM accuracy, postoperative complications, hypoglycemia/hyperglycemia events, health-economic indexes and satisfaction assessments. Safety including adverse events and device-related reactions will be descriptively evaluated. Follow-up includes in-hospital monitoring plus telephone follow-up 30 days after surgery.
primary_outcomes: Hierarchical composite endpoint of postoperative length of hospital stay and CGM-derived time in range (TIR)
title: Real-time CGM in Perioperative Glycemic Management

brief_summary: This is a single arm, prospective non-interventional study with primary data collection in patients initiated BGF MDI treatment as part of routine clinical care. In this study, 200 patients will be enrolled from approximately 20 sites mainly in general hospitals with respiratory/allergy/asthma specialists in Japan.
primary_outcomes: Change from baseline in Asthma Control Questionnaire-5 (ACQ-5) score
title: Changes in Symptom and Quality of Life in Patients With Uncontrolled Asthma Treated With Budesonide/Glycopyrronium/Formoterol Fumarate Metered Dose Inhaler (BGF MDI)

brief_summary:
The goal of this clinical trial is to test how safe and effective it is to treat early form of cancer cells found in the upper skin layer of the face, upper extremities and trunk, using a light sensitive cream used in combination with a light source.

The main questions this trial aims to answer are:

* to confirm using laboratory testing, how much of the affected skin cancer section the treatment was able to remove, and;
* seeing how many participants had no remaining affected skin cancer sections after treatment.

Participants who qualify will be asked to complete 12 visits in total and will receive a total of two treatments, after voluntarily consent has been given.
conditions: Cutaneous Squamous Cell Carcinoma in Situ
Facial Cutaneous Squamous Cell Carcinoma in Situ
Upper Extremities/Trunk Cutaneous Squamous Cell Carcinoma
interventions: Aminolevulinic Acid 20% Topical Solution with Blue Light (dose 20 J/cm2)
Aminolevulinic Acid 20% Topical Solution with Blue Light (dose 10 J/cm2)

primary_outcomes: Number of participants with Histological Clearance of treated isSCC lesion
title: Evaluating Photodynamic Therapy Used to Treat Cutaneous Squamous Cell Carcinoma in Situ (isSCC) on the Face, Upper Extremities & Trunk.

brief_summary:
Nephrostomy tube placement involves inserting a small tube through the skin and soft tissues into the kidney's collecting system to provide external drainage of urine when flow to the bladder is obstructed. A local anesthetic is injected along the nephrostomy tract and adjacent to the renal capsule to provide pain relief during the procedure.

Published medical literature predominantly describes lidocaine as the medication of choice for perirenal local anesthesia. However, no professional society guideline mandating a specific local anesthetic as the "standard of care" for nephrostomy tube placement was identified in the literature. In clinical practice, lidocaine is predominantly used.

Bupivacaine is a longer-acting alternative to lidocaine that may provide more sustained post-procedure pain relief. Use of bupivacaine has been well established in other procedural settings such as laparoscopic trocar-site infiltration (commonly performed by general surgery and gynecology) and nephrostomy-tract infiltration during percutaneous nephrolithotomy (performed by urologists).

A small subset of interventional radiologists in the Edmonton Zone-informally estimated at 2 out of 10-use bupivacaine for perirenal local anesthesia during percutaneous nephrostomy tube placement. These interventional radiologists anecdotally report better post-procedure pain control than with lidocaine for perirenal anesthesia. However, bupivacaine use for perirenal local anesthesia during nephrostomy tube placement has not been formally studied.

Our study aims to determine whether bupivacaine, compared with lidocaine, reduces pain during early recovery when used for perinephric local anesthesia.

We propose a prospective, randomized, controlled study with single-blinded outcome assessment. Patients undergoing percutaneous nephrostomy tube insertion will be randomized to receive either lidocaine or bupivacaine for perinephric local anesthesia. Participants will rate their pain at scheduled intervals after the procedure. Pain assessments will be performed by the site's nurse coordinator, who will be blinded to the local anesthetic technique used for each patient. We will compare pain scores and additional analgesic requirements between the two groups.

We expect patients receiving bupivacaine to experience significantly better post-procedure pain control than those receiving lidocaine. The findings may guide local anesthetic selection and ultimately improve comfort during recovery from nephrostomy tube placement.
title: Perirenal Bupivacaine Infiltration for Post-Procedure Pain Control in Percutaneous Nephrostomy Tube Insertion

brief_summary: Glucagon-like peptide-1 receptor agonist (GLP-1 RA) use among adult elective surgical patients is increasing. The exact prevalence is unclear, and the possible association with pulmonary aspiration is a major concern. This study was designed to quantify the prevalence of GLP-1 RA use and the incidence of perioperative aspiration among other 30-day pulmonary complications in adult elective surgical patients at a single institution in 2025.
title: GLP-1 Receptor Agonists in the Surgical Patient: Prevalence, Epidemiology, and Pulmonary Complications

brief_summary:
The Cervantes Scale and its short form (Cervantes-SF) have been the reference instruments for measuring menopause-related quality of life in Spain for two decades, but they do not capture several of today's most prevalent symptoms (weight and body changes, mood lability, cognitive complaints, dyspareunia), they confound the presence or intensity of a symptom with its actual impact, and they contain socioculturally outdated items.

This study develops and psychometrically validates the CervantesPROM, a new self-administered, digital patient-reported outcome measure (PROM) of health-related quality of life for women aged 35 to 75 years in the menopausal transition and postmenopause, following Classical Test Theory and COSMIN standards. For each symptom, the instrument records separately whether it is present and how much it bothers the woman in daily life, which is the dimension scored for quality of life.

The project has three phases: item generation and content validity (Phase 1, completed with an expert panel), item reduction and psychometric validation (Phases 2A and 2B), and responsiveness (Phase 3). Reference values for the Spanish population are an objective of the linked SILVA study, which has its own registration.
lead_sponsor: Asociación Española para el Estudio de la Menopausia
primary_outcomes: Number of CervantesPROM symptom items retained after item reduction
Comparative Fit Index (CFI) of the reduced CervantesPROM
Tucker-Lewis Index (TLI) of the reduced CervantesPROM
Root Mean Square Error of Approximation (RMSEA) of the reduced CervantesPROM
Standardized Root Mean Square Residual (SRMR) of the reduced CervantesPROM
Cronbach's alpha of the reduced CervantesPROM total score
McDonald's omega of the reduced CervantesPROM total score
title: Development and Validation of the CervantesPROM, a New Menopause-Specific Quality-of-Life Measure

brief_summary:
Biofeedback-based pelvic floor rehabilitation is an established treatment approach for dyssynergic defecation (DD), aiming to restore appropriate muscle coordination during defecation. However, the potential role of autonomic nervous system regulation and stress responses in gastrointestinal function has encouraged the investigation of additional therapeutic approaches.

This randomized, sham-controlled clinical trial aims to evaluate the additional effects of transcutaneous auricular vagus nerve stimulation (taVNS) combined with biofeedback-based pelvic floor rehabilitation, compared with sham stimulation combined with the same rehabilitation program, on constipation symptoms, defecation function, pelvic floor muscle activity, autonomic regulation, psychological symptoms, and quality of life in individuals with dyssynergic defecation.
interventions: Transcutaneous Auricular Vagus Nerve Stimulation (Active taVNS)
Sham Transcutaneous Auricular Vagus Nerve Stimulation (Sham taVNS)
primary_outcomes: Change in Constipation Severity Instrument (CSI) Total Score
title: Combined Effects of Transcutaneous Auricular Vagus Nerve Stimulation and Pelvic Floor Rehabilitation in Patients With Dyssynergic Defecation: A Randomized Controlled Trial

brief_summary:
The goal of this clinical trial is to learn if changing the physical environment of a pediatric waiting room can reduce the use of screen devices (such as mobile phones and tablets) by children aged 2 to 8 years while they wait for their appointment. The main questions it aims to answer are:

* Does the proportion of children who use a screen device in the waiting room decrease after the intervention?
* What types of digital content do children use most often in the waiting room, and which sociodemographic factors are associated with screen use? Researchers will compare children seen before the waiting room was changed with children seen after the change to see if fewer children use screen devices.

The intervention consists of posters for parents and caregivers on the benefits of reducing screen time, play and educational materials (books, puzzles, board games, and educational toys), and boards or murals where children and adults can draw or write.

Parents or legal guardians of participating children will complete a short anonymous survey on a tablet in the waiting room.
lead_sponsor: Consorci Sanitari de l'Alt Penedès i Garraf
primary_outcomes: Proportion of children using a screen device in the waiting room
title: Screen Use by Children in a Pediatric Waiting Room and the Effect of an Environmental Intervention

brief_summary: The purpose of this open-label study is to evaluate the effects of a single intravenous infusion of ketamine on depression and anxiety in adults with low vision.
primary_outcomes: Change in depression symptom severity as measured by the Hamilton Depression Rating Scale 17 (HDRS-17)
Change in anxiety symptom severity as measured by the Hamilton Anxiety Rating Scale (HAM-A)
title: Exploring Ketamine's Effects on Depression and Anxiety in Adults With Low Vision

brief_summary: Neck pain is often associated with scapular dysfunction. However, this relationship is not present in all cases. Previous studies on scapular-focused exercises have reported inconsistent findings, possibly due to limitations in identifying individuals with scapular-related neck pain and in the specificity and progression of exercise programs. This trial aims to investigate the effects of a Progressive Scapular-Focused Exercise Program (PSEP), compared with routine physical therapy, on neck pain intensity, neck disability, scapular muscle strength, scapular position, cervical range of motion, upper limb disability, and global perceived benefit in individuals with neck pain related to scapular dysfunction.
title: Progressive Scapular-Focused Exercises for Neck Pain Related to Scapular Dysfunction

brief_summary: A radioligand is a small amount of a radioactive imaging compound used during a positron emission tomography (PET) scan. This study aims to validate a new positron emission tomography (PET) ligand for measuring M4 receptors in the brain. M4 receptors are proteins that may play a role in various psychiatric and neurological conditions. This study will evaluate the PET ligand \[11C\]ABBV-112i in healthy adult participants to assess how well the ligand can measure the distribution of the M4 receptors across brain regions and the test-retest variability of the binding measurements.
primary_outcomes: Regional brain volume of distribution (VT) of ABBV-112i across brain regions
title: M4 Receptor PET Radioligand Validation Study in Healthy Adults

brief_summary: This study will compare adults aged 65 years or older who have mild cognitive impairment, with and without depressive symptoms. The researchers plan to participants at University Medical Centre Maribor, with two equally sized groups. They will compare outcomes in several different cognitive domains (visuospatial abilities, emotional modulation, social cognition) and in DNA methylation of relevant regions (for BDNF, COMT, and SLC6A4 gene promoters).
primary_outcomes: Social Cognition Performance on the Faux Pas Test
Regional DNA Methylation (BDNF, COMT and SLC6A4 promoter gene regions)
title: Mild Cognitive Impairment in Older Adults With and Without Depressive Symptom

brief_summary:
This prospective observational cohort study investigates cardiovascular outcomes and associated risk factors in patients undergoing coronary angiography for suspected or established coronary artery disease at Feldkirch Regional Hospital in Vorarlberg, Austria.

The study aims to identify clinical, metabolic, laboratory, and lifestyle factors associated with coronary artery disease and subsequent cardiovascular events. Baseline assessments include clinical characteristics, cardiovascular risk factors, laboratory measurements, and lifestyle-related information.

The primary outcomes are all-cause mortality and cardiovascular events. Follow-up assessments are conducted approximately every two years through telephone interviews and review of available clinical records and databases. Mortality status and causes of death are assessed using data from Statistics Austria and available medical records. Long-term follow-up is planned to evaluate cardiovascular outcomes and changes in risk factors over time.

The study aims to enroll approximately 2,000 participants, with recruitment ongoing.
lead_sponsor: Vorarlberg Institute for Vascular Investigation and Treatment
title: Prospective Cohort Study of Patients Undergoing Coronary Angiography in Vorarlberg, Austria

brief_summary: This randomized waitlist-controlled pilot trial examines whether sequential alpha (8-12 Hz) and low-beta (12-15 Hz) neurofeedback training improves mental health, social skills, attention, and quantitative EEG (QEEG) in adolescents and young adults with borderline intellectual functioning (slow learners). Thirteen participants aged 13 to 39 years were randomly assigned to a neurofeedback group (n = 7) or a waitlist control group (n = 6). The neurofeedback group completes 20 sessions (twice weekly, 50 minutes each) using a 2-channel prefrontal (Fp1, Fp2) headband device. Outcomes are assessed before and after the intervention period. The primary outcome is mean reaction time on the Psychomotor Vigilance Test (PVT). Secondary outcomes include the Brief Symptom Inventory-18 (BSI-18), the Korean Social Skills Rating System for college students (K-SSRS), PVT lapse rate, and 19-channel QEEG relative power.
primary_outcomes: Change in Mean Reaction Time on the Psychomotor Vigilance Test (PVT)
title: Neurofeedback Training for Adolescents and Young Adults With Borderline Intellectual Functioning

brief_summary: This study aims to evaluate whether long-term dual antiplatelet therapy (DAPT) with cilostazol reduces the risk of recurrent symptomatic ischemic stroke or all-cause mortality compared with single antiplatelet therapy (SAPT) in patients with symptomatic moderate-to-severe intracranial arterial stenosis, following the completion of standard DAPT.
lead_sponsor: Second Affiliated Hospital of Soochow University
primary_outcomes: Time to First Recurrent Symptomatic Ischemic Stroke or All-Cause Death
title: Long-Term Sequential Dual Antiplatelet Therapy Based on Cilostazol in Symptomatic Intracranial Arterial Stenosis

brief_summary:
The goal of this clinical trial is to compare two treatments for dental phobia in children and adolescents: One-Session Treatment for Dental Phobia (OSTD) and psychoeducation plus relaxation training (RELAX).

The main questions this study aims to answer are:

* Is one intervention more effective in reducing the severity of dental phobia 6 months after treatment?
* Are improvements in dental fear and anxiety maintained 12 months after treatment?
* How do changes in fear-related learning and beliefs contribute to treatment outcomes?
* How acceptable and practical are these treatments for youth, their parents, and the professionals delivering the treatments?

Researchers will enroll approximately 160 youth with dental phobia and randomly assign them to one of two treatment groups. Participants will receive either OSTD or RELAX.

Participants will:

* Complete an initial assessment of their dental fear and anxiety.
* Participate in their assigned treatment.
* Complete assessments 1 week, 6 months, and 12 months after treatment to evaluate changes in dental fear, anxiety, and related beliefs and behaviors.

Researchers will compare the two groups to determine which treatment is more effective in reducing dental phobia, whether improvements last over time, and how changes in fear-related learning may contribute to treatment outcomes.
lead_sponsor: University of Texas Rio Grande Valley
primary_outcomes: Change in Dental Phobia Severity From Baseline to 6 Months Post-Treatment
Change in Dental Phobia Severity From Baseline to 12 Months Post-Treatment
Change in Dental Anxiety Symptoms From Baseline to 12 Months Post-Treatment
Attainment of Personalized Treatment Goal at 6 Months and 12 Months Post Treatment
Attendance at Recommended Dental Cleaning Appointment
title: Study of Anxiety Free Experiences at the Dentist

brief_summary:
The purpose of this study is to evaluate the clinical, surgical, and postoperative outcomes of early laparoscopic cholecystectomy performed during the index hospital admission in adult patients presenting with mild gallstone pancreatitis.

Gallstone disease represents a primary cause of acute pancreatitis. While definitive cholecystectomy is essential to prevent recurrent biliary complications, the optimal timing has often been debated. Current guidelines advocate for same-admission cholecystectomy once the acute pancreatitis subsides; however, concerns regarding inflammation, adhesions around Calot's triangle, and potential surgical difficulty frequently influence practical decision-making. This study assesses the overall safety, feasibility, conversion rates to open surgery, complication profile, hospital stay, and recurrence rates among patients managed at Sohag University Hospital.
primary_outcomes: Number of Participants With Successful Early Laparoscopic Cholecystectomy Without Conversion or Major Complications
title: Early Laparoscopic Cholecystectomy for Mild Gallstone Pancreatitis

brief_summary:
The goal of this pilot clinical trial is to evaluate the feasibility of a new approach to assessing balance and mobility in everyday situations by performing established clinical tests in a stressful virtual reality environment. The study involves healthy adults aged 18 years and older with no self-reported neurological disorders or history of epilepsy.

The main questions it aims to answer are:

1. Is it feasible to perform standard balance and mobility tests in a virtual reality environment simulating a busy train station?
2. How does this virtual environment affect participants' balance and mobility test performance?
3. How do participants experience the virtual environment, including their sense of being there and any discomfort or virtual reality sickness?

Researchers will compare each participant's performance with and without virtual reality to see if the virtual environment changes balance and mobility test results.

Participants will:

* Spend a brief familiarisation period in the virtual environment before testing.
* Complete the Mini-BESTest, which assesses balance through a series of tasks, with and without virtual reality.
* Complete the Timed Up and Go test, which involves standing up from a chair, walking three meters, turning, returning, and sitting down, with and without virtual reality and with and without counting backwards by threes.
* Complete the 10-Meter Walk Test at comfortable and fast walking speeds, with and without virtual reality.
* Complete questionnaires after the final virtual reality exposure about their sense of being in the virtual environment and any symptoms of discomfort or sickness.
interventions: Immersive virtual reality exposure during balance and mobility assessment
primary_outcomes: Proportion of participants completing all planned assessments
Number of virtual reality-related technical issues
Proportion of complete outcome measurements per test and condition
Percentage increase in assessment time with virtual reality compared with no virtual reality
Number of participants experiencing adverse events during assessment
title: Feasibility and Effects of a Realistic Stressful Virtual Environment on Balance and Mobility in Healthy Adults: A Pilot Study

lead_sponsor: Institute of Hematology & Blood Diseases Hospital, China

brief_summary: This Phase 3 study will evaluate whether \[18F\]Floretyrosine (\[18F\]FET) PET imaging can help distinguish active brain tumor growth from treatment-related changes in patients with brain metastases who have unclear MRI findings after treatment. The study has two parts. Part 1 will identify the lowest effective dose of \[18F\]FET PET that provides reliable imaging results. Part 2 will evaluate the accuracy of \[18F\]FET PET, using the optimized dose, for distinguishing tumor progression from treatment-related changes. Study results will be compared with information from follow-up imaging, clinical assessments, and, when available, tissue samples obtained during routine clinical care. The goal is to determine whether \[18F\]FET PET can improve diagnostic accuracy and support clinical decision-making for patients with brain metastases.
primary_outcomes: Patient-Level Mean Dice Similarity Coefficient for Lesion Spatial Agreement Between Reduced-Dose and Full-Dose [18F]FET PET Images
Sensitivity of [18F]FET PET for Distinguishing Tumor Progression From Treatment-Related Changes Compared With CSOT
title: [18F]FET PET for Differentiating Tumor Progression vs Treatment-Related Changes in Brain Metastases

brief_summary: To evaluate the efficacy and safety of oral thalidomide for the prevention of radiation-induced dermatitis (RID) in breast-conserving surgery patients receiving intensity-modulated whole-breast radiotherapy. This is a single-center randomized controlled trial. Female breast cancer patients aged \>18 and \<70 years after breast-conserving surgery scheduled for whole-breast intensity-modulated radiotherapy will be enrolled. Subjects will be randomized at a 1:1 ratio to the intervention group (thalidomide 75 mg orally every bedtime plus standard skin care) or the control group (standard skin care alone). The observation window is defined as from the start of first radiotherapy to 42 days after completion of last radiotherapy. RID will be assessed weekly according to CTCAE v5.0, and the maximum grade within the observation window will be recorded for each subject. The primary endpoint is the incidence of grade ≥2 RID within the observation window. Secondary endpoints include incidence of grade ≥3 RID, time-to-first-onset of grade ≥2 RID, RID-related symptoms (burning, pruritus, pulling pain, tenderness), quality-of-life measured by EORTC QLQ-C30 / QLQ-BR23. Treatment-emergent adverse events will be documented using CTCAE v5.0, with special attention to thalidomide-related toxicities such as somnolence, peripheral sensory neuropathy and thromboembolism. A total of 68 participants are planned for enrolment.
lead_sponsor: First Affiliated Hospital of Guangxi Medical University
primary_outcomes: Incidence of grade ≥2 acute radiation dermatitis
title: Thalidomide for Preventing Radiation-Induced Dermatitis in Breast Cancer Patients

brief_summary:
Complex regional pain syndrome (CRPS) is a painful and debilitating disorder that usually occurs after limb injury, but can also occur without injury. Persons with CRPS commonly suffer significant levels of disability, loss of function and distress. This in turn can severely compromise a person's quality of life. Guidelines support physiotherapy and occupational therapy treatment for the management of CRPS. It is however not clear from current research as to which particular therapy interventions are most effective. Additionally, the effectiveness of different clinical approaches is poorly reported.

The study aims to establish whether the current therapy treatment offered at the Walton centre for the treatment of CRPS is effective in improving function and activity for people with long-standing complex regional pain syndrome.
title: Therapy Treatment for CRPS Within a Clinical Setting

brief_summary:
This prospective, multicenter observational study evaluates LIMA1 immunohistochemistry (IHC) and histological depth of invasion (DOI) as prognostic biomarkers in adult patients with newly diagnosed oral squamous cell carcinoma (OSCC) undergoing curative-intent primary surgical treatment.

LIMA1 expression will be assessed in surgically resected primary tumor specimens by immunohistochemistry using antibody clone Thab2c, developed by Thestra Ltd and raised against LIMA1-alpha. LIMA1 IHC staining will be scored using a prespecified four-level scoring system from 0 to 3 and classified as LIMA1-low (scores 0-1) or LIMA1-high (scores 2-3). Histological DOI will be determined from hematoxylin and eosin (H\&E)-stained primary tumor specimens and classified as DOI-low (\<5 mm) or DOI-high (≥5 mm).

The primary objective is to determine whether adding LIMA1 IHC to DOI improves the identification of patients with a favorable disease-specific outcome after surgery alone compared with DOI alone. The primary analysis will focus on patients treated with curative-intent surgery without adjuvant radiotherapy or chemoradiotherapy. A disease-specific OSCC event is defined as local recurrence, new regional lymph node metastasis, distant metastasis, or death attributable to the index OSCC.

Clinical outcomes will be assessed at 2, 3, and 5 years. The study will also evaluate overall survival, OSCC recurrence-free survival, individual disease-specific OSCC events, and the technical evaluability and interobserver reproducibility of the Thab2c LIMA1 IHC assay. Study biomarker results will not affect patient treatment.
primary_outcomes: Prognostic Performance of Thab2c-Based LIMA1 Immunohistochemistry for Disease-Specific OSCC Events
Prognostic Performance of Combined LIMA1 IHC and DOI for Disease-Specific OSCC Events
title: LIMA1 Immunohistochemistry and Depth of Invasion as Prognostic Biomarkers in Oral Squamous Cell Carcinoma

brief_summary:
This study is a prospective, multi-center, single-arm study of pediatric subjects (age 3-12) with Sleep-Disordered Breathing ("SDB") due to adeno-tonsillar hypertrophy which are treated with the ENTire IRE System.

Subjects will be followed for six (6) months post-treatment. The objective of the study is to provide an ongoing safety and effectiveness assessment of the ENTire IRE System in treating pediatric adeno-tonsillar hypertrophy.
primary_outcomes: Number of Participants With Device- or Procedure-Related Adverse Events (Bleeding, Readmission, Dehydration, or Emergency Department Visit)
Time From Treatment to First Wong-Baker FACES Pain Scale Score of 2 or Below
Change From Baseline in OSA-18 Total Score at 3 Months
Change From Baseline in OSA-18 Total Score at 6 Months
title: Pediatric Adeno-Tonsillar Hypertrophy Treatment Post-Approval Study

brief_summary: This prospective observational study aims to evaluate the diagnostic and therapeutic challenges of fungal malignant otitis externa in patients attending Sohag University Hospital. It will assess clinical presentation, diagnostic findings, treatment approaches, and clinical outcomes to improve understanding and management of this condition.
primary_outcomes: Number of participants with Clinical, Radiological, and Microbiological Findings in Patients with Fungal Malignant Otitis Externa
title: Fungal Malignant Otitis Externa

brief_summary:
This study compares two blood-filtering treatment approaches used in adults with acute-on-chronic liver failure, a sudden worsening of liver function in people with long-term liver disease.

Both approaches include plasma exchange, which removes and replaces the liquid part of the blood. One approach combines plasma exchange with a system that uses filters to remove certain substances from the blood. The other combines plasma exchange with continuous kidney support therapy, which helps remove waste and excess fluid.

The treating doctors and patients decide which treatment to use as part of routine care. The study does not assign treatment. The researchers will follow participants to find out how many are alive without a liver transplant 90 days after joining the study. They will also compare complications, blood test results, and safety outcomes. Participants may choose to join a separate part of the study that collects blood and stool samples.
lead_sponsor: The Second Affiliated Hospital of Chongqing Medical University
title: Comparison of Two Artificial Liver Support Treatments for Acute-on-Chronic Liver Failure

brief_summary: This is a first-in-human, open-label, single-arm, dose-escalation Phase 1 clinical study evaluating the safety, tolerability, feasibility, and immunogenicity of the YG-01, a personalized neoantigen peptide-based cancer immunotherapy, in patients with diagnosed glioblastoma following standard-of-care therapy. The study will assess the safety and tolerability of repeated administrations of YG-01 and explore immune responses and clinical outcomes following treatment. The study includes sequential dose-escalation cohorts to evaluate the safety and tolerability of increasing dose levels of YG-01 and to identify a recommended dose for further clinical development.
primary_outcomes: Incidence of local and systemic adverse events within 7 days following each administration of YG-01
title: First Study Evaluating the Safety and Dosage of YG-01 in Patients With Glioblastoma

brief_summary:
This study evaluates whether assistance from a large language model (LLM), a type of artificial intelligence that generates text, improves the quality of nursing care plans and reduces the time needed to complete them.

The study included 120 registered nurses working in internal medicine wards, surgical wards, and intensive care units at a medical center in southern Taiwan. Nurses were randomly assigned to one of two groups:

* Independent planning: Nurses prepared, reviewed, and submitted a care plan without LLM assistance.
* LLM-assisted planning: Nurses entered prompts to obtain an LLM-generated draft, then reviewed and revised the draft before submitting their final care plan.

Each nurse completed only the assigned workflow during a single study session. Participants completed a brief baseline questionnaire and prepared nursing problems, goals, and interventions for a standardized simulated clinical case. Tasks were performed in a secure hospital test environment without real patient data.

Expert nurse raters who were not informed of group assignments independently evaluated the final care plans. The nursing care decision quality assessment has a maximum total score of 30 points, comprising decision-content quality (25 points) and decision-language quality (5 points). The system recorded task completion time.

Researchers compare the two groups' final care-plan quality scores and task completion times.
primary_outcomes: Expert-rated nursing care decision quality (six-item total score)
title: Evaluating Large Language Models in Nursing Care Decision-Making: A Randomized Controlled Trial

brief_summary: This study is a multicenter, prospective cohort study. The main purpose of the study is to construct diagnostic model for vaginal laxity.
primary_outcomes: Construction of diagnostic model for vaginal laxity
title: Model of Vaginal Laxity

brief_summary: The goal of this study is to evaluate the feasibility, acceptability, and preliminary clinical effects of an oncology-adapted Pain Reprocessing Therapy (PRT) intervention for women with aromatase inhibitor-associated musculoskeletal symptoms (AIMSS). AIMSS is a common complication of aromatase inhibitor therapy for estrogen receptor-positive breast cancer and is associated with chronic pain, functional impairment, and premature discontinuation of endocrine therapy. The study will evaluate whether a six-session, manualized PRT intervention delivered remotely by trained palliative care therapists is feasible to implement and shows preliminary evidence of improving pain and physical function.
lead_sponsor: University of Michigan Rogel Cancer Center
title: Study of Oncology-Adapted Pain Reprocessing Therapy for Aromatase Inhibitor Associated Musculoskeletal Symptoms in Breast Cancer Survivors

brief_summary:
The goal of this clinical trial is to evaluate the effect of a digital Acceptance and Commitment Therapy (ACT)-based psychological support program for primary caregivers of older adults with severe mental disorders (SMD) in underdeveloped regions. It will also assess the feasibility and acceptability of this WeChat-mini-program-based intervention. The main questions it aims to answer are:

Does the digital ACT-based psychological support program improve psychological flexibility and family functioning among primary caregivers of older adults with SMD? Can this digital intervention improve psychological distress, perceived social support, caregiver needs-resources and disease-care-related knowledge for participating caregivers?

Researchers will compare digital ACT-based psychological support plus identical routine psychological support versus the same routine psychological support plus daily general mental-health and care-related popular-science reading materials to see whether the digital ACT program produces better outcomes.

Participants will:

Receive assigned 8-week study-related daily content on the basis of identical routine psychological support Complete online-or-paper-based questionnaires at baseline, immediately after intervention, and 1-month follow-up Take part in brief follow-up reminders via phone or WeChat during the study
interventions: Acceptance and Commitment Therapy (ACT) digital intervention
Routine care and general health education
title: Digital ACT Psychological Support for Primary Caregivers of Older Adults With Severe Mental Illness

brief_summary:
This study aims to evaluate changes in body composition and skeletal muscle composition following glucagon-like peptide-1 receptor agonist (GLP-1RA) therapy in adults with obesity or overweight with weight-related comorbidities. Ulsing computed tomography (CT), the study will quantitatively assess changes in skeletal muscle quantity, muscle attenuation, and adipose tissue distribution before and after treatment.

This is a single-center observational study consisting of a prospective GLP-1RA treatment cohort and a retrospective matched control cohort. A total of 240 participants will be included, comprising 120 patients receiving GLP-1RA therapy and 120 matched controls. The study aims to clarify whether changes in body composition following GLP-1 RA therapy reflect reductions in skeletal muscle quantity, changes in muscle composition, or both.
primary_outcomes: Change in the Ratio of Low-attenuation Muscle Area to Total abdominal muscle area (LAMA/TAMA Ratio)
title: Changes in Body Composition and Muscle Composition After GLP-1 Receptor Agonist Therapy in Patients With Obesity

brief_summary:
The goal of this randomized controlled crossover trial is to learn whether manual lymphatic drainage (MLD) and classical massage have different short-term effects on the heart, the nervous system, and mood in adults aged 18 to 65 receiving hemodialysis. A total of 60 patients from two hemodialysis centers in Tarsus, Mersin, Türkiye, are planned to take part.

The main questions it aims to answer are:

* Do MLD and classical massage differ in their short-term effects on autonomic nervous system responses, measured by heart rate variability (SDNN, RMSSD, LF, HF, LF/HF)? (Primary hypothesis 1)
* Do MLD and classical massage differ in their short-term effects on cardiovascular responses, measured by systolic and diastolic blood pressure and heart rate? (Primary hypothesis 2)
* Do MLD and classical massage differ in their short-term effects on mood (fatigue, vigor, tension, and confusion), measured by the Profile of Mood States - Short Form? (Secondary hypothesis)

Researchers will compare MLD with classical massage (active comparator). Each participant will receive both massages in a randomly assigned order (MLD first or classical massage first), so each participant serves as their own control. In addition, a no-massage control measurement will be taken in the week before the massages to show the changes caused by the hemodialysis session alone.

Participants will:

* In the first week (control period), have their blood pressure, heart rate, and heart rate variability measured three times during a hemodialysis session without any massage.
* In the second week, receive a 20-minute MLD or classical massage on both legs (thigh, lower leg, and foot), starting one hour after the beginning of the hemodialysis session.
* After a one-week break (washout period), receive the other type of massage in the same way.
* Have their blood pressure, heart rate, and heart rate variability measured before each massage, right after it, and 30 minutes later. Heart rate variability will be recorded for 5 minutes with a chest strap.
* Complete a short mood questionnaire.
primary_outcomes: Root Mean Square of Successive Differences (RMSSD)
Low Frequency to High Frequency Ratio (LF/HF)
title: Manual Lymphatic Drainage Versus Classical Massage on Heart Responses and Mood in Hemodialysis

brief_summary:
The main goal of the study is to assess the effect of rimonabant in cognitive performance in patients with Post-COVID-19 Syndrome, also known as long COVID.

The study will include 80 adults aged 18 to 75 years that will receive either rimonabant (5 mg) or placebo (a look-alike tablet that contains no drug) once daily for 90 days. Neither the participants nor the investigators will know which treatment is being given.

The study will also help to learn about the safety of rimonabant.
title: Rimonabant for Cognitive Impairment in People With Post-COVID-19 Syndrome

brief_summary: The aim of this study is to investigate the effects of exercise training applied through telerehabilitation on exercise capacity, peripheral and respiratory muscle strength, arterial stiffness, posture and quality of life in children with cystic fibrosis.
title: The Effects of Yoga Practice on Exercise Capacity, Arterial Stiffness, Respiratory Function, Peripheral Muscle Strength, Posture and Quality of Life in Children With Cystic Fibrosis

brief_summary:
Systemic sclerosis (SSc), also called scleroderma, is a rare long-term autoimmune disease that causes the body to make too much collagen (scar tissue), leading to hard, thick skin and sometimes damage to organs such as the lungs, heart, kidneys, or digestive system. An autoimmune disease is a condition where the body's immune system, which normally protects against germs, mistakenly attacks its own healthy tissues and organs.

The study has 2 parts. The main goal of Part 1 is to evaluate the safety and efficacy (how well the study treatment works) of ABBV-2294 (combination of ABBV-722 and upadacitinib) in adult participants with SSc that are currently receiving local standard of care treatment, and to determine the best dose of ABBV-2294 to be evaluated further. The main goal of Part 2 is to evaluate the safety and efficacy of the dose of ABBV-2294 determined in Part 1 when compared to placebo (looks like the study treatment but has no medicine in it) in adult patients with SSc that are currently receiving local standard of care treatment. Participants will undergo trial-related procedures throughout the study which may include physical exams, questionnaires, scans and imaging, and blood and urine tests.

ABBV-2294 (combination of ABBV-722 and upadacitinib) is an investigational drug being developed for the treatment of SSc in adult participants. At the start of Part 1, participants will be randomly assigned to receive Dose 1 of ABBV-722 and upadacitinib given together, Dose 2 of ABBV-722 and upadacitinib given together, ABBV-722 given alone, upadacitinib given alone, or placebo for 52 weeks. Participants that complete 52 weeks of treatment will be invited to join a 56-week extension period.

Participants that join Part 2 will be randomly assigned to receive either ABBV-2294 (dose determined in Part 1) or placebo for 52 weeks. Participants that complete 52 weeks of treatment will be invited to join a 104-week extension period. All participants that join the extension will receive ABBV-2294.

Participants 18 years of age and older diagnosed with Systemic sclerosis (SSc). Around 580 participants will be enrolled at approximately 200 sites worldwide.

Participants will receive upadacitinib and/or ABBV-722 oral tablets (or matching placebo) for 52 weeks in Part 1 with an optional 56-week extension period. Part 2 participants will receive ABBV-2294 (dose determined in Part 1) or matching placebo for 52 weeks with an optional 104-week extension period of open label ABBV-2294 (dose determined in Part 1).

There may be higher treatment burden for participants in this trial compared to their standard of care due to study procedures. Participants will attend regular visits during the study at a hospital or clinic, including screening, baseline, and scheduled visits. The effects of the treatment will be checked by medical assessments, blood tests, checking for side effects, and completing questionnaires.
primary_outcomes: Part 1 & Part 2: Achievement of Revised Composite Response Index in Systemic Sclerosis (rCRISS)-25
Part 1 & Part 2: Number of Participants Experiencing Adverse Events
title: A Study to Evaluate the Safety and Efficacy (How Well the Study Treatment Works) of ABBV-2294 in Adult Participants With Systemic Sclerosis That Are Currently Receiving Local Standard of Care Treatment, and to Determine the Best Dose of ABBV-2294 to be Evaluated Further.

brief_summary: This study is an ancillary study to the RESIST trial, in which adults with obesity receive the weight-loss medication tirzepatide and are randomly assigned to a structured resistance training program or to usual care for 24 weeks. RESIST-EXHALE measures acetone in exhaled breath, a non-invasive marker of fat burning, at all seven RESIST visits (Week 0 to Week 24). The study investigates how breath acetone changes during treatment, whether this change differs between participants with and without resistance training, and whether breath acetone at the start or early in treatment can predict the individual response to treatment, such as weight loss and preservation of muscle. The measurement takes about 15-20 minutes at the first visit and about 10 minutes at each later visit. No additional visits, interventions or biological samples are part of this ancillary study.
primary_outcomes: Change in breath acetone concentration from baseline to end of treatment
title: Breath Acetone During Tirzepatide Treatment and Resistance Training in Adults With Obesity

brief_summary:
This study aims to help Canada be better prepared for future pandemics by improving how hospitals collect and use information about patients with respiratory infections, such as influenza, COVID-19, and RSV. Emergency departments are often the first place where new viruses appear, and they care for people from all walks of life. By collecting the same types of information from many hospitals across the country, we can better understand how these illnesses affect people and how to respond more quickly in future emergencies.

The study will build a national database that follows patients from the time they arrive by ambulance or walk into the emergency department through their hospital stay. Researchers will look at symptoms, treatments, test results, recovery, and how well vaccines and medications work in real-world settings.

We believe that people who come to emergency departments with respiratory infections will show important differences in how sick they become, what treatments they receive, and how they recover, depending on factors like age, health conditions, and where they live. We also think this information can help create accurate tools that predict who can safely go home from the emergency department and who is at higher risk of severe illness or death.
primary_outcomes: Number of patient presentations, disease severity, treatments, procedures, health services utilization, and in-hospital mortality by subgroup, over time and by geographic region.
title: CEDRN Pandemic Preparedness Registry

brief_summary: This is a first-in-human study to evaluate the safety, tolerability, and pharmacodynamics of NBIB-0000223 (hereafter referred to as NBIB-223) in participants with Friedreich's Ataxia.
primary_outcomes: Number of Participants with Treatment-emergent Adverse Events
title: Study of NBIB-223 Gene Therapy in Friedreich's Ataxia (FACET)

brief_summary: An open-label study with maintenance dosing to evaluate the long-term safety and efficacy of ORKA-002 in adult participants with moderate-to-severe plaque psoriasis, who previously participated in an Oruka Therapeutics sponsored study.
primary_outcomes: Incidence of Treatment-emergent Adverse Events (TEAEs), Serious Adverse Events (SAEs), and TEAEs of Special Interest (TEAESIs)
title: An Open-label Study With Maintenance Dosing of ORKA-002 in Participants With Moderate-to-Severe Plaque Psoriasis

brief_summary:
The primary purpose of this study is to understand how the body processes the study medicine, called prifetrastat, in people with renal impairment compared to healthy people with normal kidney function. Renal impairment means that a person has worse kidney function than normal. The study will also look at the safety and tolerability of prifetrastat in people with renal impairment compared to healthy people with normal kidney function.

This study is seeking participants who:

* Have moderate or severe renal impairment or
* Healthy people with normal kidney function

All participants in this study will receive a single dose of prifetrastat. The study medicine will be given by mouth at the study clinic. We will compare experiences of people with renal impairment and healthy people with normal kidney function.

Participants will take part in this study for about 2 months. During this time, they will stay at the study clinic for 8 to 16 days.
primary_outcomes: Area Under the Curve From Time Zero to Extrapolated Infinite Time (AUCinf) of Prifetrastat
Maximum Observed Plasma Concentration (Cmax) of Prifetrastat
title: A Study to Learn About the Study Medicine Called Prifetrastat in People With Renal Impairment

brief_summary: To evaluate the efficacy and safety profile of sotoclax combined with azacitidine in newly diagnosed higher-risk MDS patients, including ORR, CR rate, PFS, OS and treatment-related adverse events
interventions: Each treatment cycle is 28-days. Azacitidine 75 mg/m² is administered subcutaneously or intravenously on Days 1-7 of each cycle. Sonrotoclax is orally administered once daily on Days 1-14 within each
lead_sponsor: The Affiliated People's Hospital of Ningbo University
title: Sonrotoclax in Combination With Azacitidine for Previously Untreated Higher-risk Myelodysplastic Syndromes

brief_summary:
What is this study about? This is a Phase 1 study, which means it is one of the first times WIF-2402 is being tested in people. The study includes only healthy adult men.

What are we trying to learn?

Safety and tolerability: Does the drug cause side effects, and how well do people handle it? How the body handles the drug (pharmacokinetics): How the drug is absorbed, how it moves through the body, and how it leaves the body.

What the drug does to the body (pharmacodynamics): What effects the drug has on the body.
primary_outcomes: Number of Participants With Treatment-Emergent Adverse Events
title: A Study to Evaluate the Safety, Pharmacokinetics, and Pharmacodynamics of WIF-2402 in Healthy Adults

brief_summary: To evaluate the efficacy of YKYY013 in patients with chronic hepatitis B virus (HBV) infection with negative hepatitis B e antigen (HBeAg) and treated with nucleoside (acid) analogs (NA).
lead_sponsor: Beijing Youcare Kechuang Pharmaceutical Technology Co., Ltd.
primary_outcomes: The proportion (percent) of participants who achieved serum HBsAg < LLOQ (0.05 IU/mL) and HBVDNA < LLOQ at the 24th week
title: Clinical Study of YKYY013 Injection in HBeAg-negative Chronic Hepatitis B Virus-infected Patients Treated With Nucleos(t)Ide Analogues

brief_summary:
The goal of this randomized controlled trial is to evaluate the feasibility, acceptability, efficacy, and cost-effectiveness of the self-guided online version of the Parents of Little Ones® program - Child version®, a psychological parenting intervention designed to promote mindful parenting, reduce parenting stress, and support parental psychological well-being among parents of children aged 1-6 years.

The main questions it aims to answer are:

* Is the self-guided Parents of Little Ones® program feasible and acceptable to parents of children aged 1-6 years?
* Is the program effective in reducing parenting stress and promoting mindful parenting compared to a waitlist control group? • Is the program cost-effective compared to a waitlist control group? Researchers will compare parents who receive the self-guided Parents of Little Ones®- Child version program with parents assigned to a waitlist control group to evaluate the effects of the intervention.

Participants will:

* Complete online questionnaires assessing parenting-related and psychological outcomes before and after the intervention.
* If assigned to the intervention group, complete eight self-guided online sessions of the Parents of Little Ones® program - Child version®, at a recommended pace of one session per week.
* If assigned to the waitlist control group, continue with their usual activities during the study period and be offered access to the program after the post-intervention assessment.
interventions: Parents of Little Ones - Child version®
primary_outcomes: Changes in Parental Stress From Baseline (week 0) to Post-Intervention (week 10)
Changes in Mindful Parenting From Baseline (week 0) to Post-Intervention (week 10)
title: Online Self-Guided Parents of Little Ones® - Child Version: Effects on Mindful Parenting and Parenting Stress

brief_summary: The overall purpose of this project is to improve how 5 to 7 year old children who have trouble using language use complex sentences. The questions that this study is trying to answer are: Does this treatment help children use sentences with adverbial clauses (e.g., sentences with because, so that, when, until, etc.)? Do children maintain this learning over time?
title: Therapy for Adverbial Clauses

brief_summary: This study aims to assess the proportion of patients with peripheral or central neuropathic pain who achieve at least a 50% improvement in pain at Week 12 after receiving Kabalin Cap.(Pregabalin). The study will also evaluate changes in pain characteristics, severity, and intensity; improvement in pain-related sleep interference; and safety information collected during the study period.
primary_outcomes: Proportion of participants with a ≥50% improvement in pain severity from baseline at Week 12
title: Efficacy and Safety of Kabalin Cap.(Pregabalin) in Patients With Neuropathic Pain

brief_summary:
Polycystic ovary syndrome (PCOS) is a common hormonal disorder in women of reproductive age. It can cause irregular menstrual cycles and difficulty in achieving pregnancy due to anovulation (failure to release an egg from the ovary).

This randomized controlled trial will compare the outcome of combined Myo-inositol and D-chiro-inositol with Metformin among women with anovulatory PCOS.

A total of 90 women aged 18-40 years will be included. Participants will be randomly divided into two groups, with 45 women in each group.

Group A will receive Myo-inositol 2000 mg, D-chiro-inositol 50 mg, and folic acid 200 micrograms twice daily for three months. Group B will receive Metformin 500 mg twice daily for three months.

Both groups will receive dietary advice and instructions to walk and exercise for 30 minutes daily.

The primary outcome will be ovulation after treatment. Ovulation will be assessed by ultrasound examination. The study will compare the proportion of women achieving ovulation in both treatment groups.

The findings will help assess the comparative outcomes of these two treatment approaches in women with anovulatory PCOS.
title: Myo-Inositol and D-Chiro-Inositol Versus Metformin for Treating Anovulation in Women With Polycystic Ovary Syndrome

brief_summary:
The goal of this clinical trial is to learn if a multidisciplinary review of inhaler treatment can increase the use of inhalers with a lower environmental impact in adults admitted to intermediate care units who use inhalers. The main questions it aims to answer are:

* Does the intervention change the percentage of each type of inhaler prescribed (pressurized metered-dose inhalers, dry powder inhalers, and soft mist inhalers) between admission and discharge?
* Does the intervention improve treatment adherence and inhaler technique, reduce the use of rescue inhalers, and reduce carbon dioxide (CO2) emissions? Researchers will compare patients cared for by physicians who apply the intervention with patients cared for by physicians who do not yet apply it, to see if more patients switch to inhalers with a lower environmental impact.

Participants will:

* Have their inhaler prescription reviewed by a physician, who may change it when clinically appropriate, taking environmental impact into account
* Have their adherence and inhaler technique assessed by a healthcare professional
* Receive individual education on how to use their inhalers, if needed
lead_sponsor: Consorci Sanitari de l'Alt Penedès i Garraf
primary_outcomes: Percentage of prescriptions of each inhaler type
title: Sustainable Inhaler Prescribing in Intermediate Care Units

brief_summary:
The purpose of this study is to evaluate the effectiveness of taking a turmeric extract supplement before a root canal to help reduce tooth pain after the procedure.

Patients diagnosed with symptomatic irreversible pulpitis (severe, irreversible tooth nerve inflammation causing significant pain) in their lower back teeth (mandibular molars) will participate in the study. All participants will receive a standard, single visit root canal treatment. Before the procedure begins, one group of patients will receive an oral supplement containing curcumin (the active compound in turmeric) combined with piperine (black pepper extract, which helps the body absorb curcumin). Another group will receive a placebo (an inactive substance).

The investigators will compare the levels of postoperative pain between the two groups in the days following the root canal treatment to see if the turmeric extract supplement successfully provides better pain relief.
title: Effect of Turmeric Extract With Black Pepper on Tooth Pain After Root Canal Treatment

brief_summary:
Psoriasis is a long-term skin disease that causes inflammation, thick skin, and scaly patches on the skin. This study evaluates the safety and effectiveness of risankizumab in combination with ABBV-295 compared with risankizumab alone in adult participants with moderate to severe psoriasis.

Risankizumab is an approved drug for the treatment of moderate to severe psoriasis. Participants are placed in 1 of 2 groups, called treatment arms. Each group receives a different treatment. Participants will receive either risankizumab plus ABBV-295 or risankizumab plus ABBV-295 matching placebo. Around 105 adult participants with moderate to severe psoriasis will be enrolled in the study at approximately 50 sites worldwide.

Participants will receive injections of risankizumab and ABBV-295 or risankizumab and ABBV-295 matching placebo for up to 52 weeks, with a 20-week follow-up period after the last dose of the study.

There may be higher treatment burden for participants in this trial compared to their standard of care (due to study procedures). Participants will attend regular visits during the study at a hospital or clinic. The effect of the treatment will be checked by medical assessments, blood tests, checking for side effects and completing questionnaires.
primary_outcomes: Percentage of Participants Achieving at least a 90% reduction from Baseline in Psoriasis Area and Severity Index (PASI 90)
Number of Participants with Adverse Events (AEs)
title: A Study to Assess Targeted Therapies for Treatment of Adults With Moderate to Severe Psoriasis

brief_summary: Carotid ultrasound-based assessment of maternal hemodynamics to guide HYpertension treatment in PREgnancy - Pilot study - CHYPRE-pilot Healthy pregnancy is associated with significant physiological hemodynamic changes that are critical for maternal adaptation and health. Insufficient adaptive changes can lead to pregnancy disorders such as preeclampsia. Hypertensive disorders of pregnancy (HDP) are a leading cause of maternal and foetal morbidity and mortality. Assessment of maternal hemodynamic alterations can improve management strategies by better risk stratification of pregnant women. Current methods for maternal hemodynamic measurement involve transthoracic echocardiography, requiring expert consultation with a cardiologist and highly trained staff. Simpler techniques like carotid ultrasound based hemodynamic assessment can potentially provide an easy-to perform alternative, requiring minimal training.
title: Carotid Ultrasound-based Assessment of Maternal Hemodynamics to Guide HYpertension Treatment in PREgnancy - Pilot Study

brief_summary:
The goal of this observational study is to get a better understanding which patient characteristics, available in routinely collected data, are associated with the probability that patients referred because of suspected head-and-neck cancer will receive a head-and-neck cancer diagnosis.

Participants will not be recruited specifically for this study. Instead, we will be using routinely-collected national electronic health records linked at patient level, including the National Cancer Waiting Times Monitoring Data (CWT), the National Cancer Registration Data set (NCRD), the Radiotherapy Data set (RTDS), the Systemic Anti-Cancer Therapy Data set (SACT) and the Hospital Episode Statistics.

The main questions it aims to answer are:

1. To describe the patients who are referred with a suspected head-and-neck cancer diagnosis and those who have a confirmed diagnosis.
2. To create a typology of the diagnostic pathway across the country (e.g., comparing 21 regions reflecting the Cancer Alliances).
3. To explore differences among the 21 National Health Service Cancer Alliances in the referral rates of patients with suspected head-and-neck cancer and the number of referred patients in whom a cancer can be diagnosed.
4. To develop a prognostic model that can predict the probability that referred patients will receive a head-and-neck cancer diagnosis.
5. To evaluate the value of Hospital Episode Statistics (HES), National Cancer Registration Data (NCRD), Radiotherapy Data Set (RTDS) and Systemic Anti-Cancer Therapy (SACT) data to monitor referral pathways for patients with suspected head-and-neck cancer.
6. To develop a health economic model of the diagnostic and treatment pathways of referrals for suspected head-and-neck cancer.
7. To assess hospital care costs across the diagnostic and treatment pathways for head and neck cancer.
primary_outcomes: To describe the patients who are referred with a suspected head-and-neck cancer diagnosis and those who have a confirmed diagnosis
title: EVEREST-HN-3: Linkage of National Data Sets for Suspected Head-and-neck Cancer Referrals

brief_summary: Emerging evidence highlights a bidirectional gut-heart axis, particularly relevant in patients with right heart failure. Elevated right atrial pressures and systemic congestion may impair intestinal perfusion and compromise epithelial integrity, leading to increased gut permeability ("leaky gut") and translocation of microbial products. These processes can trigger systemic inflammation and exacerbate cardiac dysfunction. Alterations in the gut microbiome-collectively referred to as dysbiosis-have also been linked to heart failure pathogenesis. However, the role of intestinal barrier dysfunction and microbial signatures in patients with severe tricuspid regurgitation (TR) remains largely unexplored.
lead_sponsor: Heart and Diabetes Center North-Rhine Westfalia
primary_outcomes: Change in Gut Microbial Metabolite Plasma Levels
title: Gut Microbial Metabolites and Intestinal Permeability in Patients With Severe Tricuspid Regurgitation Undergoing Transcatheter Tricuspid Valve Intervention

brief_summary:
The goal of this study is to learn how depression during pregnancy is linked to changes in the brain and body of the mother and to the development of the baby, in pregnant women with major depressive disorder (MDD) and pregnant women without depression.

The main questions it aims to answer are:

* How common is major depressive disorder during pregnancy in a European multi-site cohort?
* Do pregnant women with MDD show differences in hippocampal volume compared with pregnant women without depression?
* Do maternal blood, placenta, cord blood, brain imaging and heart activity measures, and the brain and development of the babies, differ between the two groups?

Pregnant women will be screened within the 20th week of pregnancy and assigned to the MDD group or to the control group based on a structured clinical interview. They will not receive any study drug: women with depression will receive the usual care recommended by clinical guidelines.

Participants will:

* Have clinical, psychiatric and psychological assessments (interviews and questionnaires) at screening, at 22, 26 and 32 weeks of pregnancy, at birth, and at 1 and 6 months after birth
* Have a brain MRI with simultaneous EEG-ECG or photoplethysmography (PPG) at about 22 weeks of pregnancy
* Have a fetal MRI by 22 weeks and fetal ultrasound scans at 22, 26 and 32 weeks
* Give blood samples at 22, 26 and 32 weeks of pregnancy, and a cord blood sample at birth (placenta samples in a subgroup at the Milan center only)

brief_summary:
People with chronic heart failure or chronic lung disease (such as COPD or interstitial lung disease) often feel short of breath when they exert themselves. A handheld fan blowing air on the face may ease this feeling, but it is not clear whether the benefit lasts with longer home use, whether it depends on the direction of the airflow, or whether it works in patients with heart disease and in hot climates.

This study will compare three conditions in adults with stable chronic heart and/or lung disease who become breathless on exertion: (1) a handheld fan directed at the face, (2) a handheld fan directed at the leg, and (3) no fan (usual care). Participants will be randomly assigned (1:1:1) to one of the three groups. The two fan groups will use the fan at home for 12 weeks. The no-fan group will receive a fan after the final assessment. The person measuring outcomes will not know which group each participant is in.

The main outcome is breathlessness (Borg 0-10 scale) in the 5 minutes after a 6-minute walk test at week 12. Other outcomes include walking distance, recovery time, breathlessness severity and impact (Dyspnoea-12), functional class, global change in breathlessness, fan use and acceptability, and emergency visits or hospital admissions.

The study also includes interviews with about 24 to 30 participants from the three groups after week 12, to understand how the fan was used, how acceptable it was, and how heat and humidity affected it. Trial and interview findings will be analysed separately and then combined.
interventions: Handheld Fan Directed at the Face
Handheld Fan Directed at the Leg
primary_outcomes: Breathlessness intensity (Borg CR10) after the 6-minute walk test
title: Handheld Fan Direction for Breathlessness in Chronic Heart and Lung Disease

brief_summary:
Lower-extremity arterial disease in the stage of chronic limb-threatening ischemia (CLTI) carries a high risk of major amputation and death. According to international vascular guidelines for the management of patients with CLTI, revascularization should aim to restore blood flow to the arteries of the foot, ensuring the minimum level of perfusion required for tissue repair and regeneration. However, establishing direct blood flow to the foot arteries is often limited in patients with distal arterial occlusion or multilevel arterial disease. Furthermore, simultaneous multilevel revascularization carries an increased operative risk for patients with significant comorbidities. Collectively, these factors complicate the prediction of optimal limb perfusion-both before and after revascularization-and, consequently, the selection of an appropriate treatment strategy.

Traditional diagnostic methods have limitations in assessing the severity of ischemia, particularly in patients presenting with rest pain and/or trophic lesions.

The study (PERIOX) is to be undertaken to evaluate the use of near-infrared spectroscopy (NIRS, Medtronic, INVOS) - a rapid, simple, non-invasive, and painless method that can be applied to any area of the skin and allows for continuous, real-time monitoring of changes in tissue oxygenation - as a tool for assessing limb viability before, during, and after revascularization in patients with lower-extremity arterial disease presenting with CLTI
interventions: Near-infrared spectroscopy (NIRS, Medtronic, INVOS) tissue oxygenation monitoring
primary_outcomes: Changing in regional tissue oxygenation in the distal lower limb (rSO2, %) from baseline before, during surgery, and after lower limb arterial revascularization
title: Perioperative Limb Oxygenation Monitoring in Patients With CLTI

* Do community-based non-contact boxing exercises improve the balance in participants with chronic stroke?
* How is the exercise intensity of boxing exercises in individuals with chronic stroke? Researchers will test one group of participants without a comparison group.

Participants will need to complete the following tasks over 8 weeks:
