brief_summary: This 12- week, single-center, open-label case study is being conducted to assess the efficacy and tolerance of a brightening skincare regimen comprised of a facial wash, brightening serum, brightening exfoliating pads, face cream and sunscreen by healthy females with clinically determined mild to moderate Post-inflammatory hyperpigmentation (PIH).
primary_outcomes: Improvement of Clinical Efficacy Parameters at 2, 4, 8, and 12 weeks versus Baseline
Measurement of subject self assessment questionnaire
title: A Case Study to Assess a Brightening Skincare Regimen in Patients With Bothersome Skin Dark Spots

brief_summary:
The Miami Pouch is a continent cutaneous urinary diversion using the plicated right colon and the ileocecal valve as a catheterizable continent stoma. Despite its long history, functional outcomes remain poorly reported, with no consensus on continence definition or standardized assessment tools.

This single-center cross sectional cohort study evaluates functional outcomes in patients who underwent Miami Pouch urinary diversion at Hôpital Lyon Sud (Hospices Civils de Lyon, France) between 2015 and 2025. Patients were identified through institutional medical coding (PMSI) and contacted by telephone to complete validated patient-reported outcome measures.

The primary objective is to assess stomal continence using the International Consultation on Incontinence Questionnaire - Short Form (ICIQ-SF).

Hypothesis: The Miami Pouch provides acceptable long-term stomal continence with limited impact on digestive function.
title: Functional Outcomes of the Miami Pouch Continent Cutaneous Urinary Diversion: A Quality of Life Study

brief_summary: This randomized controlled study aimed to evaluate the effectiveness of a Digital Aging Training Program in improving e-health literacy and adaptation to digital health systems among adults aged 65 years and older. Participants were randomly assigned to an intervention or control group. The intervention group received six structured training sessions over three weeks, focusing on digital health literacy and the practical use of Türkiye's digital health systems, the Central Physician Appointment System and Türkiye's Personal Health Record System. The control group received usual care.
title: Supporting Digital Aging in Older Individuals

brief_summary: Autism Spectrum Disorder (ASD) is a pervasive neurodevelopmental disorder that currently affects 1 in 32 children. ASD is characterized by persistent deficits in social communication and restricted, repetitive behaviors. For instance, people with ASD often show great difficulty in recognizing social cues and understanding others' emotions, as well as having a tendency to act inflexibly and inappropriately in social situations, all of which contribute to lifelong social and occupational dysfunctions.To date, there is no cure for ASD. Existing treatments are primarily behavioral or educational based. Although some treatments show positive therapeutic effects in reducing patients' core autistic symptoms, the interventions are often labor- and time-intensive. Recently, a non-invasive painless brain stimulation technique, "transcranial direct current stimulation (tDCS)," has received increasing interest in clinical settings as a potential tool for cognitive enhancement and neurorehabilitation for various cognitive dysfunctions. This study aims to examine the effectiveness of tDCS treatment combined with cognitive training for individuals with ASD. We will study the effect before and after treatment.
primary_outcomes: Change in Executive Functioning - Executive Composite Score
title: Effects of Transcranial Direct Current Stimulation for Enhancing Cognitive Function in Individuals With Autism Spectrum Disorder - A Pilot fMRI Study

brief_summary:
The goal of this feasibility clinical trial is to learn whether a small device that stimulates a nerve in the outer ear can be safely and practically used at home by adults with generalized anxiety disorder (GAD). The study will also explore whether this treatment may help lower anxiety and improve sleep quality. Participants will be adults aged 18 to 65 years in Birjand, Iran.

The main questions it aims to answer are:

* Is ear stimulation safe and practical for participants to use at home for four weeks?
* Do participants who receive active stimulation have lower anxiety levels than those who receive sham stimulation?
* Does the treatment help improve sleep quality and other anxiety-related symptoms?
* Can participants follow the treatment schedule and use the monitoring devices as instructed?

Researchers will compare active stimulation with sham stimulation. Sham stimulation is a comparison procedure designed to resemble the active treatment but does not deliver the same active stimulation. This comparison will help researchers explore possible treatment effects and assess whether a larger study is practical.

Participants will:

* Complete screening assessments and questionnaires about anxiety, sleep, and other symptoms.
* Be randomly assigned to receive active ear stimulation or sham stimulation.
* Use their assigned device at home for four weeks, following the study instructions.
* Wear a wristband to help record treatment use and selected body measurements.
* Complete assessments during weeks 2 and 4, followed by check-ups during weeks 6 and 8.
* Report any side effects and provide information about their experience using the device.
interventions: Sham Transcutaneous Auricular Vagus Nerve Stimulation (sham-taVNS)
primary_outcomes: Change in Anxiety Severity Measured by the Hamilton Anxiety Rating Scale (HAM-A)
title: Auricular Vagus Nerve Stimulation for Anxiety and Sleep Quality in Patients With Generalized Anxiety Disorder

brief_summary: This study is an ancillary study to the RESIST trial, in which adults with obesity receive the weight-loss medication tirzepatide and are randomly assigned to a structured resistance training program or to usual care for 24 weeks. RESIST-EXPLORE investigates which molecular, metabolic, inflammatory, immune-cell and microbiome-related changes occur during this treatment, and how they relate to changes in body weight, body composition and muscle-related outcomes measured in RESIST. Blood samples are collected at the start (Week 0) and at the end (Week 24) of treatment; stool samples and tongue and nasal swabs are collected at Week 0, Week 4 and Week 24.
primary_outcomes: Change in circulating protein biomarker profile (plasma/serum)
Change in frequencies of circulating lymphocyte subsets
Change in gut microbiome composition and diversity (stool)
Change in oral microbiome composition and diversity (tongue swab)
Change in nasal microbiome composition and diversity (nasal swab)
title: Molecular and Microbiome Changes During Tirzepatide Treatment and Resistance Training in Obesity

brief_summary: Use of tele-assessment for evaluation and diagnosis of autism in toddlers has demonstrated success in increasing service access and reducing clinical wait times, with high levels of diagnostic accuracy, clinician confidence, and family satisfaction; however, these models have not yet been rigorously evaluated within the preschool age range. The TAP-Preschool (TAP-P) was developed by the investigative team for tele-assessment of autism in preschool-aged children, with preliminary studies demonstrating utility with many children with limited verbal language and some children with more flexible verbal language. The proposed study will recruit a larger sample of children with varied language and phenotypic profiles to (1) thoroughly evaluate the psychometric properties of the TAP-P and (2) investigate child and family factors associated with diagnostic ascertainment and family satisfaction with tele-assessment to inform the creation of a decision support tool intended to recommend families for either tele- or in-person assessment, with the ultimate goal of optimizing clinical care models to serve patients in efficient ways while routing families to diagnostic care pathways that best fit their needs.
primary_outcomes: Rate of diagnostic agreement between tele-assessment and clinical best estimate in-person assessment
title: Evaluation of the TAP-Preschool (TAP-P) for Tele-assessment of Autism in Preschool-aged Children

brief_summary: This study aims to assess the proportion of patients with essential hypertension who achieve blood pressure control rates at Week 24 following treatment with Ex-one tablets or Ex-one Plus tablets, and to collect safety information observed during the study period.
primary_outcomes: Proportion of patients achieving blood pressure control rates at Week 24 after treatment with Ex-one tablets or Ex-one Plus tablets
title: Blood Pressure Control and Safety of Ex-one or Ex-one Plus in Essential Hypertension

brief_summary:
Rehabilitation of the partially or totally edentulous mandible with implant supported prosthesis has become a common practice in the last few decades. Local conditions of the edentulous ridges may be unfavorable for dental implant placement, where sufficient bony support in both the horizontal and vertical dimensions is the foundation of any successful oral rehabilitation with dental implants.

Challenges include the resorpative changes of the alveolar ridge after tooth extractions and the hard tissue deficits due to chronic periodontal disease or congenitally missing teeth. Neoplasm, osteomyelitis, cysts or trauma can also compromise the situation. All these factors require the oral implantologist to create using regenerative techniques sufficient hard tissue support at the appropriate site before or during dental implant installation.

Multiple bone grafting materials and techniques have been used to reconstruct the partially dentate and edentulous posterior mandibular ridges with high rates of success, these techniques include block onlay grafting technique, guided bone regeneration using membranes or meshes and distraction osteogenesis. The selection of the optimal technique depends on various factors, including the degree of the defect, the grafted bone substitute available, the medical condition of the patient and also the skill and experience of the operator.

The aim of this study is to evaluate the alveolar bone volume by the CBCT after performing oblique sandwich osteotomy in conjunction with interpositional autogenous bone grafting in the atrophied posterior mandible.
title: Assessment of the Oblique Sandwich Osteotomy for Augmentation of Posterior Atrophic Mandible

brief_summary: This phase I/II trial tests the safety, best dose, and effectiveness of disulfiram for preventing treatment complications in patients with large B-cell lymphoma that has come back after a period of improvement (relapsed) or that does not respond to treatment (refractory) and who are undergoing chimeric antigen receptor (CAR) T-cell therapy. Two major complications of CAR T-cell therapy include cytokine release syndrome (CRS) and immune effector cell-associated neurotoxicity syndrome (ICANS). CRS results from inflammation in the body when the immune system responds too aggressively to the modified T cells working to attack cancer cells. ICANS is inflammation of the brain or nerves. CRS is most often a prelude to ICANS, and both of these toxicities currently require immunosuppression for treatment, which can inhibit CAR T-cell response. Disulfiram has been found to impact several biologic pathways that cause CRS. Disulfiram may be safe and effective for reducing the incidence and severity of reactions to CAR T-cell therapy without inhibiting CAR T-cell response.
lead_sponsor: University of Michigan Rogel Cancer Center
primary_outcomes: Proportion of patients that are alive and free from grade 2-4 cytokine release syndrome (CRS) with no intervening treatment of CRS
title: Disulfiram for Preventing Treatment Complications in Patients Undergoing CAR T-cell Therapy for Relapsed or Refractory Diffuse Large B-cell Lymphoma

brief_summary: This Stage II behavioral intervention development project will examine the efficacy of a multi-domain health behavior intervention for primary prevention of Alzheimer's disease and related dementias (ADRD) in middle age.
conditions: Alzheimer's Disease and Alzheimer's Disease Related Dementias (AD/ADRD)
title: Tailored Education for Aging and Cognitive Health: A Health Behavior Change Intervention for Midlife Adults at Risk for Alzheimer's Disease and Related Dementias

brief_summary: Respiratory illnesses are a leading cause of morbidity and mortality worldwide, yet their prevalence in the general population remains poorly characterized. Computed tomography (CT) is the most effective diagnostic tool for identifying respiratory illnesses that cause changes to the lung parenchyma, such as pulmonary infections, fibrosis, and nodules. The diagnostic power of CT led the US Preventive Services Task Force (USPSTF) to issue lung cancer screening guidelines. In this prospective, observational cohort study, the study team will recruit 10,000 individuals aged 21 to 85 years, stratified into three cohorts: Cohort 1 (Medical Indication Group), Cohort 2 (Guideline-Based Screening Group), and Cohort 3 (Asymptomatic Research Low-Dose CT \[LDCT\] Group). The primary analysis will estimate the baseline cross-sectional prevalence of LDCT-detectable pulmonary findings in Cohort 3. Secondary analyses will compare baseline LDCT findings across all three cohorts and evaluate baseline associations between risk/exposure variables and CT findings. Exploratory follow-up analyses will use clinical data from the electronic health record (EHR), as available, for up to 5 years after the baseline/index CT. This study has the potential to transform health screening strategies, reduce disease burden, and improve health outcomes across diverse populations.
title: Comprehensive Lung Health

brief_summary:
The purpose of this study is to learn about the safety and effectiveness of berobenatide in adult women who have both stress urinary incontinence (SUI) and obesity or overweight.

Participants will be in the study for about 63 weeks
primary_outcomes: Change From Baseline in Stress Incontinence Episode Frequency (IEF)

brief_summary:
This randomized controlled study compared podcast-based clinical scenarios with printed clinical scenarios. Participants were first-year nursing students enrolled in a health assessment course. The aim was to examine whether the learning format affected students' self-reported clinical reasoning and reflective thinking.

Ninety nursing students were randomly assigned to a podcast group or a printed-material group. The podcast group received six audio recordings presenting clinical scenarios. The printed-material group received materials covering the same core clinical content. Students completed questionnaires assessing clinical reasoning and reflective thinking before the intervention and 12 weeks after the first assessment. Researchers compared the groups' final questionnaire scores, taking their starting scores into account.
title: PODCAST VERSUS PRINTED CLINICAL SCENARIOS FOR CLINICAL REASONING AND REFLECTION IN NURSING STUDENTS

brief_summary: To establish a longitudinal cohort spanning the entire care continuum of acquired aplastic anemia (AA), from diagnosis and treatment through long-term follow-up, integrating routinely collected clinical data with biospecimens obtained in accordance with applicable ethical and regulatory requirements. The cohort will support observational studies of the natural history of AA; treatment effectiveness and safety; the evolution of clonal hematopoiesis and clonal T-cell populations; immune reconstitution following immunosuppressive therapy (IST); the incidence of platelet transfusion refractoriness and its association with response to IST; and hematopoietic and immune reconstitution after transplantation. Ultimately, the cohort aims to generate real-world evidence to inform clinical practice and reduce the burden of AA.
interventions: A combined retrospective and prospective observational follow-up
lead_sponsor: Institute of Hematology & Blood Diseases Hospital, China
title: Aplastic Anemia Life-Course Cohort Study

brief_summary: this study aims to evaluate the clinical efficacy of a novel, targeted tracheal Kinesio taping protocol as a complementary intervention to enhance airway clearance and expedite weaning milestones in severely burned patients. Specifically, we investigate the direct impact of this neurosensory and biomechanical airway modality on objective cough power-measured via Peak Cough Flow (PCF)-and its ultimate influence on total tracheostomy decannulation time. We hypothesize that the targeted application of tracheal Kinesio taping will safely stabilize airway structures, augment the explosive expiratory phase necessary for productive secretion clearance, and significantly shorten the temporal window required to achieve successful, complication-free decannulation in this vulnerable population.
primary_outcomes: Peak Cough Flow (PCF)expressed in Liters per minute, L/min
title: Effect of Targeted Tracheal Kinesio Taping on Cough Efficacy and Decannulation Time in Burned Patients

brief_summary:
The goal of this observational study is to learn how much energy and protein patients actually take by mouth in the days after surgery for colorectal cancer, compared with the amounts recommended by the hospital's enhanced recovery after surgery (ERAS) programme.

The main questions it aims to answer are:

* How many patients reach at least 60% of the recommended daily energy intake by day 5 after surgery, or by the day they leave hospital?
* Do patients aged 60 years or older reach the recommended intake less often than younger patients?

Participants will:

* Have all food, drinks and oral nutrition supplements recorded every day, either by a family member using a simple diary or during a daily interview with a dietitian
* Undergo daily assessment of gastrointestinal tolerance using the I-FEED score and the feeding intolerance score
* Have the results of routine blood tests recorded
* Be contacted by telephone about 3 months after surgery to ask about body weight and any further cancer treatment No new treatment is given. All participants receive the usual care of the hospital's ERAS programme.
lead_sponsor: First Affiliated Hospital of Chongqing Medical University
primary_outcomes: Proportion of patients reaching at least 60% of the prescribed energy target
title: Postoperative Energy and Protein Intake Attainment After Elective Laparoscopic Colorectal Cancer Surgery

brief_summary: Auto-immune conditions affecting the central nervous system are complex and can be serious life-threatening disorders. Some are well described and have established pathways of diagnosis and management e.g. multiple sclerosis (MS). But most others are quite rare, with little knowledge on clinical course, effect of treatments and long-term outcomes. Current treatments are mainly based on case reviews and expert opinions that are often limited to very few cases encountered. Through the ADONeS Study data on a substantial number of patients could be collected and shared through collaborative research.
primary_outcomes: Increase in overall knowledge and level of understanding regarding autoimmune disorders of the nervous system
title: ADONeSS - Study of Autoimmune Diseases of the Nervous System

brief_summary: The aim of this study is to investigate the relationships among balance, mobility, pain, fatigue, and quality of life in individuals diagnosed with Lyme disease. Lyme disease can cause various musculoskeletal and neurological symptoms that significantly impact physical function and overall well-being. In this observational study, participants will undergo clinical evaluations to assess balance performance, functional mobility levels, pain severity, fatigue levels, and health-related quality of life. The data obtained will help to better understand the clinical burden of Lyme disease and provide insight for developing targeted rehabilitation strategies.
title: Investigation of the Relationships Among Balance, Mobility, Pain, Fatigue, and Quality of Life in Individuals With Lyme Disease

brief_summary:
Human dignity is an important value in nursing care. However, nursing students may find it difficult to understand this abstract concept and apply it to clinical situations. This study aimed to compare the effects of creative drama and case analysis-based education on nursing students' perception and understanding of human dignity and to examine whether the educational effects were maintained four weeks later.

This randomized controlled study included 80 fourth-year nursing students at a public university in Türkiye. Participants were randomly assigned to two groups: creative drama (40 students) and case analysis (40 students).

Both groups received 120 minutes of education covering the same topics related to human dignity. Students in the creative drama group participated in role-playing, improvisation, and reflection activities based on clinical situations. Students in the case analysis group examined and discussed clinical cases involving human dignity in nursing care.

Students' perception and understanding of human dignity were assessed using the Perception and Understanding of Human Dignity in Nursing Scale before the educational intervention, immediately afterward, and four weeks later.

A total of 74 students completed all three assessments. Both educational approaches improved students' perception and understanding of human dignity. However, students who received creative drama-based education demonstrated greater improvements immediately after the intervention and higher scores at the four-week follow-up compared with those who received case analysis-based education.

The findings suggest that creative drama may be an effective educational approach for helping nursing students understand human dignity and its importance in nursing care.
primary_outcomes: Change in Perception and Understanding of Human Dignity in Nursing Scale (PUHDNS) Total Score
title: The Effect of Creative Drama on Human Dignity in Nursing Students

brief_summary: As modulator therapies extend the lifespan of CF patients, the detection of complications like Cystic Fibrosis Related Diabetes (CFRD) becomes increasingly vital. The current gold standard for CFRD screening, the 2-hour OGTT, is cumbersome and suffers from low compliance. This study proposes that Continuous Glucose Monitoring (CGM) could offer a more comprehensive, easier, and potentially more compliant screening method. The research aims to correlate various CGM parameters (e.g., time in hyperglycemia) with traditional glycemic markers like OGTT glucose levels, GMI, average glucose, variability, and HbA1c. Additionally, the research seeks to understand patient and parent/guardian preferences for CFRD screening modalities. This prospective observational study will involve CF patients wearing a Dexcom CGM around the time of standard OGTT and HbA1c tests, followed by surveys, with the ultimate goal of paving the way for CGM to improve early detection and management of dysglycemia in CF children.
primary_outcomes: Average Blood Glucose Level from Continuous Glucose Monitoring
title: Continuous Glucose Monitoring Parameter and Oral Glucose Tolerance Testing (OGTT) Parameters in Children and Young Adults With Cystic Fibrosis (CF)

brief_summary:
This study aims to investigate lower limb and foot health in children aged 7-16 years who participate in ballet or football. Both sports provide important health benefits but involve repetitive movements and physical demands that may affect the developing musculoskeletal system.

The study will include approximately 148 children: 74 ballet dancers from the Royal Danish Ballet School and 74 football players from participating Danish football clubs. Their findings will be compared with existing reference data from 501 typically developing Danish schoolchildren.

The main objective is to determine whether children participating in ballet have greater outward hip rotation than children in the reference group. The researchers will also examine ankle mobility, foot shape, joint flexibility, muscle function, balance, pain, and quality of life. Differences between ballet dancers and football players will be explored.

Each child will undergo a standardized clinical examination, including measurements of joint movement, lower limb alignment, and foot characteristics. Additional assessments will include three-dimensional foot scanning, functional movement tests, and questionnaires about pain, physical activity, and quality of life.

A subgroup of children will also participate in observations and group interviews to explore how young athletes experience and manage pain and soreness during training.

This is an observational study. No experimental treatment or intervention will be provided. The findings may improve our understanding of normal physical development and sport-related adaptations in active children and help inform future approaches to preventing musculoskeletal problems in young athletes.
title: Lower Limb and Foot Health in Danish Paediatric Ballet Dancers and Foot-ballers

brief_summary:
Background:

Malaria is a disease caused by parasites spread by mosquito bites. Researchers want to test a vaccine that could stop mosquitoes from picking up these parasites when they bite infected people. This could stop malaria from spreading.

Objective:

To test a study vaccine (Pvs230D1-EPA/MM) to stop malaria transmission in healthy adults.

Eligibility:

Healthy people aged 18 to 54 years. People who already received the vaccine during a different study are also needed.

Design:

Participants will be screened. They will have a physical exam. They will have blood tests and a test of their heart function (a simple electrocardiogram or EKG).

The vaccine is given as an injectionin the upper arm. Participants who have never gotten the study vaccine will get 3 vaccines; each injection will be about 1 month apart. Participants who were vaccinated before will receive only 1 vaccine for this study. All participants will have multiple phone and in-person follow-up visits after each vaccination.

Two to 12 weeks after their last vaccine, all participants will be injected with live malaria parasites. Then they will be seenin the clinic for about 3 days. They will be monitored daily until they develop symptoms of malaria, usually in about 10 days then will be admitted to the NIH hospital.

While in the NIH hospital, participants will have 3 mosquito feedings: Two cups containing mosquitoes will be placed on an arm or leg. The mosquitoes will feed for about 15 minutes. Participants will receive medicines to relieve discomfort from the bites.

Participants will then be treated for malaria. They will have follow-up visits and calls until they fully recover.
interventions: Plasmodium vivax Challenge Agent Derived from PvHMB-CCE001
lead_sponsor: National Institute of Allergy and Infectious Diseases (NIAID)
primary_outcomes: To assess efficacy of Pvs230D1-EPA/MM vaccine using the CHMI-T model.
To assess the safety and reactogenicity of Pvs230D1-EPA/MM primary vaccine series in healthy malaria-naive adults.
title: Transmission-Blocking Vaccine Pvs230D1-EPA/Matrix-M in Healthy Malaria-Naive Adults Using a Plasmodium Vivax Controlled Human Malaria Infection and Transmission Model

brief_summary:
This clinical study aims to evaluate bone healing after the surgical removal of jaw cysts using a bone graft material made from chicken eggshells, with or without platelet-rich fibrin (PRF), a substance prepared from the patient's own blood.

Removal of a jaw cyst can leave an empty space in the surrounding bone. Although this space may heal naturally, bone regeneration can take several months. Hydroxyapatite is a bone-like mineral that may support new bone formation. Combining it with PRF may further improve healing.

This prospective, controlled clinical study is being conducted in Sana'a, Yemen. Participants undergo surgical removal of jaw cysts and receive one of the treatment approaches included in the study. The researchers compare bone healing between treatment groups using clinical examinations and dental imaging, including cone-beam computed tomography (CBCT).

Participants are followed for up to six months after surgery. The study evaluates bone regeneration, postoperative pain, wound healing, and possible complications.

The researchers aim to determine whether eggshell-derived hydroxyapatite combined with PRF improves bone regeneration compared with the other treatments being investigated.
interventions: Eggshell-Derived Hydroxyapatite With Platelet-Rich Fibrin Grafting
primary_outcomes: Change in Alveolar Bone Defect Dimensions Following Cyst Enucleation
Change in Radiographic Density Within the Healing Bone Defect
title: Eggshell-Derived Hydroxyapatite With Platelet-Rich Fibrin for Bone Regeneration After Jaw Cyst Removal

brief_summary:
The goal of this ambispective cohort study is to evaluate the safety and palliative efficacy of a dose-escalated stereotactic ablative radiotherapy (SABR) protocol in ultra-elderly patients (age \> 75) with medically inoperable bladder cancer. This study combines a retrospective analysis of early clinical cases with a prospective observation of subsequent patients treated under the same institutional protocol.

The main questions it aims to answer are:

1. What is the safety profile and durability of symptom control (specifically hemostasis) of a 5-fraction SABR regimen for focal bladder tumors in this fragile population?
2. Does dose escalation (from 30 Gy to 40 Gy) impact the occurrence of dose-limiting toxicities (DLTs)? As an ambispective study utilizing a 3+3 design-based logic, there is no separate comparison group. Researchers evaluate four dose levels (30 Gy, 35 Gy, 37.5 Gy, and 40 Gy) to observe if higher radiation doses improve local control without increasing severe side effects.

Participants in this cohort:

1. Received/Receive SABR delivered in 5 daily fractions to the primary bladder tumor, with a 'safety-first' optimization strategy that prioritized OAR sparing over target coverage.
2. Are evaluated for DLTs and followed up for Hematuria-Free Survival (HFS) and overall survival.
primary_outcomes: Maximum tolerated dose (MTD) of five-fraction SABR
title: Dose-Escalation Stereotactic Ablative Radiotherapy for Ultra-Elderly Bladder Cancer

brief_summary:
The goal of this three-arm cluster randomized controlled trial is to evaluate and compare the effectiveness of two psychological group interventions, Enhanced WELLFOCUS Positive Psychotherapy (EWPPT) and the culturally adapted Narrative Enhancement and Cognitive Therapy (NECT) program, in Chinese adults (aged 18 to 65) diagnosed with schizophrenia or related psychotic disorders who live in halfway houses (HWHs) in Hong Kong. The primary outcomes are personal recovery, quality of life, and wellbeing. The secondary outcomes are self-efficacy and meaning in life. Additional outcomes are self-stigma and strengths use. Randomization is done at the halfway house level: each participating HWH is randomly assigned to EWPPT, NECT, or a treatment-as-usual (TAU) control. All participants within a given HWH receive the same condition. This reduces the risk of contamination between residents who live together.

The study has two objectives. Objective 1 is to compare each intervention against the TAU control on these outcomes. Objective 2 is to identify the psychological processes underlying change in each active arm. Participants will be asked to complete standardized paper-and-pencil questionnaires at three time points: at baseline before the group sessions start (T1), immediately after the sessions end (T2), and at 3-month follow-up (T3). A purposive sample of participants will also be invited to an individual face-to-face semi-structured qualitative interview.
primary_outcomes: Change of Personal Recovery from T1 to T3
Change of Quality of Life from T1 to T3
Change of Wellbeing from T1 to T3
title: Evaluating EWPPT and NECT for People With Schizophrenia

brief_summary:
The goal of this study was to determine whether eating before exercise changes how male soccer players use fat and carbohydrate for energy. This study also examined how consistent these measurements are when the same exercise test was repeated on separate days. The main questions it aimed to answer were:

Were measurements of fat and carbohydrate use during exercise consistent across two tests performed after an overnight fast?

Did fat and carbohydrate use during exercise differ between fasted and fed conditions?

Participants attended the laboratory on four occasions after fasting overnight for 10-12 hours, had their body composition and maximal aerobic fitness measured, and completed a practice cycling session during the first visit.

During the second and third visits, all participants completed a 30-minute cycling test at a moderate intensity following overnight fasting to establish the test-retest reproducibility of metabolic measurements.

During the fourth visit, they completed two 30-minute cycling tests: one before eating and another one hour after an unrestricted meal of pasta and meatballs. During cycling test, participants wore a mask so researchers could measure their breathing gases and estimate how much fat and carbohydrate they used for energy.
interventions: Moderate-Intensity Cycling Under Fasted and Fed Conditions
primary_outcomes: Fat Oxidation Rate During Fasted and Fed Exercise
Carbohydrate Oxidation Rate During Fasted and Fed Exercise

brief_summary:
The goal of this clinical trial is to learn whether a peer recovery support program designed for people experiencing homelessness can be successfully delivered as part of opioid use disorder treatment. Peer recovery support specialists are individuals who use their personal experience with substance use and recovery to support others. The main questions this pilot study aims to answer are:

* Is it feasible to conduct the study and deliver the peer recovery support program?
* Is the program acceptable to participants?
* Can the program be delivered as intended?
* Does the program show promise for helping participants stay engaged in opioid use disorder treatment?

Researchers will compare participants who receive peer recovery support in addition to usual opioid use disorder treatment with participants who receive usual treatment alone.

Participants will:

* Be randomly assigned to one of the two study groups.
* Complete a survey when they enroll and another survey approximately 3 months later.
* If assigned to the peer recovery support group, be offered individualized support from a peer recovery support specialist for 3 months, with meetings approximately weekly.
* If assigned to the peer recovery support group, complete an interview at the end of the study about their experiences with the program.

brief_summary:
This study aims to find out whether a dietary supplement containing ginseng and notoginseng (GIN-201) can safely reduce persistent fatigue in adults. Chronic fatigue is a lasting feeling of tiredness that rest does not relieve which affects about 10% of adults in Hong Kong and can harm sleep, thinking, and quality of life. Ginseng and notoginseng are traditional Chinese medicine herbs thought to boost energy, and early research suggests they may help with fatigue, but their combined effect has not been tested in people.

The study will recruit 130 adults aged 30 to 75 who report fatigue and poor sleep. Participants will be randomly assigned to one of two groups: one group takes GIN-201 capsules (4 per day) for 6 weeks, while the other group waits 6 weeks before starting the same supplement. Both groups will then be followed for another 6 weeks. Fatigue, sleep, mood, quality of life, and sexual/menopausal symptoms will be measured with standard questionnaires, and blood tests will check for markers of inflammation, stress, aging, and mitochondrial health, as well as for safety.

The main question the study is trying to answer is: Does taking GIN-201 for 6 weeks reduce fatigue more than no treatment, and is it safe? The researchers hypothesize that GIN-201 will reduce fatigue in adults with persistent fatigue. The study will also explore whether changes in blood biomarkers are linked to any benefits, which may help identify who is most likely to respond to the supplement.
title: Ginseng-notoginseng Containing Supplement for Chronic Fatigue

brief_summary:
Background: Patients living with chronic kidney disease (CKD) face numerous therapeutic decisions throughout their care pathway, particularly regarding the choice of kidney replacement therapy modality. In this context, shared decision-making plays a central role in enabling patients to actively participate in treatment decisions according to their preferences and quality-of-life expectations. However, several studies have shown that the information provided to patients may sometimes be insufficient and that patients' preferences are not always aligned with the treatment modalities ultimately initiated.

Patients with CKD may also feel overwhelmed by their diagnosis and by the large amount of medical information they receive. Emotional responses to the disease vary considerably and are associated with heterogeneous needs for information and support, which may contribute to impaired quality of life.

In this context, peer support, based on the sharing of experiences between individuals facing similar situations, may represent a valuable complement to the support provided by healthcare teams.

Methods: A pragmatic, comparative, open-label, randomised, parallel-group, multicentre trial will be conducted involving 260 patients at six nephrology centres in French region. The primary objective is to compare, over a 12-month follow-up period, quality-adjusted life years (QALYs) - which take into account both survival time and health-related quality of life - in patients with stage IV chronic kidney disease, between a group of patients receiving standard care and support from the nephrology team and a group using the TOMO platform in addition to standard care Discussion: At a time when digital technology in healthcare is establishing itself as a means of ensuring access, personalised care and continuity of care, Tomo® offers a structured, secure and supervised peer-support model. We hypothesise that offering peer support, in addition to the standard care provided fro the nephrology team to patients with stage IV chronic kidney disease, should improve their life expectancy and well-being.
title: TOMO-QALY: Peer Mentoring in Chronic Kidney Disease

brief_summary:
Background: Mothers whose children are in the pediatric intensive care unit may experience negative emotional distress due to intense stress, uncertainty, and psychological strain. Therefore, there is a need for safe, non-pharmacological interventions that support these mothers' psychological needs.

Aim: This study was conducted to evaluate the effects of mandala coloring on perceived stress levels and resilience among mothers of children hospitalized in a pediatric intensive care unit.

Method: This randomized controlled experimental study was conducted betweenAugust 2025 and February 2026. in the pediatric intensive care unit of a city hospital in eastern Turkey. A total of 100 mothers (experimental group = 50, control group = 50) were included in the study. Data were collected using Demographic Information Form, Perceived Stress Scale, and Brief Resilience Scale. While the mothers in the experimental group participated in a 35-40-minute mandala coloring activity every weekday for one week, no intervention was administered to the control group. The data were analyzed using descriptive statistics and a t-test.
title: The Effects of Mandala Coloring on Perceived Stress Levels and Resilience Among Mothers of Children Hospitalized in a Pediatric Intensive Care Unit

brief_summary:
This study is designed using an experimental research model with a pre-test-post-test control group.

The study population consists of women receiving postpartum care following a cesarean section. The sample size was determined through a power analysis using the G\*Power software; based on an effect size of d=0.80, an alpha (α) level of 0.05, and a power of 0.95, a minimum of 33 women per group was calculated. Accounting for a potential 10% attrition rate, a total of 72 women-36 in the experimental group and 36 in the control group-will be included in the study. Participants will be assigned to the groups using a simple randomization method.

The experimental group will receive Transcutaneous Electrical Nerve Stimulation (TENS) three times, beginning prior to mobilization. TENS will be applied for 20 minutes at a frequency of 20-40 Hz, a pulse duration of 90-100 µs, and an intensity level tolerable for the participant. The control group will receive no interventions other than routine care.

Data will be collected using a Personal Information Form, the Visual Analog Scale (VAS), the Patient Mobility Scale (PMS), the Observer Mobility Scale (OMS), and the Insomnia Severity Index (ISI). Pre-test measurements will be taken before the first intervention, and post-test measurements will be taken prior to hospital discharge.

Data will be analyzed using the SPSS 29.0 software; descriptive statistics, the chi-square test, and independent and dependent samples t-tests will be employed. A significance level of p\<0.05 will be adopted. Informed written consent will be obtained from the participants, and the principles of the Declaration of Helsinki will be adhered to throughout the study process.
title: The Effect of Transcutaneous Electrical Nerve Stimulation (TENS) on Pain, Mobilization, and Insomnia Severity After Cesarean Section: A Randomized Controlled Trial

brief_summary:
Multiple myeloma (MM) is a malignant hematologic neoplasm arising from abnormal plasma cells within the bone marrow. Although substantial therapeutic progress has been achieved over the past twenty years, MM remains an incurable disease for the vast majority of patients. When the disease relapses or becomes refractory after 1 to 3 prior lines of therapy (termed early relapsed or refractory multiple myeloma \[RRMM\]), achieving deep and durable remission during early salvage therapy is critical to extending long-term survival.

Current guideline-recommended second-line therapies exhibit distinct clinical challenges: standard triplet regimens lack head-to-head comparisons, novel cellular therapies (such as CAR-T) are costly and difficult to access, and optimal combinations for early relapse remain undefined. Furthermore, novel targeted therapeutics have predominantly originated overseas, highlighting an urgent need for effective regimens based on innovative domestic agents.

Therapeutic Rationale of the SKCD Regimen: This study evaluates a novel quadruplet combination regimen termed SKCD, comprising four complementary therapeutics:

* 1\. Sonrotoclax: Sonrotoclax (BGB-11417): A highly potent and selective oral BCL-2 inhibitor that restores the cell's internal (mitochondrial) apoptosis pathway.
* 2\. Carfilzomib: Carfilzomib: A second-generation selective proteasome inhibitor that inhibits myeloma cell proliferation and downregulates anti-apoptotic proteins like MCL-1.
* 3\. Aponermin (CPT): Aponermin (CPT): A first-in-class recombinant circularly permuted human TRAIL and DR4/DR5 agonist, independently developed in China and approved for RRMM, which selectively activates external (death receptor) apoptosis.
* 4\. Dexamethasone: Dexamethasone: A synthetic corticosteroid with established anti-myeloma activity that synergizes with BCL-2 and proteasome inhibitors.

Preclinical studies demonstrate that simultaneously stimulating internal mitochondrial apoptosis and external death receptor apoptosis produces synergistic anti-myeloma cytotoxicity. The primary objective of this Phase II study is to evaluate the clinical efficacy (assessed by the best complete response or better rate \[\>= CR\]) and the safety profile of the SKCD quadruplet regimen followed by carfilzomib and dexamethasone (Kd) maintenance therapy in early relapsed RRMM.
primary_outcomes: Best Complete Response or Better Rate (≥CR)
title: SKCD in Early Relapsed/Refractory Multiple Myeloma

brief_summary:
The goal of this prospective observational cohort study is to identify independent risk factors for subclinical and clinical hypoxemia and factors promoting progression from subclinical to clinical hypoxemia in elderly patients undergoing painless digestive endoscopy under propofol-etomidate sedation.

The main questions it aims to answer are:

* What are the independent risk factors for subclinical hypoxemia (90%≤SpO₂\<95%)?
* What are the independent risk factors for clinical hypoxemia (SpO₂\<90%)?
* Among patients with subclinical hypoxemia, what factors promote progression to clinical hypoxemia?

Researchers will compare three groups stratified by lowest intraoperative SpO₂-normal control (SpO₂≥95%, n=382), subclinical hypoxemia (90%≤SpO₂\<95%, n=181), and clinical hypoxemia (SpO₂\<90%, n=77)-to see whether factors such as sex, BMI, snoring, hypertension, and anesthesia duration are associated with hypoxemia severity and progression.

Participants will:

* Undergo painless gastrointestinal endoscopy.
* Receive propofol combined with etomidate sedation.
* Have intraoperative SpO₂ monitored.
* Have relevant clinical data recorded.

brief_summary:
Liver cancer (hepatocellular carcinoma, HCC) is usually treated first with a combination of immunotherapy (drugs that help the immune system attack cancer) and targeted therapy (drugs that block signals cancer cells need to grow). However, many patients' cancer grows again after this first-line treatment, and currently available second-line single drugs shrink tumors in only about 5-15% of patients.

This study will test whether a new three-drug combination can work better as a second-line treatment. The combination includes: (1) QL1706 (iparomlimab and tuvonralimab), an investigational immunotherapy that blocks two immune "brakes" on cancer cells (PD-1 and CTLA-4) at the same time; (2) lenvatinib, an approved targeted-therapy capsule taken by mouth; and (3) FOLFOX, a standard chemotherapy combination given by infusion (oxaliplatin, levoleucovorin, and fluorouracil).

About 33 adults (18 years or older) with advanced HCC whose disease has worsened after first-line immune-targeted therapy will take part in this study at a single hospital in China. Participants will receive QL1706 by intravenous infusion once every 3 weeks, lenvatinib by mouth once daily, and FOLFOX chemotherapy every 3 weeks for up to 6 cycles. QL1706 and lenvatinib will continue as long as the cancer is controlled and side effects are acceptable, for up to 2 years.

The researchers hypothesize that the three-drug combination will shrink tumors in at least 30% of patients-clearly better than the approximately 10% response typically seen with currently available second-line single-drug treatments. The main outcome measure is the proportion of patients whose tumors shrink (objective response rate), assessed by the study doctors using standard imaging criteria (RECIST 1.1). The study uses a two-stage design: if the treatment appears ineffective after the first 10 patients are evaluated, the study will stop early.

Researchers will also measure how long the cancer stays under control, how long patients live, side effects, patients' quality of life, and whether blood markers can help predict who benefits from the treatment.
interventions: Intervention 1 - Drug QL1706 (Iparomlimab and Tuvonralimab) Intervention 2 - Drug Lenvatinib Intervention 3 - Drug FOLFOX Chemotherapy (Oxaliplatin, Fluorouracil, and Levoleucovorin Calcium)
lead_sponsor: Sun Yat-Sen Memorial Hospital of Sun Yat-Sen University
primary_outcomes: Objective Response Rate (ORR) per RECIST v1.1
title: QL1706 and Lenvatinib Combined With FOLFOX Systemic Chemotherapy as Second-line Treatment in Advanced Hepatocellular Carcinoma Patients

brief_summary: This prospective, randomized controlled trial investigates the effect of deflating the endotracheal tube cuff at different Train of Four (TOF) recovery levels on the incidence of bucking (involuntary respiratory efforts and coughing against the tube) during emergence from general anesthesia. The study includes 60 patients scheduled for cholecystectomy procedures. Participants are randomly assigned to two distinct groups based on the predetermined TOF ratio at which their endotracheal tube cuff pressure is reduced prior to extubation. The primary objective is to determine if timing the cuff deflation according to objective neuromuscular monitoring minimizes airway complications and enhances overall patient safety and comfort. Secondary objectives include evaluating the effects of this intervention on hemodynamic stability and the incidence of postoperative nausea and vomiting.

All participants will perform a maximal 20-meter shuttle run test (Beep Test). Blood samples will be collected at three time points: before exercise (PRE), immediately after exercise (POST), and 60 minutes after exercise (REC).

The study will assess changes in circulating biomarkers associated with intestinal barrier function and innate immune activation, including lipopolysaccharide (LPS), lipopolysaccharide-binding protein (LBP), soluble CD14 (sCD14), and soluble Toll-like receptors. Additionally, TLR2 and TLR4 expression on peripheral blood leukocytes will be evaluated using flow cytometry, and TLR2 and TLR4 gene expression will be assessed in peripheral blood mononuclear cells.

The primary objective is to determine whether acute exercise-induced immune responses and subsequent recovery differ between age groups. The findings may provide insight into age-related variations in physiological responses to high-intensity exercise in soccer players.

brief_summary:
Background: Military life transition involving the Medical Evaluation Board (MEB) and Physical Evaluation Board (PEB) could be stressful. Receiving an "unfit for duty" PEB determination, especially when one wishes to be retained, may be associated with emotional distress and suicide risk. Peers who have undergone MEB/PEB in the past may have the greatest understanding of and empathy towards Service members currently undergoing transitions. Providing transitioning Service members with a peer-support cognitive behavioral psychosocial intervention can provide early behavioral health support, ease the transition process, and mitigate suicide risk.

Objective/Hypothesis: The study objective is to pilot test a peer-support, low-intensity cognitive behavioral intervention, Mil-iTransition, for military Service members and recently separated Veterans (i.e., within 12 months) who received an "unfit for duty" PEB determination. We hypothesize that Mil-iTransition, compared to Transition as Usual (TAU), will demonstrate acceptability, feasibility, and meaningful variability of changes in psychological health, suicide-related, and help-seeking outcomes.

Specific Aims: (1) To evaluate the acceptability of Mil-iTransition; (2) To test feasibility of recruitment, intervention delivery, and retention; and (3) To determine degree of change and variability in psychological health, suicide-related, and help-seeking outcome responses to Mil-iTransition compared to TAU only.

Study Design: A total of 50 Service members and/or recently separated Veterans (i.e., within 12-months) will be randomly assigned to the Mil-iTransition + TAU condition or the TAU only condition. Mil-iTransition + TAU will consist of 8 to 12 hours of manualized telephone intervention via weekly phone calls over 3 months (i.e., averaging 40-60 minutes per phone call per week). Veterans with first-hand experience of MEB/PEB, either peer support specialist certification or at least a year of peer-support experience, and a minimum of an Associate's degree in psychology, behavioral health, social work, public health, or a related field, will be trained to deliver the Mil-iTransition intervention under supervision. Both the Mil-iTransition + TAU and the TAU only conditions will have access to routine Physical Evaluation Board Liaison Officer (PEBLO) care coordination and Department of Defense (DoD)/Veterans Affairs (VA) resources that aid military transition. Participants in both conditions will receive research case management consisting of monthly phone calls. Feasibility, acceptability, and fidelity will be monitored throughout the study. Variability of responses on psychological health, suicide-related, and help-seeking outcomes will be measured at baseline, 3-months, and 6-months.

Military Benefit: Currently, no evidence-based intervention exists where military/Veteran peers are supported for suicide prevention at the vulnerable stage of transitioning after receiving an "unfit for duty" PEB determination. The proposed research has notable implications for DoD and VA early suicide prevention endeavors. Transitioning Service members and recently separated Veterans who are under pressure to navigate through complex transition processes can receive guided support by those who have overcome similar challenges.
lead_sponsor: Henry M. Jackson Foundation for the Advancement of Military Medicine
title: Peer-Support Cognitive Behavioral Intervention for Military Life Transitions (Mil-iTransition)

brief_summary: Sedatives and analgesics are usually given for analgesic, anxiolytic, or sedating purposes for patients with critical illness, while they inevitably inhibit respiratory and circulatory function. Sometimes, patients receive deep sedation to induce hypoventilation or suppress spontaneous respiratory effort. The sedation level in clinical practice is usually assessed with subjective sedation scoring systems, such as the Richmond Agitation Sedation Scale (RASS). However, studies have found that sedation depth based on RASS is not a reliable marker of respiratory drive during critical illness. In recent years, researchers have proposed to monitor the effects of sedatives and analgesics on respiratory indicators and to implement lung-protective sedation, such as airway occlusion pressure (P0.1), airway occlusion pressure (Pocc). However, different pharmacological characteristics, different depths of sedation, and different sedation regimens among different sedatives and analgesics make a great difference in their effects on respiration. Remimazolam is a new benzodiazepine sedative developed by adding a methyl propionate side chain to the structure of midazolam. As an organic weak base, remimazolam forms a salt with benzenesulfonic acid, which enhances its solubility and stability. The sedative effect of remimazolam primarily occurs through binding to γ-aminobutyric acid type A (GABAA) receptors, opening chloride channels, promoting chloride ion influx, hyperpolarizing neuronal membranes, and thereby suppressing neuronal excitability. The drug acts rapidly, achieving maximum sedation within three minutes after administration. Research on adverse effects of remimazolam remains limited, particularly regarding its impact on respiratory function. Therefore, this study aims to investigate the effects of remimazolam on breathing patterns, respiratory drive, and inspiratory effort in mechanically ventilated patients.
title: Effects of Remimazolam on Breathing Patterns, Respiratory Drive, and Inspiratory Effort in Mechanically Ventilated Patients

brief_summary:
This observational study examines leg muscle activity during supported standing and heart rate in different body positions in children aged 3-16 years with cerebral palsy who receive palliative care and have severe limitations in movement (Gross Motor Function Classification System levels IV-V).

Heart rate is recorded while lying and sitting for all participants. Children who can undergo supported standing as part of their usual care also have heart rate and leg muscle activity recorded while standing. Small sensors placed on the skin measure muscle electrical activity. Standing duration and any signs of discomfort are documented.

The researchers do not assign standing as a treatment. The study records responses during routine care.
primary_outcomes: Lower-Limb Surface Electromyography RMS Amplitude During Supported Standing
title: Leg Muscle Activity and Heart Rate in Different Body Positions in Children With Cerebral Palsy

brief_summary:
The goal of this observational study is to understand how injury risk is related to dynamic and static balance, foot posture, training characteristics, and sleep quality in competitive acrobatic gymnasts of different ages, sexes, categories, and positions (base, middle, top). The main questions it aims to answer are:

Do acute and overuse injury occurrence and severity differ by age, sex, acrobatic category, and position in the pyramid?

Are injury risks associated with balance performance, foot posture index, overuse injury questionnaire scores, and sleep quality scores?

Participants will:

Complete online questionnaires including a sports injury/overuse questionnaire (OSTRC-O) and the Pittsburgh Sleep Quality Index (PSQI).

Provide information on age, sex, training history, acrobatic category and position, and previous injuries.

Undergo balance and foot posture assessments according to the study protocol.
primary_outcomes: Oslo Sports Trauma Research Center Overuse Injury Questionnaire (OSTRC-O)
title: Injury Risks Among Acrobatic Gymnastics in Relation to Balance Training

brief_summary: The purpose of this pilot study is to evaluate whether narrow-band green light filtering glasses improve symptom management and participation in rehabilitation among individuals recovering from traumatic brain injury (TBI). Common post-traumatic symptoms such as photophobia, headaches, difficulty concentrating, anxiety, and sleep disturbances may interfere with engagement in rehabilitation therapies and limit recovery. This study will examine whether use of green light filtering eyewear reduces symptom burden and improves participation in physical, occupational, and speech therapy sessions. Findings will provide preliminary evidence regarding the feasibility and potential clinical utility of green light filtering eyewear as a non-pharmacologic intervention during rehabilitation.
lead_sponsor: Casa Colina Hospital and Centers for Healthcare
title: Green Light Filtering Glasses During Traumatic Brain Injury Rehabilitation

brief_summary:
This study is for people with locally advanced adenocarcinoma of the stomach or of the junction between the stomach and esophagus (gastroesophageal junction adenocarcinoma) that can be removed by surgery. Serplulimab (an anti-PD-1 antibody) has been approved in China for use around the time of surgery in this type of cancer. This study will evaluate a treatment approach called total neoadjuvant therapy, in which all planned immunotherapy plus chemotherapy is given before surgery.

About 42 patients will take part at 2 hospitals in China. All participants will receive serplulimab plus the SOX regimen (oxaliplatin and S-1) before surgery, followed by surgical removal of the tumor. All treatment is given before surgery. After surgery, participants will not receive additional chemotherapy or immunotherapy. They will be followed regularly with examinations and tests to check for any return of the cancer.

Researchers will collect tumor tissue, blood, and stool samples before, during, and after treatment. These samples will be used to study how the tumor and the immune system change during treatment, including the immune cells inside the tumor, the tumor's genetic features, and traces of tumor DNA in the blood. Researchers will also grow mini-tumors (organoids) from patients' tumor tissue in the laboratory to test how the tumor responds to drugs.

The study will measure how completely the tumor shrinks or disappears after treatment, the side effects participants experience, and how long participants remain free of cancer after surgery. Participants will be followed regularly after treatment ends.
title: Total Neoadjuvant Immunotherapy Plus Chemotherapy for Locally Advanced Gastric or Gastroesophageal Junction Adenocarcinoma

brief_summary:
Oxidative stress occurs when the production of reactive molecules exceeds the body's antioxidant defenses. Pregnancy is associated with physiological changes that may increase oxidative stress in both the mother and fetus. The type of anesthesia used during cesarean delivery may influence this process.

This study aimed to investigate whether general anesthesia using target-controlled infusion (TCI) of propofol affects maternal and fetal oxidative stress compared with spinal anesthesia and general anesthesia using thiopental and sevoflurane.

A total of 90 healthy pregnant women undergoing elective cesarean delivery were included in this prospective study. Participants were divided into three groups of 30: spinal anesthesia, propofol-based general anesthesia, and thiopental-sevoflurane general anesthesia.

Maternal venous blood, umbilical venous blood, and placental tissue samples were collected to assess biochemical markers of oxidative stress and antioxidant defense. Clinical and anesthesia-related data were also recorded.

The study was designed to compare oxidative stress markers across the three anesthesia techniques and evaluate the potential antioxidant effects of propofol on the mother and fetus.

Umbilical Cord Venous Erythrocyte Reduced Glutathione (GSH) Concentration
Umbilical Cord Venous Erythrocyte Catalase (CAT) Activity
title: Effects of Anesthesia on Maternal and Fetal Oxidative Stress During Cesarean Delivery

brief_summary:
This study aims to evaluate the Intellicens software, an artificial intelligence (AI)-based early warning system designed to help doctors and nurses detect serious complications in premature babies at an early stage. These complications include bloodstream infections (sepsis) and necrotizing enterocolitis (NEC), a serious condition affecting the intestines.

The study will involve babies born before 32 weeks of pregnancy who are admitted to the Neonatal Intensive Care Unit (NICU). The Intellicens Neo model analyses routinely collected medical data, such as heart rate, to identify patterns that may indicate an increased risk of sepsis or NEC and generate an early warning for healthcare professionals. The treating doctor remains responsible for deciding whether further examinations or treatment are needed.

The software has previously been tested using data from babies who had already been discharged from hospital, with promising results. This study will evaluate how well the software performs in real-life clinical practice during the hospital stay.
primary_outcomes: The time between the last Intellicens Neo visual alert preceding LOS/NEC diagnosis and the timepoint of administration of IV antibiotics.
Substudy: Proportion of Intellicens Neo visual alerts acknowledged by the clinical care team within 3 hours.
title: Neonatal AI-Based Early Warning System for Late-Onset Sepsis and Necrotizing Enterocolitis in the NICU: Assessment of Response and Effectiveness

brief_summary:
Aspiration pneumonia is a lung infection that can occur when food, liquid, saliva, or material from the stomach enters the airways. It is an important health problem, particularly among older adults and people with swallowing difficulties, neurological conditions, frailty, or reduced functional ability. Diagnosis can be challenging, and patients may differ in their risk factors, investigations, treatment, and outcomes.

The ASPEN study (Aspiration Pneumonia Evaluation Network) is a retrospective observational study of adults aged 18 years or older who were hospitalized in Region Örebro County, Sweden, with a registered diagnosis of aspiration pneumonia between September 2024 and September 2026.

The researchers will review existing medical records and collect information using a structured data collection form. Information will include patients' age and other characteristics, living situation and functional status, underlying diseases, risk factors for aspiration, clinical findings, imaging, microbiological investigations, antibiotic treatment, other healthcare interventions, and outcomes.

The study will describe the characteristics of patients hospitalized with aspiration pneumonia, how the condition is investigated and treated in routine clinical practice, and how patients' hospital stays and subsequent outcomes develop. Outcomes of interest include clinical deterioration, length of hospital stay, discharge destination, readmission, a new documented episode of aspiration pneumonia, and death within 90 days, where information is available.

The study will also explore associations between patient characteristics, clinical features, investigations, treatment patterns, and outcomes. As this is an observational study based on existing medical records, it is not designed to establish whether a particular treatment causes better or worse outcomes.

The overall aim is to improve knowledge of aspiration pneumonia and provide a foundation for future research, with particular attention to older adults, functional ability, and healthcare needs.
interventions: Antibiotic Treatment in Routine Clinical Care
title: Aspiration Pneumonia in Adults: Patient Characteristics, Diagnosis, Treatment, and Outcomes

brief_summary: Injection of botulinum toxin (BT) is standard of care at Vanderbilt University Medical Center (VUMC) for management of facial synkinesis. Current practices at VUMC involve use of electromyography (EMG) guidance for precise targeting of selective muscles, but the utility of this practice has never been objectively measured. Patients underwent standardized BT injection with use of EMG guidance as well as a BT injection without use of EMG-guidance, separated by 3 months. Patients were allocated such that half underwent EMG-guidance during their first session while the other half do not, and then the cohorts switched to the opposite group at the second session. Patients completed a standardized patient reported outcome measures (the Synkinesis Assessment Questionnaire and the Facial Clinimetric Evaluation) and photographic assessment before, and 3 weeks after each treatment session. Patients also completed a non-standardized survey assess injection pain, anxiety, and preference for EMG guidance after each treatment session. Patient scores from these surveys were compared between EMG-guided and non-EMG-guided BT injections to evaluate for differences in functional outcomes with use of EMG during injection.
primary_outcomes: Change in Synkinesis Assessment Questionnaire (SAQ) score
Change in Facial Clinimetric Evaluation (FaCE) score
title: Electromyography-Guidance for Chemodenervation in Facial Synkinesis

To assess the association between the initial anti-PLA2R antibody trajectory (between 0 and 6 ± 3 months after treatment, before any potential re-treatment) and the occurrence of immunological remission.

To evaluate, in real-world practice, the safety of immunosuppressive therapies in the treatment of severe PLA2R-positive membranous nephropathy.

brief_summary:
Coronary microvascular dysfunction (CMD) has emerged as a key pathophysiological mechanism underlying symptoms in patients with angina and/or exertional dyspnea, particu-larly in the absence of obstructive coronary artery disease. CMD is prevalent in both ANOCA (Angina with Non-Obstructive Coronary Arteries) and HFpEF (Heart Failure with preserved Ejection Fraction), and is associated with poor clinical outcomes, including hospitalization and mortality. However, CMD remains frequently underdiagnosed due to the lack of simple, non-invasive diagnostic tools and the complexity of invasive assessment techniques such as the Index of Microcirculatory Resistance (IMR) and corrected Fractional Flow Reserve (cFR).

Cardiopulmonary exercise testing (CPET) and echocardiography are widely accessible and routinely used modalities that may reflect hemodynamic consequences of CMD. CPET pro-vides a comprehensive assessment of cardiopulmonary performance and exercise tolerance, while echocardiography allows for non-invasive evaluation of diastolic function, left atrial pressure, and right heart-pulmonary interactions. Nevertheless, the extent to which these measures correlate with invasive CMD parameters has not been systematically studied.

brief_summary:
NN2802 is a new product that is being developed for treating participants with CSU who remain symptomatic despite treatment with antihistamines. NN2802 is not yet an approved product and it can only be used in an experimental study like this one.

The purpose of this study is to learn more about a new experimental drug called NN2802. NN2802 is an investigational fully human monoclonal antibody that inhibits c-Kit. c-Kit is involved in the survival, development, and activity of mast cells, which are important cells involved in allergic and inflammatory reactions. By inhibiting c-Kit, NN2802 may reduce mast cell numbers and activity and may help improve symptoms of CSU, such as hives, itching, and angioedema.

The study will assess the safety, tolerability, pharmacokinetics (PK, amount of drug in your blood), pharmacodynamics (PD, how the drug affects your body), immunogenicity (whether your body develops antibodies against the study drug), and preliminary efficacy (whether the drug may improve CSU symptoms) of NN2802. It also aims to identify suitable doses and dosing schedules of NN2802 for use in future clinical trials.

This study will be conducted at multiple study sites, involving around 44 to 46 participants in total, including healthy participants and participants with CSU who remain symptomatic despite treatment with antihistamines. The number of participants depends on how well the study participants tolerate the treatment and the number of dose groups studied.
primary_outcomes: Part A: Incidence of Adverse Events
Part B: Incidence of Adverse Events
title: A Study of NN2802, an Anti-c-Kit Antibody, in Healthy Participants and in Adults With Chronic Spontaneous Urticaria (CSU)

brief_summary:
In this randomized controlled clinical trial we will compare the clinical outcome of Full thickness palatal graft technique (FTPGT) to coronally advanced flap (CAF) + subepithelial connective tissue graft (SCTG) in the treatment of RT1 (Cairo et al. classification) recessions.

Forty patients, presenting at least one RT1 recession, will be treated with bilaminar procedures . 20 participants will receive FTPGT approach (test group) and 20 patients will undergo CAF+SCTG (control group). Complete root coverage (CRC) will be assumed as the main outcome at 12 months after treatment. Gingival recession (GR), clinical attachment level (CAL), pocket depth (PD), keratinized tissue width (KT,) thickness of keratinized tissue (GT) will be assessed at baseline and 12 months after treatment. Patient-reported outcome measures (PROMs) will be reported: namely, the number of painkiller tablets taken during the first week, the degree of general discomfort (D) experienced assessed on a VAS scale (0-10), the extent of changes in their eating habits (CFH), dentin hypersensitivity (DH), patient-reported aesthetic satisfaction (PRES) quantified on a VAS scale (0-10) and overall treatment satisfaction (OTS).
title: Coronally Advanced Flap Associated With Connective Tissue Graft From Tuberosity Area or Palatal SCTG or L-PRF in the Treatment of Gingival Recession

brief_summary: Older adults have difficulty optimizing two tasks at once and typically experience greater interference than younger adults when dual-tasking, meaning that there is greater decline in performance of at least one task when comparing single and dual-tasking. Difficulty dual-tasking may actually predict falls in community-dwelling older adults. Dual-task training has been shown to improve cognitive outcomes (attention, memory), motor outcomes (balance, gait), and dual-task performance in older adults; however, most dual-task training involves simulated tasks that do not reflect functional dual tasks in the real world. Greater dual-task improvements could be seen when training functionally specific tasks. One way to increase task specificity is to offer real-life, contextually-relevant, dual-task training embedded in instrumental activities of daily living (IADLs). Therefore, the purpose of this study is to assess feasibility, acceptability, and preliminary efficacy of a real-life dual-task training program for older adults at risk to fall compared to fall prevention education.
title: Real-life Dual-Task Training for Older Adults at Risk to Fall: A Pilot Clinical Trial

brief_summary:
The investigator-initiated, CArdiac Stereotactic radiation Treatment for Ablation of ventRicular tachycardia (CASTAR) study will be conducted in patients with ventricular tachycardia (VT) which is either refractory to antiarrhythmic medication therapy in maximal dose or to catheter ablation or with contraindications to antiarrhythmic medication or catheter ablation.

The study is a non-randomized, multicenter, interventional study of cardiac SBRT, for which a total dose of 25 Gy will be delivered in a single fraction using volumetric modulated arc therapy (VMAT). The aim of the CASTAR study is to assess the feasibility and the safety of cardiac SBRT for the treatment of VT. Secondary objectives are efficacy, toxicity and QoL of cardiac SBRT for Ventricular tachycardia .
primary_outcomes: Feasibility of SBRT for the treatment of ventricular tachycardia
Safety of SBRT for the treatment of ventricular tachycardia.
title: CArdiac STereotactic Radiation Treatment for Ablation of ventRicular Tachycardia

brief_summary: This is a prospective, open-label, randomized controlled clinical trial designed to evaluate rabies virus neutralizing antibody responses to rabies vaccination among patients infected with human immunodeficiency virus (HIV). Eligible participants will be divided into two groups according to baseline CD4+ T cell count before randomization. Within each group, participants will be randomly assigned to one of two different rabies vaccination regimens for simulated post-exposure prophylaxis. Blood samples will be collected before vaccination and at scheduled time points after vaccination. Rabies virus neutralizing antibody titers will be tested to assess the seroconversion rate and geometric mean concentration (GMC). Adverse events after vaccination will also be recorded.
interventions: Rabies Vaccine (Vero Cell) for Human Use, Freeze-dried

brief_summary: This study aims to evaluate the effect of earmuffs on physiological stability, sleep-wake states, and weight gain in preterm neonates admitted to neonatal intensive care units (NICUs). The study will compare preterm neonates receiving earmuffs in addition to routine nursing care with those receiving routine nursing care alone. Physiological stability will be assessed by measuring heart rate, respiratory rate, oxygen saturation, and body temperature. Sleep-wake states will be assessed using the Anderson Behavioral State Scoring (ABSS) system, and weight gain will be evaluated through body-weight measurements. The study may provide evidence on the potential role of earmuffs as a supportive nursing intervention for preterm neonates.
title: Effect of Earmuffs on Physiological Stability, Sleep-Wake States, and Weight Gain in Preterm Neonates

brief_summary:
The goal of this observational, cross-sectional study is to examine the relationship between training intensity and awareness of lower urinary tract dysfunction (LUTD) among female student athletes aged 18-25 years who are actively engaged in gymnastics, volleyball, football, or basketball.

The main questions it aims to answer are:

* What is the prevalence and severity of lower urinary tract dysfunction among female university athletes?
* Is there a relationship between LUTD symptoms (as measured by UDI-6 and ICIQ-SF) and years of sports participation, training load, weekly hours, or sport type?

Researchers will compare the four sport groups (gymnastics, volleyball, football, basketball) to determine whether training characteristics and sport-specific demands influence LUTD prevalence and symptom severity.

Participants will:

* Read and sign an electronic informed consent form.
* Complete an online questionnaire via Google Forms, including:

Urogenital Distress Inventory-6 (UDI-6)

International Consultation on Incontinence Questionnaire-Short Form (ICIQ-SF) Contentment with Life Scale

Demographic and lifestyle questions (e.g., training duration, intensity, fluid intake, menstrual regularity, sleep, stress).

The study aims to contribute to early detection and prevention strategies for pelvic floor health issues in young female athletes.
primary_outcomes: International Consultation on Incontinence Questionnaire- Short Form (ICIQ- SF)
title: Lower Urinary Tract Dysfunction and Training Intensity in Female Student Athletes

brief_summary:
The goal of this clinical trial is to learn whether motivational interviewing helps smokers with acute coronary syndrome (heart attack or unstable angina) quit smoking. It also looks at whether motivational interviewing changes patients' self-efficacy, anxiety, views about the pros and cons of smoking, and nicotine dependence.

The main question it aims to answer is: Does motivational interviewing increase the rate of quitting smoking at 6 months compared with routine follow-up?

Researchers compared patients who received motivational interviewing with patients who received routine outpatient follow-up only.

Participants in the intervention group received a face-to-face motivational interviewing session at the first visit and a telephone session at 3 months. Participants in both groups completed questionnaires at the first visit, at 3 months and at 6 months.
title: Motivational Interviewing for Smoking Cessation in Patients With Acute Coronary Syndrome

brief_summary:
Improving emotional well-being (EWB) is a national research priority given its central role in resilience, functioning, and long-term health. Mechanisms of developing EWB in adolescents are not well understood, particularly in those with psychiatric disorders and emotional dysregulation (ED), a transdiagnostic construct that may underlie multiple psychiatric disorders, with significant and potentially life-threatening sequelae if untreated. Integrative treatment options are critical to reach more youth at-risk of ED and to support youth EWB in this at-risk population.

Trauma Adapted Yoga (TAY) is a protocolized integrative intervention tailored for youth with psychiatric conditions - a population with high rates of trauma exposure - and is designed to target critical elements of EWB including emotional valence, qualify of life, self-efficacy, and life satisfaction, as well as improving emotion regulation (ER) and interoceptive awareness (IA), two mechanistic pathways that can be targeted in treatment.

The overall goal of this project is to use a randomized control trial (RCT) to evaluate the effectiveness of TAY for adolescents and young adults with psychiatric disorders as well as understand psychological and biological mechanisms. We hypothesize that TAY will improve psychiatric symptoms through improving ER and IA.
