We also examine biologic markers of stress and emotion response through epigenetic and heart rate variability changes. Given the high sensitivity of DNA methylation (DNAm) to various environmental influences, connections to neuroendocrine function, and its role in reflecting how a person's exposure to certain therapies is incorporated biologically, it serves as an excellent and novel candidate to explore.

We target adolescents and young adults in psychiatric treatment within the last 6 months and randomize them into the following arms 1) TAY and 2) physical control arm. We hypothesize that adolescents and young adults in the TAY enhanced care arm will have improved EWB via improvements in ED and IA and that outcomes may be moderated by age, trauma exposure, severity of ED and type of treatment. The potential to improve psychopathology utilizing TAY in vulnerable adolescents is significantly important to public health.

Specific Aims:

Aim 1. Feasibility and acceptability: Demonstrate the feasibility of recruiting, retaining, and delivering a 6-week TAY group intervention to adolescents and young adults with psychiatric disorders in psychiatric care within the last 6 months. We hypothesize that TAY will be uniquely appealing to and positively received by this vulnerable population and that 80% retention will be achieved.

Aim 2. Psychiatric symptom outcomes: Evaluate the effectiveness of 6-week twice weekly TAY on psychiatric symptoms in adolescents and young adults with psychiatric disorders using a physical exercise control arm cross-over design. We hypothesize that participating in the intervention group will:

Reduce participants' reported trauma symptoms ( CPSS V), internalizing (anxiety and depression measured on the BSI, negative affect measured on PANAS), and externalizing (hostility measured on the BSI, attention/impulsivity/opposition measured on the SNAP IV) symptoms.

Aim 3. Emotional well-being and physiological outcomes: Evaluate improvements in EWB via pre/post self-report measures (such as Emotional valence via PANAS-X) real-time Fitbit monitoring of emotions and emotional intensity twice weekly, ongoing physiologic data utilizing Fitbit (resting HR, HRV, sleep quality), patients' self-reported resilience, emotional control, bodily awareness (IA).

Aim 4. DNAm changes: Utilize exploratory discovery DMR (differentially methylated regions) and inflammation targeted gene investigation. Specifically, we aim to explore the association between targeted CpG sites known to play a role in regulating the HPA-axis activity and emotional response to stressful situations with the intervention type and regulatory outcomes. We will use EWAS to discover DMS within promoter regions of NR3C1, CRH, and FKBP5 because they have already been shown to play a key role in stress regulation.

Aim 5. DNAm-outcome associations: Utilizing matched biological and clinical data, determine how pre-post changes in DNA methylation are related to pre-post changes in interoception, heart rate variability, and emotion regulation. Our study will determine whether differences exist between DNAm change from baseline to post-intervention among individuals who underwent TAY and the other group who were exposed to the physical activity condition. Furthermore, our study will determine whether there is an association between DNAm changes at the identified targeted inflammation CpG sites and DMRs and changes in interoception, heart rate variability (HRV), and emotion regulation.
lead_sponsor: State University of New York - Upstate Medical University
title: Trauma Adapted Yoga for Adolescents and Young Adults in Psychiatric Outpatient Treatment

brief_summary:
This multicenter randomized controlled trial evaluates the effect of edaravone dexborneol on blood-brain barrier repair in patients with acute anterior circulation large artery atherosclerotic ischemic stroke within 48 hours of onset.

Patients are randomized 1:1 to receive either edaravone dexborneol (30mg/7.5mg BID IV) or edaravone (30mg BID IV) for 9±2 days, in addition to standard stroke treatment. The primary outcome is the change in blood-brain barrier permeability (Ktrans) measured by DCE-MRI. Secondary outcomes include neurological function scores, serum biomarkers, and safety events.
primary_outcomes: Change in Ktrans (blood-brain barrier permeability) measured by DCE-MRI
title: Edaravone Dexborneol for Blood-Brain Barrier Repair in Acute Anterior Circulation Stroke

brief_summary:
The goal of this clinical trial is to learn if Surgery works better than Intra-lesional Sclerosis With Polidocanol to treat Labial Venous Malformations in Children and Adults. It will also learn about the safety of both approaches. The main questions it aims to answer are:

* Does Surgery has greater Global efficacy, including (including lesion volume reduction, scar quality, and lip symmetry) than Intra-lesional Sclerosis With Polidocanol?
* What complications do participants have when undergoing Surgery or Intra-lesional Sclerosis With Polidocanol? Researchers will compare surgery to Intra-lesional Sclerosis With Polidocanol.

Participants will be randomized to one of two treatment strategies:

* Experimental group: Surgical excision of the labial venous malformation (VM).
* Control group: Sclerotherapy strategy consisting of one or two sessions of intralesional polidocanol 3% injection.

Patients will be identified and recruited during multidisciplinary vascular anomalies clinics. The study protocol will be explained to eligible patients and their families. After obtaining written informed consent (or consent from both parents together with the child's assent, when applicable), participants will be enrolled in the study.

Following enrollment, participants will be randomly assigned to one of the two parallel treatment groups. A baseline assessment will be performed, and patients will receive a patient diary to record subjective outcomes, including pain, during the pre-intervention period until the date of the procedure.

Study follow-up visits will take place at 1 month (telemedicine visit), 3 months, and 12 months after treatment. Outcome assessments will be performed at each scheduled follow-up visit.
interventions: Excision by surgery of the superficial venous malformation
title: Surgery Versus Intra-lesional Sclerosis With Polidocanol (Aetoxisclerol) in Labial Venous Malformations in Children and Adults

brief_summary:
Major depressive disorder (MDD) is a common and disabling mental health condition that can substantially affect emotional well-being, daily functioning, physical health, and quality of life. Although medication and psychotherapy are established treatments, many people continue to experience depressive symptoms and related health problems. Supervised physical exercise has emerged as a promising complementary treatment for depression. However, it remains unclear whether exercising in natural environments provides additional benefits compared with performing a similar exercise program indoors.

The NEST study (Nature-Based Exercise for Major Depressive Disorder) aims to investigate the effects of supervised physical exercise performed in natural versus indoor environments on depressive symptoms in adults with major depressive disorder. The study will also examine whether these exercise programs improve physical fitness, cardiometabolic health, daily functioning, psychological well-being, and quality of life.

NEST is a randomized, controlled, three-arm clinical trial that plans to enroll 206 adults aged 18 to 75 years with major depressive disorder. Participants will be recruited through mental health services in Álava, Spain. Eligible participants will be randomly assigned to one of three groups:

1. Nature-based exercise group: Participants will complete a supervised exercise program in natural green spaces in Vitoria-Gasteiz.
2. Indoor exercise group: Participants will complete a comparable supervised exercise program in indoor facilities.
3. Usual-care control group: Participants will continue receiving usual mental healthcare, together with general physical activity and healthy lifestyle recommendations and occupational activities.

Both exercise groups will participate in a 12-week program consisting of two supervised sessions per week, lasting approximately 80 minutes each. Sessions will combine aerobic interval exercise and resistance training. Exercise intensity will be individually adjusted and monitored by qualified professionals. The main difference between the two exercise groups will be the environment in which the sessions take place.

All participants will undergo assessments before the intervention and after 12 weeks. The primary outcome will be the change in depressive symptom severity, measured using the Montgomery-Åsberg Depression Rating Scale (MADRS).

Secondary assessments will examine clinical functioning, quality of life, cardiorespiratory fitness, muscle strength, body composition, physical activity, cardiometabolic risk factors, and selected inflammatory and neurotrophic biomarkers. The study will also explore participants' experiences of the exercise programs.

Exercise will be provided as an addition to usual mental healthcare rather than as a replacement for prescribed treatments. The findings may help determine whether natural environments offer additional therapeutic benefits and inform the development of accessible, supervised exercise programs for people living with major depressive disorder.
interventions: Usual Mental Healthcare and Occupational Activities
primary_outcomes: Change in Depressive Symptom Severity Assessed by the Montgomery-Åsberg Depression Rating Scale (MADRS)
title: Nature-Based Exercise for Major Depressive Disorder

brief_summary:
This study aims to investigate how auditory fatigue caused by a prolonged and demanding listening task affects central auditory processing abilities in adults with normal hearing. Central auditory processing refers to how the brain processes and interprets sounds, including the ability to recognize differences in sound timing and patterns.

A total of 60 adults aged 18-40 years will participate. Participants will be divided into two groups based on their occupational listening demands. One group will include 30 individuals working in professions that require frequent and sustained verbal communication, such as simultaneous interpreters, speech and language therapists, special education teachers, and psychologists. The comparison group will include 30 individuals whose occupations do not require intensive and continuous verbal communication.

All participants will undergo hearing assessments and central auditory processing tests before and after a 60-minute listening task involving Turkish speech materials presented with background noise from multiple speakers. Participants will also rate their perceived auditory fatigue, listening effort, and task demands before and after the listening task.

The study will examine changes in auditory processing performance following the listening task and determine whether these changes differ between the two occupational groups. The findings may help researchers and clinicians better understand how auditory fatigue influences auditory processing test results.
title: Effects of Auditory Fatigue on Central Auditory Processing in Adults With Normal Hearing

brief_summary:
Background: Emotional distress (anxiety and depressive symptoms) among adolescents is rising globally. In China, the detection rate of depression risk among secondary school students is 24.6%, and that of anxiety risk is 18.1%; comorbidity, relapse and disability rates are all high, seriously affecting adolescents' academic performance, social relationships and quality of life. Mindfulness-based interventions (MBIs) have shown substantial effects in children and adolescents, with meta-analyses reporting a moderate effect size for internalizing problems (Hedges' g = 0.47). Group-based mindfulness interventions for adolescents are feasible: the group format improves efficiency, reduces costs and provides social support. However, existing research remains limited in cultural adaptation and in the systematicity of intervention protocols. The MIED (Mindfulness Intervention for Emotional Distress) system, developed by Professor Liu Xinghua on the basis of MBSR and the Unified Protocol (UP), centres on the "diamond model" of emotional distress, which identifies four core maintaining mechanisms: engagement in life, tolerance of distress, emotional behaviours, and cognitive flexibility. Adult studies of MIED show significant improvement in emotional distress, yet no dedicated study has applied it to adolescents.

Methods: This is an exploratory feasibility study using a single-group pre-post design. It plans to recruit 26 adolescents aged 12-18 years with emotional distress for an 8-week online MIED group intervention for adolescents (two online groups, 12-13 participants per group, with an expected effective sample of 20-24). Data will be collected at multiple time points: baseline, after the 4th session, after the 8th session, and at 1-month follow-up.

Objectives: The primary objective is to evaluate the feasibility of the MIED-based adolescent mindfulness group intervention (recruitment feasibility, retention feasibility, implementation feasibility, acceptability, and safety). The secondary objective is to preliminarily evaluate the intervention's effects on anxiety, depression, stress and other outcomes, and to estimate effect sizes, thereby providing methodological preparation for a subsequent large-scale randomized controlled trial (RCT).
title: A Preliminary Study on the Feasibility and Effects of a Mindfulness Intervention for Emotional Distress (MIED)-Based Group Intervention for Adolescents (Online Format)

brief_summary:
The goal of this clinical study was to compare Halova vaginal ovules, a non-hormonal medical device, with vaginal estriol 0.5 mg, an estrogen treatment, for genitourinary symptoms in postmenopausal women.

The main questions were:

* How do the treatments compare in reducing bothersome symptoms and improving vaginal health?
* How do the treatments affect sexual function?
* What medical problems and changes in the thickness of the lining of the uterus occur during the study?
* Are improvements maintained after treatment has ended? Women willing to receive either treatment were randomly assigned to Halova or estriol in a 1:1 ratio. Women who declined hormonal therapy received Halova without randomization. Participants knew which treatment they received, while the clinicians assessing clinical outcomes did not know their treatment assignment.

Participants:

* Used one vaginal ovule daily for the first two weeks, then one ovule twice weekly until the end of the 12-week treatment period.
* Attended assessments at baseline, Week 12, and Week 24 for symptoms, vaginal health, sexual function, safety, and the thickness of the lining of the uterus.
* Received telephone monitoring at Weeks 2, 4, and 8 for treatment use, tolerability, medical problems, and satisfaction.
* Received individualized menopause-related education and written materials, and completed a questionnaire about knowledge, attitudes, and behaviors at baseline and Week 12.
primary_outcomes: Change From Baseline in Most Bothersome Symptom (MBS) Score at Week 12
Change From Baseline in Study-Adapted Vaginal Health Index (VHI) Total Score at Week 12
Change From Baseline in Vaginal pH Component Score of the Study-Adapted VHI at Week 12
title: Halova Vaginal Ovules Versus Vaginal Estriol for Genitourinary Symptoms in Postmenopausal Women

brief_summary:
The goal of this clinical trial is to evaluate the safety and effectiveness of Small Intestinal Submucosa (SIS) material used for anastomotic reinforcement in patients with high-risk factors for colorectal cancer to prevent anastomotic leakage. It will also explore the molecular biological mechanism of SIS/polycaprolactone-acrylic acid (PCA) patches in promoting tissue regeneration and verify the biological versatility of the new SIS/PCA patches at the cellular level. The main questions it aims to answer is:

Can the use of SIS reinforcement patches effectively reduce the incidence of anastomotic leakage in patients with high-risk colorectal anastomosis after surgery (within 1 month, 3 months, and 6 months of follow-up)? This is a single-arm, non-randomized, open-label, multi-center exploratory study. All eligible patients will be in the intervention group and receive SIS reinforcement patch for anastomosis during surgery; there is no control group for comparison.

Participants will:

Sign an informed consent form during the screening period (7 days before surgery) and provide basic clinical information, medical history, and undergo assessment against inclusion and exclusion criteria.

Undergo gastrointestinal anastomosis using SIS reinforcement patches during surgery (Day 0 of the study), with intraoperative observation of the immediate stapling effect and recording of anastomotic conditions and complications.

Complete follow-up visits at approximately 30 days, 90 days, and 180 days after surgery. During follow-up, they will undergo assessments of anastomotic leakage, healing status, adverse events, and effectiveness; they will also cooperate with the recording of concomitant medications/implanted devices and filling out of Case Report Forms (CRFs).

Have their relevant perioperative indicators collected by researchers to evaluate the safety and effectiveness of the SIS material anastomotic reinforcement patch.
interventions: SIS Patch Intervention for High - Risk Colorectal Anastomosis
title: Multicenter Study of SIS Patch in High-risk Colorectal Anastomosis

brief_summary:
The 2021 Ministerial Decree (DM) defines the appropriateness criteria for admissions to hospital rehabilitation facilities. This Ministerial Decree recommends patient classification through the use of standardized clinical assessment scales along with the definition of diagnosis and procedures using the ICD 9 CM codes, aiming to improve admission efficiency and streamline resource allocation. All these data are gathered in the Rehabilitation Hospital Discharge Form (SDO-R).

Based on this classification, a prospective observational clinical study was designed to describe the SDO-R data in 12 Rehabilitation and Functional Recovery (RRF) facilities operated by ICS Maugeri, accredited for high-complexity intensive rehabilitation (code 56a), lower-complexity intensive rehabilitation (code 56b), spinal cord injuries rehabilitation (code 28), and severe brain injuries rehabilitation (code 75).

The primary objective of the study is to describe the frequency of utilization of new SDO-R variables in code 56, 28, and 75 hospital rehabilitation units and identify RCS-E cut-offs associated with the different admission codes (56, 28, 75).
primary_outcomes: SDO-R diagnosis defined by ICD 9 CM codes
Type of Rehabilitation setting as defined by the Italian Ministry of Health
title: Appropriate and Value-based Access to Inpatient Rehabilitation (ARVA)

brief_summary: This study will test whether adding a lifestyle program to GLP-1 medication treatment can help preserve muscle, reduce cardiovascular risk, and improve quality of life in adults with overweight or obesity. About 670 adults who are starting a GLP-1 medication for weight loss will be enrolled. Participants will be randomly assigned to either a 6-month YMCA lifestyle program that includes resistance exercise and nutrition support, or to enhanced usual care with monthly health education workshops. Study assessments will occur at baseline, 6 months, and 12 months. The main outcome is the change in appendicular lean tissue mass measured by DXA at 6 months. Other outcomes include cardiovascular risk, quality of life, bone density, total lean mass, weight loss, dietary intake, and physical activity.
primary_outcomes: Change in Appendicular Lean Tissue Mass
title: Lifestyle Strategies to Preserve Muscle and Reduce Cardiovascular Risk in Adults With Obesity Using GLP-1 Receptor Agonists

brief_summary: Cesarean scar diverticulum (CSD, uterine niche) is a common long-term complication of cesarean delivery, frequently presenting with abnormal vaginal bleeding (postmenstrual spotting, prolonged menses), pelvic pain, and adverse reproductive outcomes. Current surgical repair yields variable niche shrinkage and inconsistent symptom and fertility improvement. This prospective, multicenter, controlled study aims to evaluate the efficacy and safety of collagen fibrous scaffold implantation versus conventional repair alone. Eligible symptomatic women will be enrolled from multiple tertiary obstetrics and gynecology centers. The primary outcome is change in CSD niche volume measured by transvaginal three-dimensional ultrasound. Secondary outcomes include improvement of abnormal vaginal bleeding and reproductive outcomes. Participants will be followed at 1, 3, 6, and 12 months postoperatively.
interventions: Hysteroscopic localization of the diverticulum combined with laparoscopic diverticulectomy and repair
lead_sponsor: Women's Hospital School Of Medicine Zhejiang University
primary_outcomes: Change from baseline in cesarean scar niche volume (mL)
title: A Prospective, Multicenter, Controlled Clinical Study of Collagen Fibrous Scaffold for the Treatment of Cesarean Scar Diverticulum

brief_summary:
Poor indoor air quality affects the health of millions of Americans. People spend most of their time indoors, yet indoor air can be more polluted than outdoor air. Many everyday activities, such as cooking, using fireplaces, cleaning, and using air fresheners, affect indoor air quality, but most people don't know how their choices affect the air they breathe.

This study will test whether giving people information about their indoor air quality motivates them to make healthier choices. The investigators will work with 120 households, providing them with air quality monitors and sending different types of information about their indoor air quality. Through randomized assignment, some will receive general tips, while others will get personalized messages based on their home's air quality patterns.

By understanding how to best help people create healthier indoor environments, respiratory health can be protected across diverse communities. This research could lead to practical, affordable ways for families to breathe cleaner air at home.
title: Translating Indoor Air Quality Data Into Action

brief_summary:
The goal of this clinical trial is to compare the effectiveness and safety of silicone gel and white petrolatum for skin recovery after fractional CO₂ laser treatment in patients with atrophic acne scars.

The main questions it aims to answer are:

* Does silicone gel improve skin-barrier recovery and shorten healing time compared with white petrolatum?
* Does silicone gel provide better acne scar improvement and patient satisfaction?
* Are there differences in side effects, such as redness, acneiform eruptions, and post-inflammatory hyperpigmentation?

Researchers will compare silicone gel with white petrolatum in 39 patients using a randomized, double-blind, split-face design.

Participants will:

* Receive one full-face fractional CO₂ laser treatment for atrophic acne scars.
* Apply silicone gel to one randomly assigned side of the face and white petrolatum to the other side.
* Attend follow-up visits at weeks 1, 2, and 6.
* Undergo assessments of acne scar severity, skin hydration, transepidermal water loss, redness, pigmentation, healing time, and adverse effects.
* Report their skin sensations and satisfaction with each treatment.
lead_sponsor: University Medical Center Ho Chi Minh City (UMC)
title: Silicone Gel Versus White Petrolatum After Fractional CO₂ Laser

brief_summary: This prospective, randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled clinical trial will evaluate the efficacy and safety of Escherichia coli 5C (Colipral®) in adult patients undergoing diagnostic colonoscopy. Participants will be randomized in a 1:1 ratio to receive either Colipral® or placebo for 14 days immediately after colonoscopy. The study aims to determine whether Colipral® reduces post-colonoscopy gastrointestinal symptoms compared with placebo, using validated symptom and stool assessment tools, patient-reported global improvement, and safety monitoring.
lead_sponsor: Liaquat University of Medical & Health Sciences
primary_outcomes: Change in Gastrointestinal Symptom Rating Scale (GSRS) total score at Day 14
title: Assessment of the Efficacy of E. Coli 5C in the Management of Post-Colonoscopy Symptoms

brief_summary:
Central hypersomnias are rare diseases that include narcolepsy and idiopathic hypersomnia.

The Sleep and Vigilance Center at Hôtel-Dieu has been certified as a Rare Disease Reference Center (CRMR) for these conditions since 2005.

Scientific advances and changes to the ICSD (International Classification of Sleep Disorders) since 2005 (diagnostic criteria and drugs brought to market) have greatly improved the care of patients with central hypersomnia.

This retrospective and prospective study aims to evaluate how each advance translates into concrete terms in the care of patients followed at our center.

Main objective :

Determine whether new treatments are prescribed to replace treatments already on the market (reduction in prescriptions for treatments previously marketed) or whether they enable patients who have reached a therapeutic impasse to be treated (no reduction in prescriptions for treatments previously marketed).
primary_outcomes: Ratio of the number of patients who were prescribed this treatment during the year to the number of patients who had at least one consultation at the center during the same year.
title: Evolution of the Treatment of Rare Hypersomnias in a Reference Center Certified Since 2005

brief_summary: This study looks at whether the physical fitness of young judo athletes before a match can help predict how their bodies and effort perception respond after a match. Judo matches are short, intense and tiring. After a match, athletes show higher blood lactate (a marker of intense effort), weaker grip strength and lower jump height. Not much is known about whether baseline tests of core endurance, throwing power, speed, agility and force-velocity profile can predict these changes in young athletes. Male judo athletes aged 10-13 years will complete these baseline tests in one session and then take part in one 3-minute simulated judo match with a training partner of similar body mass. Blood lactate, vertical jump height and grip strength will be measured before and right after the match, and athletes will rate how hard the match felt. The study will examine how the changes after the match relate to the baseline test results. The findings may help coaches monitor training load and plan conditioning for young judo athletes.
primary_outcomes: Change in Blood Lactate Concentration After a Simulated Judo Match
Change in Countermovement Jump Height After a Simulated Judo Match
title: Baseline Neuromuscular Performance and Responses to a Simulated Match in Young Athletes

brief_summary:
Introduction

Every year, about 80,000 adults in Denmark are seen in the emergency department (ED) with a broken bone. Many of these fractures do not need to be set back into place or operated on. Instead, patients are treated with a cast, splint or brace and sent home. At home, patients must manage their pain on their own until seeing a general practitioner or an outpatient clinic, sometimes weeks later. Earlier studies suggest that more than one in three patients still have pain a week after leaving the ED. Little is known about the pain medicine prescribed at discharge, whether patients take it, or whether it works.

Purpose and relevance

The study will describe how pain is managed after discharge. The investigators will examine which pain medicines are prescribed, whether patients follow the treatment plan, how much pain patients experience, and whether side effects occur. The study will also examine how many patients contact a general practitioner, out-of-hours doctor or the ED because of pain within the first week.

This matters for two reasons. Poorly treated pain can reduce quality of life, disturb sleep, slow recovery and lead to additional contact with an already busy health care system. At the same time, strong opioid painkillers (morphine-like medicines) are not clearly better than ordinary painkillers such as paracetamol and ibuprofen for fracture pain. Opioids can cause side effects and carry a risk of dependence, and leftover tablets at home can end up in the hands of others, including young people.

What the study will examine

The main question is how many patients experience moderate to severe pain, defined as 4 or more on a scale from 0 to 10, during the first 24 hours after leaving the ED. The investigators will also examine average pain over seven days, contacts with doctors because of pain, sleep problems caused by pain, side effects, whether patients received a written pain plan, and satisfaction with the pain management plan. In addition, the study will examine how many patients were prescribed opioids and how much unused strong pain medicine remains at home.

Who can take part and how the study works

Adults (18 years or older) with a fracture confirmed in the ED, which does not require reduction or surgery, can be invited to participate. Fractures of the hands and feet are not included, and fractures must be limited to one body region. Patients who cannot provide informed consent, require planned follow-up within two weeks, or have multiple serious injuries cannot participate.

Patients who agree to participate are enrolled at the time of discharge from the ED. For seven days, participants complete a short daily pain diary in a smartphone app or on paper, according to their preference. The diary asks about pain, medicine use, side effects, mood, activity and sleep. One to two weeks after discharge, a member of the research team contacts each participant for a short interview by telephone or video. The interview covers satisfaction with the pain management plan, any contact with doctors because of pain, and any side effects or medicine use not already recorded.

The study is observational, meaning that participants' treatment is not changed as part of the study. The investigators only record what happens during routine care and follow-up. Data will be collected at seven hospitals in Denmark from October 2026 to March 2027. The investigators plan to invite 300 to 400 patients, with approximately 150 expected to complete the full follow-up.

Limitations

Patients are followed for one week only, so the study cannot describe changes in pain or medicine use in the longer term. Most information comes from patient-reported data, which may be less precise than other types of data. Because not all participants are expected to complete the follow-up, the results may not represent all patients.

Clinical importance

The results will provide insight into the pain experienced at home after discharge from the ED. The findings will also show how well current pain management plans work in practice and whether patients receive adequate preparation for managing pain after discharge. In the long term, the findings may form the basis for developing more structured and consistent pain management plans for patients with fractures.

Patient involvement

The patient panel at the ED at Odense University Hospital contributed to the design of the study. Panel members provided feedback on the pain diary, the outcomes and the practical aspects of the study, and reviewed this lay summary. The patient panel will also help prepare the patient information and, if possible, contribute to sharing the results.
primary_outcomes: Proportion of patients with inadequate pain control within 24 hours after discharge
title: Post-Discharge Pain Management Following Fractures in Adults in the Emergency Department: The POST-PAIN Study

brief_summary:
Orthognathic surgery involves the maxillary and/or mandibular skeletal bases; it entails maxillary and/or mandibular osteotomies (such as sagittal split osteotomies of the mandibular rami) aimed at restoring normal maxillomandibular skeletal and dento-occlusal relationships in patients with maxillomandibular dysmorphosis. These deformities give rise to morphological, aesthetic, and functional abnormalities that can be severe (e.g., respiratory issues, temporomandibular joint pain). Postoperative edema is inevitable following orthognathic surgery; it can be significant, causing pain and discomfort while delaying patient recovery and hospital discharge. The use of Redon-type drains for mandibular osteotomies is not a standard practice across surgical teams due to a lack of consensus. The only available data come from studies with methodologies that do not allow for a definitive conclusion regarding the superiority of using-or not using-postoperative Redon drains (Lee et al. 2020), and no clinical trials have investigated this issue. This project aims to evaluate the impact of Redon-type drainage in mandibular osteotomies (sagittal split osteotomies of the mandibular rami), whether or not combined with genioplasty (osteotomy of the mental symphysis). We hypothesize that drainage using Redon-type drains for 6 hours in the immediate postoperative period following mandibular osteotomies significantly reduces postoperative edema.

The primary objective of this clinical trial is to demonstrate the superiority-in terms of reducing postoperative edema at day 2-of placing Redon-type drains for 6 hours immediately following sagittal split osteotomy of the mandibular rami (in addition to standard postoperative care) compared to standard postoperative care alone, without a drainage device.

Hypothesis: Demonstrating that the use of Redon-type drains following orthognathic surgery osteotomies reduces postoperative edema, pain, and discomfort would provide a rational basis for this practice and support its routine implementation. The expected benefits are twofold, impacting both patients and public health. For patients, the anticipated benefits include reduced postoperative discomfort and pain, faster recovery, and shorter hospital stays, with the future prospect of outpatient care.
title: Effect of Redon-type Drains on Postoperative Edema Following Mandibular Orthognathic Surgery: a Randomized, Controlled Superiority Trial With Two Parallel Arms

brief_summary:
Open-ear bone conduction headphones are increasingly used as an alternative to conventional in-ear air conduction headphones. Because bone conduction headphones do not block the ear canal, it is often assumed that users may be more affected by background noise and may increase their listening volume to hear music clearly. However, direct evidence supporting this assumption is limited.

This study aims to compare self-adjusted listening volumes between bone conduction and air conduction headphones under different background noise conditions. Approximately 32 healthy adults aged 18-35 years with normal hearing will participate in the study. Each participant will test three listening conditions: in-ear air conduction headphones, open-ear bone conduction headphones, and bone conduction headphones combined with ear occlusion. Each condition will be tested in a quiet environment and under four levels of background noise (30, 40, 50, and 60 dB(A)).

Participants will listen to the same music and adjust the volume themselves to a level they consider comfortable and clear for prolonged listening. The selected listening volume and adjustment behavior will be recorded and compared across headphone types and noise conditions.

The findings may provide behavioral evidence on whether open-ear bone conduction headphone users choose higher listening volumes in noisy environments compared with users of conventional in-ear air conduction headphones, helping to improve understanding of potential noise exposure and hearing safety.
interventions: Bone Conduction Headphones with Ear Occlusion
lead_sponsor: Second Affiliated Hospital, Zhejiang University, School of Medicine
primary_outcomes: Change in Self-Adjusted Listening Volume From Quiet to 60 dB(A) Background Noise Levels
title: Listening Volume Adjustment in Bone and Air Conduction Headphones

brief_summary:
The goal of this clinical trial is to learn how acute inflammation affects the body's ability to absorb iron in adults who are hospitalized with community-acquired pneumonia.

The main questions it aims to answer are:

* How does intestinal iron absorption change during acute inflammation compared with after recovery?
* How are changes in iron absorption related to markers of iron metabolism and inflammation, including hepcidin?

Participants will:

* Receive an oral dose of stable isotope-labelled ⁵⁷Fe-ferrous sulfate, followed one hour later by a small intravenous dose of stable isotope-labelled ⁵⁸Fe-citrate.
* Provide blood samples to measure iron absorption, iron status, and markers of inflammation.
* Repeat the study procedures after recovery from the acute illness to compare iron absorption during acute inflammation and convalescence.
* Attend follow-up visits over approximately 3-4 months.
primary_outcomes: Within-Participant Change in Fractional Iron Absorption Between Acute Inflammation and Convalescence
title: FIA Acute Inflammation

brief_summary: This trial compares intravenous thrombolysis (IVT) alone, endovascular treatment (EVT) alone, and bridging therapy (IVT followed immediately by EVT) in patients with acute ischemic stroke due to medium vessel occlusion (MeVO) and a baseline National Institutes of Health Stroke Scale (NIHSS) score ≥6. The hypotheses are that EVT alone and bridging therapy each increase the proportion of patients with functional independence at 90 days compared with IVT alone. This is a multicenter, prospective, randomized, open-label trial with blinded outcome assessment. Patients will be randomized 1:1:1 within 24 hours of symptom onset or last known well. The primary outcome is functional independence, defined as a modified Rankin Scale (mRS) score of 0 to 2 at 90 days.
lead_sponsor: The First Affiliated Hospital of University of Science and Technology of China
title: Intravenous Thrombolysis, Endovascular Treatment, or Bridging Therapy for Medium Vessel Occlusion Stroke Within 24 Hours

brief_summary: The goal of this clinical trial is to learn whether adding hip strengthening exercises to a calf strengthening program works better than the calf program alone for athletes aged 18 to 40 who keep getting shin splints (pain along the inner edge of the shin bone during or after running). The study will find out which program better reduces shin pain, increases calf and hip muscle strength, improves balance while reaching on one leg, and helps athletes return to their sport without pain. Researchers will compare a progressive calf (soleus) strengthening program alone with the same calf program plus hip strengthening exercises. Participants will receive one of the two programs 3 times a week for 8 weeks (24 sessions), along with advice on managing training load, stretching, balance exercises and a gradual return-to-running plan. They will complete tests of pain, muscle strength, balance, daily function and return to sport at the start, at week 4 and at week 8.
lead_sponsor: University of Management and Technology Lahore
title: Calf Strengthening With or Without Hip Strengthening for Athletes With Recurring Shin Splints

brief_summary:
The goal of this clinical trial is to evaluate the safety, tolerability, pharmacokinetics (PK), and effectiveness of the investigational drug QLS5133 (injectable) in combination with other therapies for participants with advanced solid tumors. This is a multicenter, open-label study consisting of two parts: dose escalation and tumor-specific expansion.

The main questions it aims to answer are:

* In the dose-escalation part: What is the safety, tolerability, PK profile, and preliminary efficacy of QLS5133 combination therapy, and what are the recommended dose(s) for expansion?
* In the expansion part: What is the anti-tumor efficacy and further safety profile of QLS5133 combination therapy at the selected dose(s) in participants with specific tumor types?

Participants will:

* Be enrolled in sequential cohorts to receive QLS5133 in combination with other anticancer agents.
* Undergo regular assessments for safety, drug concentration levels (PK), and tumor response.
primary_outcomes: Phase Ib Outcome 1:Incidence and severity of adverse events and serious adverse events
title: Phase Ib/II Clinical Study of QLS5133 Combination Therapy in Advanced Solid Tumors

brief_summary: The aim of this study is to determine the effect of discharge education delivered by the teach-back method and by podcast on discharge readiness, self-efficacy, and postoperative recovery in patients undergoing open heart surgery. Ninety patients will be randomly assigned to a teach-back group, a podcast group, or a control group receiving routine care. Discharge readiness and self-efficacy will be measured on the day of discharge, and self-efficacy and postoperative recovery will be measured one month after discharge.
title: Discharge Education After Open Heart Surgery

brief_summary:
This study will investigate whether adding electrical muscle stimulation (EMS) to standard physiotherapy helps preserve thigh muscle and improve recovery after knee surgery.

Pain, swelling and reduced activity after surgery can make it difficult to activate the quadriceps muscles at the front of the thigh. These muscles straighten the knee and support everyday activities such as standing, walking and climbing stairs. Muscle weakness and loss of muscle volume can delay rehabilitation. EMS delivers small electrical pulses through pads placed on the skin to make these muscles contract. It may therefore support muscle activation during recovery, when voluntary exercise can be difficult.

This prospective, randomised, controlled clinical trial will be conducted at one centre. The planned sample is 60 adults aged 18 years or older undergoing elective surgery on one knee. Participants will provide written informed consent before joining the study. After surgery, they will be assigned by chance to one of two groups, with 30 participants in each group.

All participants will receive standard physiotherapy and routine post-operative care. The intervention group will also use a portable Regen EMS device at home. Participants will receive training in operating the device and positioning the pads on the thigh, approximately 20 cm above the surgical wound. They will be asked to complete five 10-minute sessions each day. The comparison group will receive standard physiotherapy alone.

The primary outcome is the percentage change in quadriceps muscle volume in the operated leg, measured using magnetic resonance imaging (MRI) before surgery and six weeks afterwards. Researchers will compare the average percentage change between the two groups to assess whether adding EMS helps preserve muscle volume.

The study will also assess knee function using the Oxford Knee Score and Knee Society Score, alongside pain and satisfaction with recovery. These assessments will help establish whether changes in muscle volume are accompanied by differences in symptoms and function.

The research team will monitor EMS use, complications and any unwanted effects, including skin irritation or discomfort. EMS treatment may be adjusted, paused or stopped if necessary, while participants continue to receive appropriate standard care.

The findings will provide preliminary evidence about the effects of EMS on muscle preservation and early recovery after knee surgery, and help inform the design and sample size of a larger clinical trial.
primary_outcomes: Percentage Change in Quadriceps Muscle Volume in the Operated Leg
title: Electrical Muscle Stimulation (EMS) Versus Standard Physiotherapy for Quadriceps Recovery Following Total Knee Replacement

brief_summary: The study is testing zenagamtide in participants with type 2 diabetes and chronic kidney disease. The purpose of this clinical study is to find out if zenagamtide is safe and effective for treating people who have type 2 diabetes. Participants will either get zenagamtide or placebo. Which treatment participants get is decided by chance. Zenagamtide is a new medicine that doctors cannot prescribe yet, but it has been tested in humans before.
title: A Research Study Investigating How Well Zenagamtide Lowers Blood Sugar and Body Weight Compared to Placebo in People With Type 2 Diabetes and Chronic Kidney Disease Treated With Once Daily Basal Insulin Alone or in Combination With Metformin, SGLT2i, or Both

brief_summary:
The goal of this clinical trial is to learn whether the type of root canal sealer affects pain after root canal treatment in adults aged 18 to 65 who need root canal treatment of a single-rooted upper front tooth with a non-vital (dead) pulp and no signs of infection around the root tip. The main questions it aims to answer are:

Does a bioceramic-based sealer (TotalFill BC Sealer HiFlow) cause a different level of pain after treatment than an epoxy resin-based sealer (AH Plus)? Does the need for pain medicine after treatment differ between the two sealers?

Researchers will compare the bioceramic-based sealer with the epoxy resin-based sealer, which is widely used as a standard reference material, to see if one causes less pain after the root canal is filled.

Participants will:

Receive root canal treatment of one tooth, filled with the warm vertical compaction technique using one of the two sealers, assigned by chance; participants will not know which sealer was used Rate their pain on a 0-100 scale at 6, 12, and 24 hours and on days 3, 5, and 7 after treatment Record whether and when they took pain medicine (paracetamol) Return for a check-up visit one week after treatment
title: Bioceramic Versus Epoxy Resin-Based Root Canal Sealer and Postoperative Pain After Warm Vertical Compaction

brief_summary: Few people realize that environmental pollution and some behaviors like physical activity and tobacco smoking can affect their health by "turning on" or "turning off" certain genes through a process called "epigenetic modification." This study will develop and test strategies for communicating about epigenetics that are understandable and that do not increase ethical, legal or social issues (ELSI).
title: Investigating ELSI Issues That May Facilitate or Impede Clinical Translation of Epigenetic Research.

brief_summary:
The goal of this feasibility trial is to find out whether a culturally tailored resilience intervention, called BRIGHT, can be delivered and tested with breast cancer survivors from underserved communities in Ireland. These include women from minority ethnic groups (including Travellers), migrant women, women living in rural areas and women experiencing socioeconomic disadvantage.

The main questions it aims to answer are:

* Can enough women be recruited and kept in the study?
* Do women attend the sessions and find the intervention acceptable?
* Can facilitators deliver the intervention as planned? Researchers will compare the BRIGHT resilience intervention with usual survivorship care plus a resource booklet. The results will show whether a larger, definitive trial is possible and will give early signals of benefit for psychological distress, fear of cancer recurrence, resilience, quality of life and unmet supportive care needs.

Participants will:

* Be randomly assigned to the BRIGHT resilience intervention or to usual care plus the BRIGHT Survivorship Resource Booklet
* In the BRIGHT group, attend 8 weekly 90-minute facilitated group sessions, in the community or online
* Complete questionnaires at the start, after 8 weeks and 3 months after the programme ends
* Be invited to take part in an interview about their experience (some participants only) Women in the usual care group will be offered the BRIGHT programme after their final follow-up.
title: Feasibility Trial of a Culturally Tailored Resilience Intervention for Underserved Breast Cancer Survivors

brief_summary: This study will compare three ways of treating adult teeth with a dead nerve (pulp) and an infection at the root tip. All three groups receive a regenerative endodontic procedure, which aims to help healthy tissue grow back inside the tooth. The groups differ in how the root canal is cleaned: (1) standard cleaning without a laser, (2) standard cleaning plus a diode laser to help disinfect the canal, or (3) standard cleaning plus the diode laser plus a single session of low-level light therapy (photobiomodulation) applied over the gum to support healing. Eighty-one patients aged 20 to 40 will be randomly placed into one of the three groups. Healing of the infection at the root tip will be measured with a 3D dental scan (CBCT) before treatment and 12 months later. Pain after treatment, painkiller use, and clinical signs such as swelling, tenderness, and gum pimples (sinus tract) will also be recorded. The study aims to find out whether adding laser treatment, with or without light therapy, improves healing.
primary_outcomes: Change in periapical lesion volume (mm3) measured on CBCT
title: Laser-Assisted Disinfection With and Without Photobiomodulation in Regenerative Endodontic Procedures for Necrotic Mature Teeth

brief_summary: The researchers will test whether high-definition transcranial direct current stimulation (HD-tDCS) combined with real-time short-form video cue exposure can reduce addiction severity and daily usage time in college students with problematic short-form video use. By modulating the dorsolateral prefrontal cortex, this study aims to explore whether the treatment improves executive function (such as self-control and risk decision-making) and emotional-cognitive processes (such as craving and attentional bias). Assessments will be conducted before, immediately after the 2-week intervention, and at a 4-week follow-up, using both subjective surveys and objective computer cognitive tasks. Results could pave the way for a low-cost, non-invasive, and scalable intervention strategy to address the growing public health concern of short-form video addiction among young adults.
interventions: Active High-Definition Transcranial Direct Current Stimulation (Active HD-tDCS)
Sham High-Definition Transcranial Direct Current Stimulation (Sham HD-tDCS)
primary_outcomes: Change in Short-form Video Addiction Scale Score
Change in Average Daily Short-form Video Use Duration
title: Electrical Brain Stimulation for College Students With Short-Form Video Addiction: Effects and Mechanisms

brief_summary: This is a post-marketing, prospective observational study to evaluate the safety of a subunit influenza vaccine and the factors influencing influenza vaccination in individuals aged 6 months and older. A total of 7,000 vaccinated participants will be divided into Subgroup A (1,000 participants, active surveillance) and Subgroup B (6,000 participants, passive surveillance), and monitored for adverse events and serious adverse events within 28 days after vaccination. Participants in Subgroup A will additionally complete an electronic questionnaire on their knowledge of influenza and factors influencing their vaccination decisions.
title: A Study to Evaluate the Safety of Subunit Influenza Vaccine in People Aged 6 Months and Older

brief_summary:
The HiPERion Trial is a prospective, randomized, controlled, non-inferiority study designed to compare the efficacy and safety of two oxygen and respiratory support methods during sedated endoscopic procedures in patients at increased risk of respiratory complications.

Patients with significant pre-existing medical conditions (American Society of Anesthesiologists \[ASA\] physical status III or IV) have an increased risk of breathing-related complications during endoscopic procedures performed under sedation. These complications include low blood oxygen levels (hypoxemia) and elevated carbon dioxide levels in the blood (hypercapnia).

The study will compare two respiratory support methods: high-flow nasal cannula (HFNC) oxygen therapy and a nasal positive airway pressure (nPAP) system using the SuperNO2VA mask. Both methods are used to support breathing and maintain adequate oxygen levels during medical procedures. However, they differ in their technical approach and in the way they support ventilation.

A total of 140 adult patients undergoing diagnostic or therapeutic endoscopic procedures lasting more than 15 minutes will be enrolled at the University Hospital Ulm, Germany. Eligible participants will be randomly assigned to receive either HFNC oxygen therapy or respiratory support via the nPAP mask during the procedure.

Throughout the endoscopic procedure, patients will receive standard clinical monitoring, including measurement of oxygen saturation, heart rate, and blood pressure. In addition, carbon dioxide levels will be continuously monitored using a non-invasive transcutaneous capnometry sensor attached to the patient's forehead. This method allows continuous measurement of carbon dioxide levels through the skin without the need for additional blood sampling.

The primary objective is to compare the occurrence of hypoxemic events between the two respiratory support methods. Hypoxemia is defined as a decrease in oxygen saturation below 90% lasting more than 10 seconds. Severe hypoxemic events, defined as a decrease in oxygen saturation below 80% lasting more than 10 seconds, will also be assessed.

Secondary objectives include comparing changes in transcutaneous carbon dioxide levels during the procedure, the number of interventions required to maintain an open airway or optimize respiratory support, and the occurrence of adverse events.

The study aims to determine whether respiratory support using the nPAP mask is not inferior to HFNC oxygen therapy in terms of safety and prevention of hypoxemic events during endoscopic procedures in high-risk patients. The findings may help identify an effective and safe respiratory support strategy for this patient population.
title: Evaluation of the Efficacy and Safety of High-Flow Oxygen Therapy Compared With a Nasal Positive Airway Pressure (nPAP) Mask Using Transcutaneous Capnometry During Endoscopic Procedures in High-Risk Patients

brief_summary:
The goal of this observational study is to learn whether a short screening test can identify healthy young adults who develop low back pain during prolonged standing ("pain developers"). The study includes university students aged 20 to 35 years with no history of clinical low back pain.

The main questions it aims to answer are:

* How accurately does a combined screening protocol (three simple clinical hip and movement tests plus a 15-minute muscle activity recording of the gluteus medius) identify people who develop low back pain during 2 hours of standing?
* Can this short protocol be used instead of the standard 2-hour standing test?

Participants will attend two sessions on separate days:

* Session 1: Participants will complete three clinical tests (self-reported difficulty of a side-lying leg-lifting task, hip rotation range of motion, and a single-leg squat), fill out a pain catastrophizing questionnaire, and stand for 15 minutes while performing a simple manual task, with surface electrodes recording hip muscle activity.
* Session 2: Participants will stand for 2 hours while performing simple manual tasks and will rate their low back pain every 15 minutes.

Participants who report an increase of at least 10 mm on a 100 mm visual analog scale during the 2-hour standing session will be classified as pain developers. The screening results will be compared with this classification to calculate sensitivity, specificity, and overall accuracy.
primary_outcomes: Diagnostic Accuracy (Sensitivity and Specificity) of the Combined Screening Protocol
title: Screening Protocol for Standing-Induced Low Back Pain in Pain Developers

brief_summary: This study is testing a novel telehealth-based, status-neutral care model for integrating HIV prevention/treatment and substance use disorder services into street-based primary care for people experiencing homelessness who use drugs.
interventions: Standard of Care (Patient Navigation to Off-Site Clinic)
title: STRIVES: Status-Neutral TeleHealth Concierge Intervention for Unhoused People Who Use Drugs Via Engagement Through Street Medicine

brief_summary:
This prospective observational study will evaluate whether speech collected through a smartphone application can be used to assess depressive symptom severity and detect symptom changes among adults with major depressive disorder receiving ketamine, esketamine, or infliximab.

Up to 100 participants will complete brief speech tasks and self-report measures of depression, anxiety, and insomnia at baseline, week 2, and week 4. Clinician-rated depression severity will be assessed at baseline and week 4.

Optional passive smartphone data, including activity and sleep measures, may also be collected. The study will examine the agreement between speech-based model predictions and established clinical assessments, as well as the ability of the model to identify symptom severity and treatment response. The study is observational and will not alter participants' clinical treatment. By evaluating remote speech-based assessments alongside optional passive behavioral monitoring, this research may support more effective measurement-based care and improve the evaluation and management of depression in clinical settings.
title: Longitudinal Assessment of Biomarkers Among Patients With MDD

brief_summary:
The goal of this clinical trial is to evaluate whether an ICF-based interdisciplinary case management model can improve adaptive functioning, functioning and participation, and vocational functioning among adults aged 18 to 60 years with mild to moderate intellectual disabilities receiving residential care or vocational rehabilitation services in Hong Kong. The main questions it aims to answer are:

* Does ICF-based interdisciplinary case management lead to greater improvements in adaptive functioning, as measured by the Vineland Adaptive Behavior Scales, Third Edition (Vineland-3), compared with conventional multidisciplinary rehabilitation care?
* Does ICF-based interdisciplinary case management improve functioning and participation outcomes across relevant ICF domains compared with conventional multidisciplinary rehabilitation care?
* Among participants receiving vocational rehabilitation services, does the intervention improve vocational functioning and work-related behaviours compared with conventional multidisciplinary rehabilitation care?

Researchers will compare participants receiving ICF-based interdisciplinary case management with those receiving conventional multidisciplinary rehabilitation care to determine whether the ICF-based approach produces better outcomes in adaptive functioning, functioning and participation, and vocational functioning.

Participants will:

* Complete baseline and post-intervention assessments over a 6-month study period.
* Be randomly assigned to either the ICF-based case management group or the conventional care group.
* Receive rehabilitation services from multidisciplinary professionals.
* If assigned to the intervention group, undergo ICF-based assessment, interdisciplinary goal setting, case conferences, and coordinated rehabilitation planning guided by the ICF Rehab-Cycle®.
* Complete outcome evaluations using the Vineland-3, WHO ICF Checklist v2.1a, and, where applicable, the Chinese Work Personality Profile (CWPP).
title: Evaluating ICF-Based Case Management in Adults With Intellectual Disabilities

brief_summary:
The goal of this clinical trial is to test whether adding alpha-lipoic acid (ALA) to usual treatment with metformin and dapagliflozin improves insulin resistance in adults with type 2 diabetes mellitus. The main questions it aims to answer are:

* Does ALA 600 mg once daily for 12 weeks lower insulin resistance, measured by the Homeostatic Model Assessment of Insulin Resistance (HOMA-IR), more than a placebo?
* Does ALA also improve blood sugar control, body weight and waist size, blood pressure, and blood fats, and is it safe and well tolerated?

Participants will:

* Keep taking their usual metformin and dapagliflozin 10 mg daily without any change.
* Take one capsule every day for 12 weeks, either ALA 600 mg or a matching placebo (a capsule with no active ingredient), assigned by chance.
* Visit the clinic at the start, at week 6, and at week 12 for blood tests, body measurements, and safety checks.

Researchers will compare the ALA group with the placebo group to see if ALA lowers HOMA-IR more than placebo.
primary_outcomes: Change in Homeostatic Model Assessment of Insulin Resistance (HOMA-IR)
title: Alpha-Lipoic Acid Added to Dapagliflozin and Insulin Resistance in Type 2 Diabetes

brief_summary:
The goal of this prospective, randomized trial is to determine the optimal duration of urinary catheterization in patients that receive elective, right-sided colectomy. The main objectives of this study are:

* To compare rates of urinary retention in patients with post operative urinary catheter duration of 0 days and 1 day following right-sided colectomy.
* To compare rates of urinary tract infection (UTI) in patients with postoperative urinary catheter duration of 0 days and 1 day following right-sided colectomy.

Enrolled participants will be randomized to one of two groups, immediate removal of urinary catheter at the conclusion of the operation or removal of urinary catheter on post operative day one.
primary_outcomes: Percentage of Participants With Post Operative Urinary Retention
title: Optimal Duration of Urinary Catheterization After Right-Sided Colectomy

brief_summary:
This randomized controlled trial aims to evaluate the effects of web-based interactive learning and simulation-based disaster education on disaster preparedness among senior nursing students. The study will also evaluate the effects of the educational program on students' disaster response self-efficacy, psychological preparedness for disaster threats, disaster management knowledge, and practical skills.

The study will be conducted with senior nursing students from three universities. Students who voluntarily agree to participate and meet the eligibility criteria will be randomly assigned to the intervention or control group following baseline assessments. To achieve balance between the groups, stratified randomization will be performed considering baseline Disaster Management Knowledge Test scores, previous disaster education, previous participation in simulation activities, and previous disaster experience.

Both groups will receive the same disaster education content developed in accordance with the International Council of Nurses (ICN) core competencies in disaster nursing. The educational content consists of three main modules: prevention and preparedness, response, and recovery and rehabilitation.

Students in the intervention group will receive the educational content through a web-based disaster learning and teaching platform. In addition to the educational modules, the platform will include interactive learning activities and scenario-based case analyses to reinforce learning. After completing the web-based educational modules, students will participate in three disaster simulation scenarios at a simulation center. These scenarios will address emergency care, intensive care, and rehabilitation processes related to disaster management.

Students in the control group will receive the same disaster education content through conventional PowerPoint-based instructional materials. Therefore, the main difference between the groups will not be the educational content itself, but the method of delivery and the interactive web-based learning and simulation components provided to the intervention group. After completion of post-intervention data collection, the educational program provided to the intervention group will also be made available to students in the control group.

Students' perceptions of disaster preparedness, disaster response self-efficacy, psychological preparedness for disaster threats, disaster management knowledge, and practical skills will be assessed using pre-intervention and post-intervention measurements. In the intervention group, the web-based learning environment will also be evaluated in terms of usability and students' perceptions of the platform. Simulation performance will be assessed using scenario-specific checklists and skill assessment tools developed for the study.

The study is designed to determine whether integrating web-based interactive learning and simulation-based education into disaster nursing education improves nursing students' preparedness, knowledge, self-efficacy, psychological preparedness, and practical skills compared with conventional delivery of the same educational content.
interventions: Web-Based Disaster Education and Simulation-Based Training
primary_outcomes: Change in Psychological Preparedness for Disaster Threat
title: Simulation-Based Disaster Preparedness Education for Nursing Students

brief_summary:
The goal of this clinical trial is to learn if Paraffin wax therapy combined Electroacupuncture works to treat capal tunnel syndrome patients. It will also learn about the safety of Paraffin wax therapy combined Electroacupuncture. The main questions it aims to answer are:

* To compare the improvement in symptoms and functional status among three treatment groups: electroacupuncture alone, paraffin wax therapy alone, and combined electroacupuncture-paraffin wax therapy in patients with carpal tunnel syndrome.
* To identify adverse events associated with each treatment modality (electroacupuncture, paraffin wax therapy, and combined electroacupuncture-paraffin wax therapy) in patients with carpal tunnel syndrome.

Participants will:

* Following the treatment sessions: 5 days per week, total 3 sessions.
* To be examined by an investigator and answer some questions when admitted and after 3 treatment sesions.
lead_sponsor: The University of Health Sciences, VNU-HCM
primary_outcomes: Boston Carpal Tunnel Questionnaire's symptom severity scale
title: Clinical Efficacy of Acupuncture and Paraffin Wax Therapy in the Treatment of Carpal Tunnel Syndrome

brief_summary:
The goal of this randomized waitlist-controlled trial is to evaluate whether an online Mindfulness Intervention for Emotional Distress (MIED) can reduce self-reported emotional eating in Chinese adults. Emotional eating in this study refers to the urge or tendency to eat in response to negative emotions, such as anxiety, sadness, loneliness, or stress. The program teaches mindfulness and psychological skills for responding more flexibly to difficult emotions and urges.

The main questions this study aims to answer are:

Can online MIED reduce self-reported emotional eating compared with a waitlist control?

Can online MIED reduce anxiety and depressive symptoms and increase mindfulness?

The study will also examine course attendance, digital practice participation, acceptability, and adverse experiences.

An estimated 108 participants will be randomly assigned in equal numbers to receive online MIED immediately or to a waitlist control group. Researchers will compare questionnaire scores between the groups across the scheduled assessments. The waitlist group will be offered the same program after completion of the comparison follow-up assessments.

Participants will:

Complete eligibility screening, provide informed consent, and complete baseline assessments before random assignment.

Be randomly assigned to the intervention group or the waitlist group.

If assigned to intervention group, attend eight weekly online group sessions, approximately two hours each, and complete 49 days of self-help learning and practice through the iMIED WeChat mini-program, approximately 15-30 minutes daily.

Complete online questionnaires before the intervention, at Weeks 2 and 4, at program completion, and one month after the post-program assessment. Both groups will follow the same assessment schedule, referenced to the intervention group.

Provide feedback on participation, course experiences, and any adverse experiences. A subset of participants will be invited to interviews about their learning experiences and the relevance of the program to emotional eating.
title: Online Mindfulness Intervention for Emotional Distress (MIED) in Adults With Emotional Eating

brief_summary: The researchers are exploring the effectiveness of a new method of controlling symptoms associated with LPR. Those symptoms may include hoarseness, throat clearing, globus (lump in the throat) sensation, excessive throat mucus, postnasal drip and coughing. Initial studies have been performed that indicate abdominal breathing exercises can reduce symptoms associated with reflux. This may represent a simple and inexpensive means of controlling symptoms associated with a very common disorder. The researchers wish to extend these studies on a set of other reflux-related conditions.
primary_outcomes: Change in Reflux Symptom Index (RSI) Score
Change in Reflux Disease Questionnaire (RDQ) Score
title: Effectiveness of Two Diaphragmatic Strengthening Programs on Symptoms of LPR as Measured by the Reflux Symptom Index (RSI) and the Reflux Disease Questionnaire (RDQ)

brief_summary: This study is an exploratory self-controlled trial, aiming to preliminarily evaluate the effectiveness and safety of surgical treatment for ankylosing spondylitis.
primary_outcomes: Change in Bath Ankylosing Spondylitis Functional Index(BASFI) from baseline to 12 months after surgery (ΔBASFI)
Change in T1 pelvic angle (TPA) from baseline to 12 months after surgery (ΔTPA)
title: Corrective Spinal Surgery for Severe Spinal Curvature in People With Ankylosing Spondylitis

brief_summary:
The goal of this feasibility study was to find out whether a larger trial of a school- and family-based lifestyle programme for primary school children in Punjab, Pakistan, can be carried out successfully. The programme aims to help children aged 7 to 11 years eat more healthily, be more physically active and sleep well, in order to prevent unhealthy weight gain.

The main questions it aimed to answer were:

* Will schools and families agree to take part, and will children stay in the study until the end?
* Can measurements and questionnaires be completed fully and within a reasonable time?
* Can the programme be delivered in schools as planned, and will children and parents attend the sessions?

Ten primary schools in three districts of Punjab (Lahore, Sahiwal and Bahawalnagar) took part. Children in five schools received the 17-week programme, and children in the other five schools continued their usual school routine.

Children in the programme schools:

* attended a weekly classroom session about healthy eating, physical activity and sleep
* took part in extra physical activity at school
* kept a weekly activity diary at home

Their parents were invited to group sessions and two individual meetings, and received printed guidance.

In all schools, children's height, weight, waist size and blood pressure were measured, and children and parents completed questionnaires at the start of the study and after 18 weeks.
primary_outcomes: Standard deviation of change and intracluster correlation coefficient of BMI-for-age z-score
title: School- and Family-Based Lifestyle Programme for Primary School Children in Punjab, Pakistan: A Feasibility Study

brief_summary: This study aimed to investigate the effect of a puzzle room-based gamified learning experience on nursing students' cooperative learning skills and gameful experience. Nursing students participated in educational puzzle room activities designed to promote teamwork, communication, problem-solving, and engagement. Cooperative learning skills and gameful experience were assessed using validated measurement tools before and after participation. The findings may help nursing educators understand the educational value of gamified learning environments and their impact on student learning outcomes.
primary_outcomes: Cooperative learning skills Measured by the Cooperative Learning Questionnaire
title: Gamified Immersion: Investigating the Cooperative Learning Skills and Gameful Experience (GAMEX) Within Puzzles Room Environments

brief_summary: The purpose of this study is to evaluate the safety, tolerability, pharmacokinetics, pharmacodynamics and efficacy of CT204V-CD19 × CD20, a dual targeting in vivo gene therapy generating anti-CD19/CD20 CAR-T cells in participants with R/R B-cell malignancies.
primary_outcomes: Number of Adverse Events(AEs)/Serious Adverse Events (SAEs), Phase 1 of the study.
Number of Dose-Limiting Toxicities (DLTs) events during dose escalation, Phase 1 of the study.
Number of AEs leading to dose reduction, withdrawal, interruption, Phase 1 of the study.
Number of AEs leading to death, Phase 1 of the study.
Number of AESI (adverse events of special interest), Phase 1 of the study.
Objective Response Rate (Complete Response+Partial Response) per Lugano Classification, Phase 2 of the study.
Complete Response (CR) rate, Phase 2 of the study.
Best Overall Response (BOR), Phase 2 of the study.
Duration of Response (DoR), Phase 2 of the study.
Duration of Complete Response (DoCR), Phase 2 of the study.
title: A Modular, Phase I/II Study to Evaluate CT204V-CD19 x CD20 in Participants With Relapsed or Refractory B-Cell Malignancies.

brief_summary:
The goal of this clinical trial is to learn if one course of low-dose radiation therapy (LDRT) helps as much as two courses of LDRT in people with osteoarthritis.

The main questions it aims to answer are whether pain control, joint function, and quality of life are the same with one course of LDRT.

Participants will receive LDRT and can expect to be in the study for up to 3 months.
primary_outcomes: Change in Western Ontario and McMaster Universities Osteoarthritis Index (WOMAC) score - 6 months
title: LDRT Retreatment for Knee Osteoarthritis

brief_summary: This study aims to investigate, through a prospective randomized controlled clinical trial, the clinical value of vagal nerve block at the gastroesophageal junction combined with tizanidine in the very early postoperative recovery following bariatric surgery. Patients who have undergone bariatric surgery often experience visceral pain due to the inflammatory response triggered by partial gastrectomy. Conventional analgesic regimens have limited efficacy in controlling this type of visceral pain, whereas vagus nerve block at the gastroesophageal junction can directly block the transmission of pain signals from this region, thereby specifically alleviating visceral pain; the combined use of tegileridine could reduce postoperative opioid dosage and lower the risk of related adverse reactions. By comparing these two different analgesic regimens, this study examines their effects on patients' postoperative pain intensity, early mobilization, and adverse reactions such as respiratory depression, nausea, vomiting, and constipation. This study aims to clarify the efficacy and safety of this combined regimen in precisely relieving visceral pain, optimizing perioperative analgesia, reducing opioid-related complications, alleviating gastrointestinal adverse reactions, promoting early ambulation, and accelerating recovery, thereby providing clinical evidence for the establishment of a more comprehensive and individualized multimodal analgesia and Enhanced Recovery After Surgery (ERAS) system for bariatric surgery.
interventions: Bilateral transverse abdominal plane block and intravenous administration of Tegileridine combined with the vagus nerve block at the gastroesophageal junction
Bilateral Transversus Abdominis Plane Block (TAPB) and Intravenous infusion of Tegileridine.
lead_sponsor: The First Affiliated Hospital of Xiamen University
title: A Clinical Study on Vagus Nerve Blockade at the Gastroesophageal Junction Combined With Tegileridine in the Very Early Postoperative Recovery Following Bariatric Surgery

brief_summary:
This study is a Post-Market Clinical Follow-up (PMCF) randomized controlled trial of a CE-marked device used in routine clinical practice. The goal of this study is to investigate whether Expiratory Muscle Strength Training (EMST) improves voice, speech, breathing, and swallowing function in people with Parkinson's disease.

The research questions are:

Does EMST improve voice, speech, breathing, and swallowing in people with Parkinson's disease, as measured by clinical tests, immediately after the training period and three months later? Does EMST lead to meaningful improvements in voice, speech, breathing, and swallowing problems as reported by people with Parkinson's disease immediately after the training period and three months later? Do the effects of EMST differ according to disease severity?

Researchers will compare participants who receive EMST with participants in a passive control group to determine whether EMST improves voice, speech, breathing, and swallowing function.

Participants will:

Be randomly assigned to either an EMST group or a passive control group. Complete a structured EMST training program, if assigned to the intervention group.

Attend study visits for assessments of voice, speech, breathing, and swallowing function.

Undergo clinical tests and complete study-related evaluations throughout the study.

Be monitored for any device-related or study-related adverse events.
title: Expiratory Muscle Strength Training for People With Parkinson's Disease

brief_summary: This is an open-label, phase 1, sequential study to evaluate the safety, tolerability, pharmacokinetics, and pharmacodynamics of single ascending dose of ISM9528 in healthy adult.
primary_outcomes: The incidence of Adverse Events (AEs) after single dose of ISM9528 capsules.
The incidence of abnormalities in vital signs measurements, 12-lead ECG, physical examinations,CNS safety battery,C-SSRS(Columbia Suicidality Severity Rating Scale) and clinical laboratory test.
title: A Phase 1, Evaluate the Safety, Tolerability, Pharmacokinetics, and Pharmacodynamics of ISM9528

brief_summary:
This study will evaluate the diagnostic performance and safety of gallium-68 (68Ga)-labeled dual-target imaging agents in patients with prostate cancer. These investigational agents are designed to target either EphA2 and prostate-specific membrane antigen (PSMA), or ACP3 and PSMA, for positron emission tomography/computed tomography (PET/CT) imaging.

The main aims are to assess how well these imaging agents detect prostate cancer lesions, evaluate their safety, and estimate the radiation doses received by different organs and the body as a whole. The study will also explore their potential use in early diagnosis, determining the extent of cancer spread, and detecting cancer recurrence.
lead_sponsor: The First Affiliated Hospital of Soochow University
title: PSMA-Targeting Dual-Target Radiopharmaceuticals for Prostate Cancer Imaging

brief_summary: To evaluate the effects and safety of croma revitalis in improving midface (cheek area) skin smoothness
