primary_outcomes: Skin Smoothness: Responder status assessed by independent evaluator at site
title: Revitalis - Midface (Cheek Area)

brief_summary:
Dental students are frequently exposed to prolonged and awkward working postures and sustained muscle activity during clinical practice. These conditions may contribute to musculoskeletal symptoms, particularly in the cervical, shoulder, and back regions. The adoption of ergonomically appropriate working postures and the development of postural awareness may help reduce muscular overload and prevent work-related musculoskeletal disorders.

The study will be a randomized, controlled, double-blind clinical trial designed to evaluate the effect of an Ergonomic Intervention Program (EIP) on electromyographic activity, working posture, and musculoskeletal symptoms in advanced dental students.

Twenty fifth-year dental students will participate in the study and will be randomly allocated to either an experimental group or a control group.

The experimental group will receive an Ergonomic Intervention Program consisting of two educational and practical sessions. The first session will include audiovisual educational material addressing the importance of ergonomically appropriate working posture and the prevention of musculoskeletal overload during dental practice, with particular emphasis on the cervical, shoulder, and back regions. The second session will consist of a practical workshop using real-time surface electromyographic biofeedback (Trigno Wireless EMG System, Delsys) to promote awareness of muscle activity and encourage appropriate postural behavior. Participants will also use the BruxApp® application for three weeks as part of the intervention. The control group will not receive the ergonomic intervention during the study period.

The study assessments will be conducted under standardized simulated clinical conditions using a dental phantom. Surface electromyographic activity will be recorded from the trapezius, deltoid, and erector spinae muscles using a wireless electromyography system (Trigno Wireless EMG System, Delsys). Electromyographic recordings will be obtained during standardized dental procedures.

Working posture will be evaluated through video recordings using the Postural Assessment Criteria (PAC), a standardized instrument for assessing operator posture. Musculoskeletal symptoms will be assessed using the Nordic Musculoskeletal Questionnaire.

Assessments will be performed at baseline, before the intervention, and at follow-up, one month after completion of the intervention program. Outcome assessors and the data analyst will be blinded to group allocation.

The primary objective of this study will be to determine whether an ergonomic intervention program can modify electromyographic activity, improve working posture, and reduce musculoskeletal symptoms in advanced dental students.

This study will provide evidence regarding the effectiveness of incorporating ergonomic education and electromyographic biofeedback into undergraduate dental training, contributing to the development of strategies aimed at promoting musculoskeletal health among future dental professionals.
title: Effect of an Ergonomic Intervention Program on Electromyographic Activity, Posture, and Musculoskeletal Symptoms in Dental Students

brief_summary:
The goal of this observational study is to evaluate the relationship between luteinizing hormone (LH)-guided recombinant LH supplementation and IVF outcomes in women aged 21-45 years undergoing their first IVF/ICSI cycle using a gonadotropin-releasing hormone (GnRH) antagonist protocol.

The main questions it aims to answer are:

* Is LH-guided recombinant LH supplementation associated with a higher number of good-quality blastocysts?
* Is LH-guided recombinant LH supplementation associated with a higher clinical pregnancy rate?

Researchers will compare two groups of women:

Group A (LH-Guided Supplementation): Women with serum LH levels below 1.2 mIU/mL on menstrual cycle day 2 or stimulation day 5 (corresponding to menstrual cycle day 6) who received recombinant LH supplementation at 75 IU/day until ovulation triggering.

Group B (No LH Supplementation): Women with serum LH levels of 1.2 mIU/mL or higher at both assessments who underwent standard ovarian stimulation without recombinant LH supplementation.
lead_sponsor: Stella Maris Women and Children Hospital
primary_outcomes: Number of good-quality blastocysts per IVF/ICSI cycle
title: LH-Guided Recombinant LH Supplementation in Women Undergoing IVF/ICSI

brief_summary: The purpose of this study is to evaluate the effect on LDL-C and the safety and tolerability of FDC laroprovstat/rosuvastatin in LLT-naïve patients with hypercholesterolaemia. Laroprovstat and FDC laroprovstat/rosuvastatin are being developed for the treatment of hypercholesterolaemia.
interventions: Placebo to match laroprovstat or FDC laroprovstat/rosuvastatin
title: A Phase III Study to Assess the Effect of FDC Laroprovstat/Rosuvastatin Compared With Laroprovstat, Rosuvastatin, and Placebo on LDL-C in LLT-naïve Patients

brief_summary:
The KT-BX-RER Study is a multicenter observational cohort study, with both retrospective and prospective components, designed to evaluate pre-implant kidney biopsies from deceased donors in the Emilia-Romagna Region and to compare findings between donors after circulatory death (DCD) and donors after brain death (DBD).

Chronic kidney disease affects 10-15% of the global population, and kidney transplantation is considered the most effective treatment for end-stage renal disease. Because the demand for donor organs exceeds their availability, the use of kidneys from DCD donors has increased. However, DCD donation is associated with prolonged warm ischemia time and ischemia-reperfusion injury, which may lead to thrombotic microangiopathy (TMA), acute tubular necrosis (ATN), delayed graft function (DGF), or primary non-function (PNF).

Kidney quality is currently assessed through pre-transplant biopsy using the Karpinski score. Since this score does not specifically evaluate TMA, the Emilia-Romagna Transplant Reference Center and Pathology Department integrated additional morphological parameters derived from the Banff classification, including assessment of TMA and ATN as indicators of ischemia-reperfusion injury.

The Emilia-Romagna Region has extensive experience with controlled DCD programs and represents a large proportion of Italian DCD activity. The study aims to provide evidence that may improve the interpretation of pre-implant biopsy findings and clarify the role of biopsy assessment in DCD kidney transplantation.

The primary objective is to determine whether there is a difference, and to what extent, in the presence of TMA and ATN in pre-implant kidney biopsies from DCD donors compared with DBD donors. Outcomes include presence, percentage, and severity (mild, moderate, severe) of TMA and ATN measured at the time of organ pre-implant assessment.

Secondary objectives include:

Comparing the prevalence of different ATN groups between DCD and DBD donors. Comparing epidemiological and transplant outcome data between DCD and DBD transplantation.

Evaluating whether the relationship between TMA and transplant outcomes is modified by donor type (DCD versus DBD).

Secondary outcome measures include:

Histological findings of pre-implant biopsies, including Karpinski score components.

Graft survival. Causes of graft loss. Recipient survival. Causes of death. Post-transplant complications. DGF and PNF. Post-transplant renal function assessed by estimated glomerular filtration rate (eGFR).

Study Design This is a retrospective and prospective multicenter cohort study involving transplant centers in Bologna, Parma, and Modena. All eligible DCD and DBD donors from Emilia-Romagna between 1 January 2017 and 31 December 2024 will be included retrospectively, while donors from 1 January 2025 to 31 December 2027 will be enrolled prospectively. Only kidneys from Emilia-Romagna donors whose biopsies were evaluated by the Pathology Department of the IRCCS Azienda Ospedaliero-Universitaria di Bologna will be included.

Kidney transplant recipients aged over 18 years who received kidneys from these donors will also be enrolled. Recipients transplanted through the national excess, highly immunized, or DECK allocation programs will be excluded. No additional treatments, examinations, or procedures beyond routine clinical practice are required.

Sample Size and Duration For the primary endpoint, the study assumes a TMA prevalence of 2% among DBD donors and 5% among DCD donors. A sample size of 1,677 subjects provides approximately 80% statistical power to detect this difference.

The overall study duration is nine years, consisting of:

36 months of enrollment, 60 months of follow-up, 12 months of data analysis. Data Collection and Analysis

Clinical data will be collected in pseudonymized form through an electronic case report form managed on the REDCap platform. Recipient follow-up will occur according to routine clinical practice, with assessments at 3, 6, 12, 24, and 36 months after transplantation. Variables include immunological characteristics, immunosuppressive therapy, DGF, PNF, creatinine levels, complications, and survival.

The primary analysis will use multiple logistic regression with TMA as the outcome and donor type (DCD versus DBD) as the exposure variable, adjusting for donor and recipient characteristics. Secondary analyses will use regression models, Cox proportional hazards models, competing-risk models, and mixed linear models, depending on the outcome evaluated. Effect modification by donor type in the association between TMA and transplant outcomes will also be assessed.

brief_summary: Psoralea corylifolia (Buguzhi) is a traditional Chinese medicine (TCM) herb with reported anti-tumor activity; its major bioactive compound, isobavachalcone (IBC), has been shown to inhibit ADORA3 and the downstream FAK/AKT/NF-κB signaling axis in gastrointestinal cancers. This is a retrospective, single-arm observational study reviewing medical records of approximately 120 patients with gastrointestinal cancers (esophageal squamous cell carcinoma, gastric cancer, hepatocellular carcinoma, and colorectal cancer; n=30 each) treated at Peking University Cancer Hospital who received TCM formulas containing Psoralea corylifolia as part of routine clinical care. The study evaluates changes in tumor response assessed by RECIST version 1.1 and in Karnofsky Performance Status (KPS) between baseline and 8-12 weeks after initiation of treatment.
title: Retrospective Analysis of a Psoralea Corylifolia (Buguzhi)-Containing TCM Formula for Gastrointestinal Cancers

brief_summary:
The VESPER study is an international, multicenter, retrospective cohort study designed to compare two surgical approaches-segmentectomy and lobectomy-for patients with non-small cell lung cancer (NSCLC) who have pathologically confirmed N1 lymph node involvement after surgery. The study is sponsor-initiated and non-funded (spontaneous study), led by the Thoracic Surgery Unit of the IRCCS Azienda Ospedaliero-Universitaria di Bologna, Italy.

Traditionally, lobectomy has been considered the standard surgical treatment for patients with early-stage NSCLC, based on trials showing higher local recurrence rates after more conservative resections such as segmentectomy. However, more recent randomized studies (CALGB 140503 and JCOG0802/WJOG4607L) have shown that, in selected patients with small peripheral tumors (≤2 cm) and no lymph node metastases (clinical N0), sublobar resection-particularly segmentectomy-can achieve similar long-term survival and better preservation of lung function compared with lobectomy, though with a slightly higher local recurrence risk.

Despite these findings, there is still limited scientific evidence regarding the best surgical approach for patients with occult N1 disease (i.e., lymph node metastases discovered only after surgery). Some real-world and database studies suggest that completion lobectomy might not be necessary if a radical segmentectomy with an extended lymph node dissection is performed, but these results have not been validated in a large, multicenter cohort.

The VESPER study aims to fill this evidence gap by analyzing outcomes from nine participating centers. It will include approximately 400 patients who underwent pulmonary resection (segmentectomy, multisegmentectomy, or lobectomy) for pathologic N1 NSCLC between January 2018 and December 2021. About 50 patients are expected to come from the Bologna center.

The primary objective is to compare overall survival (OS) between patients who underwent segmentectomy and those who underwent lobectomy or completion lobectomy. Secondary objectives include evaluating recurrence rates and patterns, disease-free survival (DFS), and perioperative complications (graded by the Clavien-Dindo classification).

The study population includes adults (≥18 years old) with pathologic N1 NSCLC, maximum tumor diameter ≤30 mm, and complete (R0 or R(un)) surgical resection. Patients who had emergency operations, neoadjuvant therapy, carcinoid histology, incomplete resections (R1/R2), or extended pulmonary resections (bilobectomy or pneumonectomy) are excluded.

Data will be collected retrospectively and pseudonymized using the REDCap electronic platform in accordance with Good Clinical Practice (GCP) and European data protection laws. Statistical analyses will use the Kaplan-Meier method for survival estimation, log-rank tests, and Cox proportional hazards models to adjust for potential confounders.

Because of the relatively small sample size of patients undergoing segmentectomy for pN1 disease, the study is exploratory. It is not powered for formal non-inferiority testing but aims to generate valuable real-world data to guide future prospective randomized trials.

No external or commercial funding is involved. Due to privacy restrictions, individual patient data will not be shared publicly. The expected study duration is 10 months (December 2025 - September 2026), including data analysis and dissemination.

Results will be submitted for publication in a peer-reviewed scientific journal within 12 months of study completion, regardless of the outcomes. Abstracts will also be presented at scientific conferences. Authorship will follow contribution guidelines, with the first and last authors affiliated with IRCCS AOU Bologna.

Significance:

The VESPER study will provide new evidence on the safety and long-term outcomes of segmentectomy compared with lobectomy in patients with resectable NSCLC and previously unrecognized N1 disease. By clarifying whether completion lobectomy is necessary after an initially radical segmentectomy, the study seeks to inform more personalized surgical strategies that balance oncologic effectiveness with preservation of lung function and quality of life.
title: Segmentectomy vs. Pulmonary Lobectomy in Resectable N1 NSCLC: The VESPER Study (VErification of Segmentectomy Versus Pulmonary Lobectomy in Resectable N1 Non-Small Cell Lung Cancer)

brief_summary:
The purpose of this clinical study is to learn about the safety and effects of the study medicine (called PF-08166744) in healthy adults. This is the first time PF-08166744 will be given to people.

This study is seeking participants who:

* are 18 to 65 years old
* are generally healthy
* have a body mass index (BMI) of 16 to 32 kg/m² and weigh more than 50 kg. Participants will receive either PF-08166744 or placebo. A placebo does not have any medicine in it but looks like the medicine being studied. PF-08166744 or placebo will be given as a shot under the skin. In some study groups, it may be given directly into a vein. Participants will receive either a single dose or 3 doses, depending on the study group they join.

The Investigators will compare the experiences of people receiving study medicine with those receiving placebo. This will help researchers learn about the safety and effects of study medicine.

People receiving a single dose will take part in the study for about 12 to 20 weeks. Those receiving multiple doses will take part for about 22 weeks. During the study, participants will have study visits and tests. These will help check their health and measure the amount of study medicine in their blood.
primary_outcomes: Number of Participants With Treatment-Emergent Adverse Events (TEAEs)
Number of Participants With Clinical Laboratory Abnormalities
Number of Participants With Vital Sign Abnormalities
Number of Participants With Electrocardiogram (ECG) Abnormalities
title: A Study to Learn How Different Amounts of the Study Medicine Called PF-08166744 Are Tolerated and Act in Healthy Adults.

brief_summary: The investigational product DXC016 is an antibody-drug conjugate (ADC) targeting c-Met. Preclinical studies have demonstrated definitive antitumor activity and a manageable safety profile. On this basis, this first-in-human trial will be conducted in participants with advanced solid tumors to evaluate the safety, tolerability, pharmacokinetic profile, and preliminary antitumor activity of DXC016, with the aim of determining the recommended Phase II dose (RP2D) and identifying the population most likely to benefit, thereby informing subsequent clinical development.
primary_outcomes: Incidence and severity of adverse events (AEs)
Maximum Tolerated Dose (MTD) and Recommended Doses for Expansion (RDEs)
title: A Study of DXC016 in Patients With Advanced Solid Tumors.

brief_summary: The purpose of this study is to adapt, refine, and test the feasibility, acceptability, and implementation of a novel Motivational Interviewing (MI) and Acceptance and Commitment Therapy (ACT) (MIACT) intervention delivered by lactation specialists to increase Black mothers' own milk (MOM) feeding with their infants and to pilot test the efficacy of the MIACT intervention in a sample of Black mothers and their infants to increase MOM-feeding initiation and duration and improve secondary infant and maternal outcomes (e.g., infant length-of-stay, maternal stress), compared to usual lactation support in a neonatal intensive care unit (NICU). The goals of MIACT are to increase mothers' psychological flexibility and motivation for MOM feeding by increasing acceptance and willingness to experience ambivalent and/or uncomfortable thoughts, feelings, and physical sensations related to MOM feeding, with particular attention to the unique needs of Black mothers. Concerns, views, and feelings around MOM feeding will be identified, followed by discussion and practice of acceptance and mindfulness skills. Maternal values will be elicited and goals based on personal values will be set.
conditions: Cessation or Non-initiation of Mothers' Own Milk Feeding

brief_summary:
The primary endpoint of this pilot randomized controlled trial (RCT) will evaluate the feasibility and acceptability of an 8-week pre-hematopoietic stem cell transplant (HSCT) nutrition counseling intervention aimed at improving dietary intake and quality before HSCT to attenuate post-HSCT malnutrition among up to 20 patients with multiple myeloma (MM).

Hypothesis: An 8-week pre-transplant nutrition counseling intervention will be feasible and acceptable among patients with MM undergoing HSCT.
title: Pre-Transplant Nutrition Counseling in Patients With Multiple Myeloma

brief_summary: Endoscopic retrograde cholangiopancreatography (ERCP) using standard techniques successfully removes common bile duct stones in most cases, but in 10-15% of patients, complex stone features or challenging biliary anatomy require advanced methods such as Endoscopic Papillary Large Balloon Dilation (EPLBD). Although EPLBD effectively facilitates the removal of difficult stones, it disrupts the papillary orifice and removes the natural barrier between the duodenum and the biliary tract, potentially increasing the risk of bacterial translocation and ascending cholangitis. This study aims to evaluate the long-term outcomes (over one year) in patients undergoing EPLBD, focusing primarily on the incidence of post-procedure cholangitis and secondarily on the rate of recurrent choledocholithiasis.
lead_sponsor: Fondazione IRCCS Policlinico San Matteo di Pavia
title: Long-term Complications in Patients With Previous Endoscopic Papillary Large Balloon Dilation: a Nationwide Retrospective Study

brief_summary:
The goal of this study is to examine whether a place-based, community-led, and culturally grounded Crime Prevention Through Environmental Design (CPTED) intervention can prevent and reduce interpersonal community violence (ICV) among youth living on the Pine Ridge Reservation. The study will evaluate The Wancantognaka Project (The Generosity Project; TGP), which combines community-led environmental improvement projects with culturally grounded youth programming. Youth ages 13-19 will participate in sessions led by Lakota Elders, Traditional Healers, and/or Traditional Knowledge Keepers focused on leadership, cultural teachings, community engagement, and implementing projects to improve community spaces.

The primary aims of the study are to: (1) Develop and implement TGP in partnership with community members; (2) Assess implementation, community acceptance, perceived impact, and costs; (3) Examine whether TGP increases protective factors and reduces risk factors for interpersonal violence among youth in the intervention community compared to youth in a similar comparison community not receiving the intervention; and (4) Examine whether TGP reduces rates of community violence compared to the comparison community.
conditions: Lakota Adapted Crime Prevention Through Environmental Design (CPTED) Program to Reduce Interpersonal Community Violence
interventions: The Wancantognaka Project (The Generosity Project; TGP)
title: Wancantognaka Project (The Generosity Project)

brief_summary:
SANTORINI-MX is a nationwide, multicenter, prospective, observational study designed to evaluate cholesterol management among adults in Mexico who are at high or very high risk of cardiovascular disease.

The main objective is to determine the proportion of patients who achieve the recommended low-density lipoprotein cholesterol (LDL-C) goals according to the 2019 European Society of Cardiology/European Atherosclerosis Society guidelines.

Approximately 1,600 adults will be enrolled from an initial network of 15 public and private healthcare centers across Mexico. Participants will be evaluated at enrollment and followed for approximately 12 months, with an allowable follow-up window of 10 to 14 months.

The study will collect information on cholesterol levels, cardiovascular risk factors, lipid-lowering medications, treatment changes, medication adherence, and barriers to optimal cholesterol management. Researchers will also examine whether treatment is intensified when LDL-C goals are not achieved.

This is a non-interventional study. Medical treatments and decisions will remain under the responsibility of each participant's treating physician, and no additional medical procedures will be required solely for research purposes.

The findings are expected to help identify gaps in cholesterol management in Mexico and inform future strategies to improve cardiovascular prevention and patient care.
interventions: Lipid-Lowering Therapy in Routine Clinical Practice
lead_sponsor: Instituto Nacional de Ciencias Medicas y Nutricion Salvador Zubiran
primary_outcomes: Proportion of Participants Achieving Risk-Based LDL-C Treatment Goals
title: Lipid Management Gaps in Mexican Patients at High and Very High Cardiovascular Risk

brief_summary:
This prospective, comparative clinical study aims to evaluate the periodontal status and response to Phase I periodontal therapy among conventional cigarette smokers, heated tobacco product users, dual users of conventional cigarettes and heated tobacco products, and non-smokers.

The study includes systemically healthy individuals aged 18-35 years diagnosed with generalized gingivitis. Participants are categorized into four groups according to their existing tobacco use habits.

Periodontal assessments include full-mouth plaque score (FMPS), bleeding on probing (BOP), probing pocket depth (PPD), and clinical attachment level (CAL). All participants receive conventional Phase I periodontal therapy and standardized oral hygiene instructions as part of routine periodontal care.

Clinical periodontal parameters are evaluated at baseline and at one and three months following treatment. The study aims to compare periodontal outcomes and changes over time among the four tobacco use groups.
lead_sponsor: Cyprus Health and Social Sciences University
title: EFFECTS OF PHASE I PERIODONTAL THERAPY IN CIGARETTE SMOKERS, HEATED TOBACCO PRODUCT USERS, DUAL USERS, AND NON-SMOKERS

brief_summary:
The goal of this clinical trial is to evaluate whether the RNP Book improves glycemic control and other diabetes-related outcomes among older adults with diabetes during Ramadan. The study will also assess participants' dietary intake, nutritional knowledge, anthropometric measurements, and clinical characteristics, as well as the reach and dose received of the RNP intervention.

The main questions it aims to answer is:

Does the RNP Book improve glycemic control among older adults with diabetes during Ramadan? Does the RNP Book lead to changes in anthropometric measurements, clinical characteristics, dietary intake, and nutritional knowledge compared with national guidelines?

Researchers will compare diabetes nutrition education using the RNP Book or national guidelines to determine whether the RNP Book leads to improvements in glycemic control and other diabetes-related outcomes.

Participants will:

Attend educational session on diabetes nutrition management during Ramadan using either the RNP Book or national guidelines, according to their assigned study group.

Receive 15 minutes of individualized nutritional counseling from a nutritionist.

Follow the nutritional rekomendation provided during Ramadan, with on going support through WhatsApp messaging Participate complete follow-up assessments and final evaluation
title: Ramadan Nutrition Plan (RNP) Education for Glycaemic Control in Older Adults With Type 2 Diabetes in Yogyakarta

brief_summary:
Children with congenital or acquired neuromotor disorders may experience difficulties in upper-limb movement and function, which can affect their ability to perform everyday activities. Technology-assisted rehabilitation, including non-immersive virtual reality and exergames, may provide motivating and engaging opportunities to promote repeated, goal-directed upper-limb movements. The PlayCuff system combines a wearable sensorized wrist orthosis with a dedicated suite of exergames designed to support upper-limb rehabilitation through interactive motor tasks.

This multicenter, exploratory, prospective clinical investigation will evaluate the performance and safety of the pre-market PlayCuff system in children aged 4 to 8 years with upper-limb motor disabilities due to congenital or acquired brain injury. PlayCuff combines mild wrist stabilization with wireless motion sensing and gesture recognition, allowing children to interact with dedicated non-immersive virtual reality exergames through movements of the upper limb. The exergames are designed to promote different upper-limb movements and motor control strategies. The rehabilitation sessions also include task-oriented grasping and manipulation activities performed with concrete objects.

Twenty children will participate in the study. Each participant will undergo approximately 3.5 months of study participation, including baseline observation and the intervention period. The intervention will consist of 10 sessions of 45 minutes using the PlayCuff system. During the study, participants will continue their usual daily activities and any standard rehabilitation therapies they normally receive.

The primary objective is to evaluate changes in upper-limb motor function, with the Melbourne Assessment 2 (MA2) serving as the primary outcome measure, with particular reference to the Range subscale. Secondary objectives are to evaluate changes in functional ability in everyday activities using the ABILHAND-Kids questionnaire and to assess cognitive functions using the inhibition subtest of the NEPSY-II and the sustained attention subtest of the Leiter-3. The usability of the PlayCuff system will also be assessed using the System Usability Scale.

Assessments will be performed before the intervention, after the intervention, and at follow-up, with an additional baseline observation period before treatment. The study will investigate changes in clinical outcomes following the PlayCuff intervention in comparison with changes observed during the baseline observation period.
primary_outcomes: Change in MA2 Range subscale score- intervention
Number of serious adverse events (SAEs) related or potentially related to the PlayCuff device
title: PlayCuff: a Unilateral Device for Pediatric Upper Limb Rehabilitation

brief_summary:
This is a prospective, single-arm, phase II study designed to evaluate the efficacy and safety of mirvetuximab soravtansine combined with suvemcitug in patients with FRα-positive partially platinum-sensitive recurrent ovarian cancer.

Approximately 80 patients will be enrolled. Eligible patients must have recurrent high-grade serous ovarian cancer, fallopian tube cancer, or primary peritoneal cancer with FRα expression and disease recurrence occurring 6 to 12 months after completion of platinum-based chemotherapy.

Participants will receive mirvetuximab soravtansine and suvemcitug every 2 weeks until disease progression, unacceptable toxicity, withdrawal of consent, or study termination. Tumor response will be assessed according to RECIST version 1.1.

The primary objective is to evaluate the objective response rate (ORR). Secondary objectives include duration of response (DOR), progression-free survival (PFS), overall survival (OS), CA125 response, and safety outcomes. Exploratory analyses will assess the relationship between FRα expression, other biomarkers, and clinical outcomes.
title: MIRV in Combination With Suvemcitug for Partially Platinum-Sensitive Ovarian Cancer

brief_summary: This study will evaluate the long-term risks of permanent kidney failure and inpatient dialysis among living kidney donors compared with matched healthy nondonors. This population-based, retrospective cohort study will use linked administrative health care databases from Ontario, Alberta, and British Columbia. Living kidney donors who donated between 1992 and 2025 will be identified and matched 1:10 within each province to a carefully selected population of healthy nondonors based on baseline characteristics. The primary outcome is permanent kidney failure (defined by kidney transplant, chronic dialysis, or eGFR \<15 mL/min/1.73 m²). The secondary outcome is dialysis (inpatient). These results will help support informed consent for potential donors, as well as guidance for transplant clinicians and follow-up care for living kidney donors.
lead_sponsor: London Health Sciences Centre Research Institute OR Lawson Research Institute of St. Joseph's
title: Kidney Function Following Living Kidney Donation

brief_summary: This randomized controlled study evaluates virtual reality education for men aged 40 to 80 years with prostate cancer who are scheduled for CyberKnife radiotherapy at the University Hospital Ostrava. Participants are assigned in a 1:1 ratio to standard patient education alone or standard education supplemented by the Virtual Doctor's Assistant. The virtual environment reproduces the CyberKnife treatment room and explains the equipment, the treatment process, and the importance of consistent bladder and rectal preparation. The study aims to reduce stress before treatment and improve patients' understanding of the procedure and preparation requirements. Cancer treatment itself is unchanged. Outcomes will be assessed using patient questionnaires.
primary_outcomes: Understanding of CyberKnife radiotherapy and preparation requirements
title: Virtual Reality Education Before CyberKnife Treatment for Prostate Cancer

brief_summary:
Sodium bicarbonate is a dietary supplement that increases blood bicarbonate levels, thereby enhancing the body's extracellular buffering capacity. This effect may facilitate the removal of hydrogen ions from working muscles, thereby helping to maintain performance during high-intensity exercise. However, it can cause gastrointestinal symptoms that limit its practical use. While enteric-coated capsules may improve gastrointestinal tolerance, the impact of this form of supplementation on bicarbonate availability and exercise performance requires further investigation.

The aim of this study is to establish whether the form of sodium bicarbonate supplementation influences gastrointestinal symptoms, changes in blood bicarbonate concentration, and repeated high-intensity cycling performance in physically active individuals who are trained in endurance or mixed-demand sports. In a randomised, double-blind, placebo-controlled crossover design, participants will receive either 0.3 g/kg of body mass of sodium bicarbonate in conventional or enteric-coated capsules, or a placebo. During each experimental session, participants will perform two 30-second Wingate anaerobic cycling tests following supplementation.

Mechanical performance outcomes, including peak power, mean power, minimum power, and total work, will be assessed alongside blood lactate concentration and markers of acid-base balance, including pH, bicarbonate concentration, and base excess. Repeated capillary blood samples will be collected before and after exercise to characterise the physiological response to supplementation. The occurrence and severity of gastrointestinal symptoms will also be recorded and compared between supplementation conditions.

The findings of this study may improve our understanding of the effects of a sodium bicarbonate formulation on gastrointestinal tolerance, blood buffering responses, and performance in repeated high-intensity exercise. They may also provide athletes and practitioners with practical information on supplementation strategies that balance potential performance benefits with gastrointestinal tolerance.
lead_sponsor: The Jerzy Kukuczka Academy of Physical Education in Katowice
title: Does the Form Matter? Effects of Standard and Enteric-coated Sodium Bicarbonate Capsules on Repeated Maximal Cycling Performance, Acid-base Balance, and Gastrointestinal Issues in Men in a Randomized Placebo-controlled Crossover Trial
